words.en: Someone who is adroit is quick and skillful in their thoughts, behavior, or actions.

words.tr:
n. 刺穿；刺孔
v. 刺穿；削弱
words.ex: The bike tire has a puncture.
words.ex_cn: 自行车轮胎有一个漏气孔。
words.en: A puncture is a small hole made by a sharp object, especially in a tire. To puncture something means to make a hole in it with a sharp object.

words.ex: The high fine will deter people from breaking the law.
words.ex_cn: 高额罚款会制止人们违法。
words.en: If something deters you from doing something, it makes you not want to do it or continue doing it.

words.tr: v. 砰地关上；猛地一动；抨击
words.ex: He slammed the door angrily.
words.ex_cn: 他生气地把门砰地关上。
words.en: If you slam a door or window, or if it slams, it shuts noisily and with great force.

words.ex: He gave her a sincere apology.
words.ex_cn: 他向她真诚地道歉了。
words.en: An apology is something that you say or write in order to tell someone that you are sorry that you have hurt them or caused trouble for them.

words.ex: The smoke from the factory is noxious.
words.ex_cn: 工厂的烟雾是有害的。
words.en: Something that is noxious is harmful or poisonous.

words.tr: n. 毁灭；引起毁灭的根源；
words.ex: The storm caused the destruction of the village.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴摧毁了村庄。
words.en: The act of destroying something, or the state of being destroyed.

words.tr: v. （使）成化石；变陈腐；（使）僵化
words.ex: The old tree fossilized over millions of years.
words.ex_cn: 这棵老树在数百万年中变成了化石。
words.en: To fossilize means to become or cause to become a fossil, or to become fixed and unable to change or develop.

words.tr:
n. 轮廓；纲要；
v. 描画轮廓；概述；
words.ex: The artist drew the outline of the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家画出了山的轮廓。
words.en: An outline is a line that shows or forms the outer edge of something, or a general description or plan showing the essential features of something but not the detail.

words.tr: n. 回路；环行；电路；巡回；
words.ex: The battery connects to the circuit to make the light work.
words.ex_cn: 电池连接到回路，使灯亮起来。
words.en: A circuit is a roughly circular line, route, or movement that starts and finishes at the same place. It can also refer to the complete path that an electric current travels along.

words.ex: The arid land has little rain and no trees.
words.ex_cn: 这片干旱的土地降雨稀少，没有树木。
words.en: An arid area of land has so little rain that it is very dry and cannot support much vegetation.

words.ex: My mom scolded me for coming home late.
words.ex_cn: 妈妈因为我回家晚而责备了我。
words.en: If you scold someone, you speak angrily to them because they have done something wrong.

words.tr:
v. 生产；获利；
n. 产量；
words.ex: This farm yields a lot of wheat each year.
words.ex_cn: 这个农场每年生产大量小麦。
words.en: If you yield to someone or something, you stop resisting them. If a tree or plant yields fruit or flowers, it produces them.

words.ex: He had a setback when he failed the test.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格，遇到了挫折。
words.en: A setback is an event that delays your progress or reverses some of the progress that you have made.

words.ex: The team celebrated their triumph after winning the match.
words.ex_cn: 球队在赢得比赛后庆祝了他们的胜利。
words.en: A triumph is a great success or achievement, often one that has been gained with a lot of skill or effort.

words.ex: The teacher will critique the student's essay tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天会对学生的作文发表评论。
words.en: A critique is a detailed analysis and assessment of something, especially a literary, philosophical, or political theory.

words.ex: His denial of the mistake made everyone angry.
words.ex_cn: 他否认错误，让所有人都生气了。
words.en: A denial is a statement that something is not true or does not exist.

words.ex: He can identify the bird by its song.
words.ex_cn: 他能通过鸟的叫声识别它。
words.en: If you can identify someone or something, you are able to recognize them or distinguish them from others.

words.tr:
n. 群；团；簇；
v. 聚集；
words.ex: The stars form a bright cluster in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 星星在夜空中形成了一群明亮的星群。
words.en: A cluster of things or people is a small group of them close together.

words.tr: adj. 像家般舒适的；朴素的；
words.ex: The small cabin had a homely feel with soft blankets and a warm fire.
words.ex_cn: 这座小木屋有柔软的毛毯和温暖的火炉，感觉像家一样舒适。
words.en: If you describe something as homely, you mean that it is simple and plain, often in a way that is comforting. If you describe a person as homely, you mean that they are not very attractive.

words.ex: The doctor prescribed medication to palliate the patient's pain.
words.ex_cn: 医生开了药来减轻病人的疼痛。
words.en: To palliate means to make something less severe or intense without actually solving the cause of it. It can refer to the easing of physical pain or the attempt to make a fault or crime seem less serious.

words.tr: n. （政治、商业或社会性）活动；运动；
words.ex: The city launched a campaign to reduce plastic waste.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市发起了一项减少塑料垃圾的活动。
words.en: A campaign is a planned set of activities that people carry out over a period of time in order to achieve something such as social or political change.

words.ex: He uses an efficient way to solve math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他用一种高效的方法解决数学问题。
words.en: If something or someone is efficient, they are able to do tasks successfully, without wasting time or energy.

words.ex: He can customize his phone with new wallpapers.
words.ex_cn: 他可以用新的壁纸自定义他的手机。
words.en: To customize something means to alter or modify it to suit a particular individual or task.

words.ex: She tried to prevail on him to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 她试图劝服他改变主意。
words.en: If a proposal, principle, or opinion prevails, it gains influence or is accepted, often after a struggle or argument.

words.ex: He reject the job offer.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这份工作邀请。
words.en: If you reject something such as a proposal, a request, or an offer, you do not accept it or you do not agree to it.

words.tr:
n. 等级；
v. 分等级；
words.ex: He earned a high rank in the army.
words.ex_cn: 他在军队中获得了很高的等级。
words.en: If you rank things or people, you arrange them in order of importance or quality. If someone or something ranks in a particular position, they are in that position on a scale that measures something such as importance or quality.

words.ex: They tried to coerce him into signing the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图强迫他签署那份文件。
words.en: If you coerce someone into doing something, you make them do it, even though they do not want to.

words.tr: adj. 杰出的；卓越的；出类拔萃的
words.ex: He is a pre-eminent scientist in his field.
words.ex_cn: 他是该领域最杰出的科学家。
words.en: If someone or something is pre-eminent in a group, they are more important, powerful, or capable than other people or things in the group.

words.ex: He tries to foment trouble between the neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在邻居之间挑起纠纷。
words.en: If someone foments trouble or violent opposition, they cause it to develop.

words.ex: He lost his job because of his integrity.
words.ex_cn: 他因为正直而失去了工作。
words.en: Integrity is the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles.

words.ex: They deem this plan too risky.
words.ex_cn: 他们认为这个计划太冒险了。
words.en: If you deem something to be the case, you consider that it is the case.

words.tr: n. 举办地点；（比赛）地点；会场；
words.ex: The concert will be held at a new venue.
words.ex_cn: 这场音乐会将在一个新的举办地点举行。
words.en: A place where an event or meeting is held, such as a concert hall or conference center.

words.tr:
v. 骗取；伪造
n. 哄骗
words.ex: She managed to wangle an invitation to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她设法弄到了派对的邀请。
words.en: If you wangle something that you want, you manage to get it by being clever or persuading someone.

words.ex: The wind abrades the rock slowly.
words.ex_cn: 风慢慢磨损岩石。
words.en: To scrape or wear away by friction or erosion.

words.ex: He crossed the threshold of adulthood at 18.
words.ex_cn: 他在18岁时进入了成年的起始点。
words.en: The threshold of something is the point at which it begins or changes.

words.tr: adj. 渴望获得的；贪得无厌的
words.ex: He is acquisitive and always wants more things.
words.ex_cn: 他很有占有欲，总是想要更多东西。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behavior as acquisitive, you mean they are very interested in acquiring money and possessions, often in a way that is selfish or unfair.

words.ex: The baby babbles when she is happy.
words.ex_cn: 当宝宝开心时，她会含糊不清地说话。
words.en: To babble means to talk rapidly and continuously in a foolish, excited, or incomprehensible way.

words.tr: adj. 坚持的；迫切要求的；持续的
words.ex: He is insistent about finishing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持要完成作业。
words.en: If someone is insistent, they keep demanding something and refuse to accept any opposition or excuses.

words.ex: The sunset was spectacular.
words.ex_cn: 日落非常壮观。
words.en: Something that is spectacular is very impressive or dramatic.

words.tr:
v. 鼓起；集合；召集
n. 集合；集合的人群
words.ex: He must muster courage to speak in public.
words.ex_cn: 他必须鼓起勇气在公众面前发言。
words.en: To muster means to gather or assemble (troops, etc.), especially for inspection or in preparation for battle. It can also mean to summon up (a feeling, attitude, or response).

words.tr:
n. 病房；病室；选区；
v. 监护；守护；挡住；
words.ex: The patient is in ward 5.
words.ex_cn: 病人在5号病房。
words.en: A ward is a separate room in a hospital, typically one allocated to a particular type of patient, or a person, especially a child, who is under the protection or care of a legal guardian or a court.

words.ex: My throat is sore after singing.
words.ex_cn: 我唱歌后喉咙疼。
words.en: If part of your body is sore, it causes you pain and discomfort.

words.tr: n. 不慎重；轻率；言行失检
words.ex: His indiscretion caused a big problem at work.
words.ex_cn: 他的轻率行为在工作中引起了大问题。
words.en: Indiscretion refers to behavior or speech that is not discreet; it can also mean a lack of good judgment or care in what one says or does.

words.ex: The school changed its curriculum last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年学校更改了课程。
words.en: A curriculum is the subjects that are studied in a school, college, or university.

words.ex: He did a preliminary test before the main experiment.
words.ex_cn: 他在主要实验之前做了一个初步测试。
words.en: Preliminary means something that is done or happens before the main part or event, especially as an introduction or preparation.

words.ex: The ancient stone has an inscription in Latin.
words.ex_cn: 这块古老的石头上有一段拉丁文碑文。
words.en: An inscription is a piece of writing or a short message that is written or carved on something, especially as a formal or permanent record.

words.tr:
v. 嘲笑；嘲弄；
adj. 仿制的；
words.ex: They mock him for his accent.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为他口音而嘲笑他。
words.en: To mock someone means to laugh at them, tease them, or make them look foolish, often by imitating their behavior or speech.

words.tr:
n. 长条；条状；
v. 剥去；剥夺；
words.ex: He cut a strip of paper to wrap the gift.
words.ex_cn: 他剪了一条纸来包装礼物。
words.en: To remove a layer from something, or to take off your clothes.

words.ex: The nurse will dispense medicine to the patients.
words.ex_cn: 护士将分发药品给病人。
words.en: To dispense means to distribute or provide something, especially in a systematic way, or to prepare and give out medicine.

words.ex: He gave her a light pinch on the arm.
words.ex_cn: 他轻轻捏了她的胳膊一下。
words.en: To pinch someone or something means to squeeze them tightly between your thumb and finger, or between two surfaces, especially in a way that causes pain.

words.ex: He studied familial patterns in his research.
words.ex_cn: 他在研究中分析了家族模式。
words.en: Relating to or occurring in a family or its members.

words.ex: The ticket is invalid because it expired.
words.ex_cn: 这张票无效，因为它已经过期了。
words.en: If something is invalid, it is not legally or officially acceptable, or it is not based on truth or reason.

words.tr: v. 恳求；征求；（妓女）拉客
words.ex: He solicits donations for the charity.
words.ex_cn: 他为慈善机构募捐。
words.en: If you solicit money, help, support, or an opinion from someone, you ask them for it.

words.ex: The luminous moon lights up the night.
words.ex_cn: 明亮的月亮照亮了夜晚。
words.en: Something that is luminous shines or glows in the dark.

words.ex: The teacher will classify the students by age.
words.ex_cn: 老师将按年龄对学生进行分类。
words.en: To classify things means to divide them into groups or types so that things with similar characteristics are in the same group.

words.tr: adj. 熙熙攘攘的； v. “bustle”的现在分词；
words.ex: The market is bustling with people.
words.ex_cn: 市场里人来人往，熙熙攘攘。
words.en: If a place is bustling, it is full of busy activity.

words.ex: The problem has too much complexity.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题太复杂了。
words.en: Complexity is the state of having many different parts connected or related to each other in a complicated way.

words.tr:
n. 鞭子
v. 鞭打；抽打；突然移动
words.ex: The farmer used a whip to guide the horse.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用鞭子赶马。
words.en: To whip means to hit a person or animal with a whip, or to move something quickly and suddenly.

words.ex: His condition improved after the treatment.
words.ex_cn: 他的状况在接受治疗后好转了。
words.en: A condition is a state of affairs that must exist or be brought about before something else can happen or be done.

words.tr: adj. 善于接受的；能接纳的；
words.ex: He is receptive to new ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他善于接受新想法。
words.en: Willing to consider or accept new suggestions and ideas.

words.ex: The child is curious about the stars.
words.ex_cn: 孩子对星星感到好奇。
words.en: If you are curious about something, you are interested in it and want to know more about it.

words.ex: After a short break, he resumed his work.
words.ex_cn: 短暂休息后，他继续工作。
words.en: If you resume an activity or if it resumes, it begins again or continues after an interruption.

words.tr:
n. 滞后；延迟；
v. 落后；缓慢移动；
words.ex: There is a lag between the signal and the response.
words.ex_cn: 信号和响应之间有滞后。
words.en: If one thing or person lags behind another thing or person, their progress is slower than that of the other.

words.ex: The long meeting was tedious.
words.ex_cn: 这场漫长的会议很沉闷。
words.en: If you describe something such as a job, task, or situation as tedious, you mean it is boring and rather frustrating.

words.ex: He crammed the suitcase with clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他把衣服塞满了行李箱。
words.en: If you cram things or people into a place, you put them into it even though there is hardly enough room for them.

words.tr:
v. 戳；刺；捅
n. 戳；刺；捅
words.ex: He poked the fire with a stick.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根棍子戳了戳火。
words.en: To poke means to prod or jab someone or something with a finger or a pointed object, or to move something in a particular direction with a sharp movement. It can also refer to the act of making a hole or opening in something by pushing a pointed object into it.

words.ex: I couldn't apprehend the math lesson because it was too fast.
words.ex_cn: 我无法理解这节数学课，因为讲得太快了。
words.en: If the police apprehend someone, they catch them and arrest them.

words.ex: The skeleton of the dinosaur is displayed in the museum.
words.ex_cn: 恐龙的骨架在博物馆里展出。
words.en: The internal structure that supports and gives shape to a person, animal, or plant, composed of bones and cartilage in vertebrates.

words.tr: n. 道德败坏；士气消沉
words.ex: The constant lies led to the demoralization of the community.
words.ex_cn: 持续的谎言导致了社区的道德败坏。
words.en: The process of undermining the confidence or morale of a person or group.

words.ex: The school prohibits students from using phones in class.
words.ex_cn: 学校禁止学生在课堂上使用手机。
words.en: If a law or someone in authority prohibits something, they forbid it or make it illegal.

words.ex: The law obliges drivers to wear seat belts.
words.ex_cn: 法律迫使司机系安全带。
words.en: If you are obliged to do something, you have to do it because the situation, the law, a duty, etc., makes it necessary.

words.ex: He tried to loosen the tight screw.
words.ex_cn: 他试图拧松那颗紧的螺丝。
words.en: If you loosen something or if it loosens, it becomes less tight, less firmly fixed, or less strongly attached.

words.tr: adj. 宏伟的；壮丽的；威严的；
words.ex: The majestic mountain stood above the clouds.
words.ex_cn: 那座宏伟的山峰耸立在云层之上。
words.en: If you describe something as majestic, you mean that it has a quality of greatness and impressiveness that often inspires admiration or awe.

words.ex: He disassembled the engine to find out what was wrong.
words.ex_cn: 他把发动机拆开，找出问题所在。
words.en: To take apart (a machine or structure) in order to examine it or repair it.

words.ex: The spectator watched the game quietly.
words.ex_cn: 旁观者安静地观看了比赛。
words.en: A spectator is someone who watches an event, show, game, or activity.

words.ex: The assembly of the car took three days.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的装配花了三天时间。
words.en: An assembly is a group of people gathered together for a particular purpose, such as a meeting or a legislative session. It can also refer to the process of fitting together the component parts of a machine or other object.

words.ex: My mother chides me for coming home late.
words.ex_cn: 我妈妈因为我回家晚而责备我。
words.en: If you chide someone, you speak to them angrily because they have done something wrong.

words.ex: She implored him to stay.
words.ex_cn: 她恳求他留下。
words.en: If you implore someone to do something, you ask them to do it in a forceful, emotional way.

words.ex: The water supply is adequate for the village.
words.ex_cn: 供水对这个村庄来说是足够的。
words.en: If something is adequate, there is enough of it or it is good enough to be used or accepted.

words.tr: v. 作…的摘要；成为…的缩影；概括；集中体现
words.ex: This painting epitomizes the beauty of nature.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画概括了自然的美。
words.en: If you say that something or someone epitomizes a particular thing, you mean that they are a perfect example of it.

words.tr:
n. 代表；典型事物；
adj. 典型的；有代表性的；代议制的；
words.ex: He is the representative of our class.
words.ex_cn: 他是我们班的代表。
words.en: A representative is a person who has been chosen to act or make decisions on behalf of another person or a group of people.

words.ex: He has a chronic cough that lasts for months.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个持续数月的慢性咳嗽。
words.en: A chronic illness or condition lasts for a long time and cannot be cured, but it can usually be controlled.

words.tr:
n. 编年史；年代记
v. 按时间顺序记录
words.ex: He writes a chronicle of his daily life.
words.ex_cn: 他记录自己每天的生活。
words.en: A chronicle is a historical account of events arranged in chronological order, typically without analysis or interpretation.

words.ex: His opinion is subordinate to the manager's.
words.ex_cn: 他的意见比经理的次要。
words.en: If someone is your subordinate, they have a less important position than you in the organization that you both work for.

words.ex: The confluence of the two rivers created a fertile valley.
words.ex_cn: 两条河流的汇流形成了一个肥沃的山谷。
words.en: The confluence of two or more things is the junction or merging of them, often forming something greater or more complex.

words.tr: adj. 可察觉到的；看得出的；可感知的
words.ex: The change was barely perceptible.
words.ex_cn: 这个变化几乎无法察觉。
words.en: Something that is perceptible can be seen, noticed, or felt.

words.ex: The volcano is quiescent now.
words.ex_cn: 这座火山现在处于休眠状态。
words.en: Someone or something that is quiescent is quiet and inactive.

words.ex: There was a surge in sales during the holiday season.
words.ex_cn: 假期期间销量激增。
words.en: If something surges, it increases suddenly and greatly, after having been steady or only small in size or amount.

words.tr:
v. 提取；
n. 摘录；提取物；
words.ex: They extract oil from plants.
words.ex_cn: 他们从植物中提取油。
words.en: To remove or take out something, especially by effort or force.

words.ex: The number of apples corresponds to the number of oranges.
words.ex_cn: 苹果的数量与橙子的数量相对应。
words.en: If one thing corresponds to another, there is a close similarity or connection between them, often because one is the cause or the result of the other.

words.ex: The architect showed us the blueprint of the new house.
words.ex_cn: 建筑师给我们看了新房子的蓝图。
words.en: A blueprint is a detailed plan or design of something, often used in the context of buildings or machinery, which shows how it is to be made or how it will work.

words.tr: adj. 有缺点的；有缺陷的；有毛病的；
words.ex: The defective phone wouldn't turn on.
words.ex_cn: 这部有缺点的手机无法开机。
words.en: If something is defective, there is something wrong with it and it does not work properly.

words.ex: The ad induced him to buy the product.
words.ex_cn: 这则广告诱使他购买了该产品。
words.en: To induce a state or condition means to cause it.

words.ex: The pedestrian crossed the street at the zebra crossing.
words.ex_cn: 行人在斑马线处过马路。
words.en: A pedestrian is a person who is walking in a city, town, or village, especially along a pavement or in a pedestrian area.

words.ex: He conveyed his thanks with a smile.
words.ex_cn: 他微笑着表达了谢意。
words.en: If you convey information or a message, you communicate it to someone, often in a way that is not direct.

words.tr: adj. 可怜的；悲哀的；差劲的；令人生厌的
words.ex: The little dog looked pathetic in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 那只小狗在雨中看起来很可怜。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as pathetic, you mean that they are sad and weak or inadequate, and you feel contempt or pity for them.

words.ex: The climax of the movie was a big chase scene.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的高潮是一场大追捕场景。
words.en: The climax is the most exciting or important part of a play, film, or piece of music, which usually happens near the end.

words.tr: adj. 谋取私利的；自私自利的
words.ex: He made a self-serving excuse to avoid blame.
words.ex_cn: 他找了一个自私的借口来推卸责任。
words.en: If you describe someone as self-serving, you are critical of them because they are only interested in what they can get for themselves.

words.ex: His opinion coincides with mine.
words.ex_cn: 他的观点与我的一致。
words.en: If one event coincides with another, they happen at the same time.

words.tr: v. 再循环；回流；再流通
words.ex: The air in the building is designed to recirculate through the ventilation system.
words.ex_cn: 大楼内的空气设计为通过通风系统再流通。
words.en: To circulate again or repeatedly.

words.tr:
n. 马笼头；缰绳；约束
v. 套笼头；表示恼怒；抑制
words.ex: He pulled the bridle to stop the horse.
words.ex_cn: 他拉了一下缰绳让马停下来。
words.en: A bridle is a set of straps that fits around a horse's head and is used to control the horse. As a verb, to bridle means to put a bridle on a horse or to restrain or control something.

words.ex: He tries to economize by walking to work.
words.ex_cn: 他通过步行上班来节省开支。
words.en: To economize means to use less money, time, or resources than usual in order to save them.

words.tr:
adj. 刺耳的；尖声的；尖厉的
v. 尖叫；发出刺耳的声音
words.ex: The baby's cry was shrill.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿的哭声很尖锐。
words.en: A shrill sound is high and unpleasant to listen to.

words.ex: He gave a strong rebuttal to the claim.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个说法给出了有力的反驳。
words.en: A rebuttal is a statement or piece of evidence that contradicts or opposes a previous statement or evidence.

words.ex: The dentist found a cavity in his tooth.
words.ex_cn: 牙医在他的牙齿上发现了一个腔。
words.en: A cavity is a hole or space inside something.

words.ex: The timid boy whispered his answer.
words.ex_cn: 这个害羞的男孩小声说出了他的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior or actions as timid, you are criticizing them for being too cautious or slow to act, because they are nervous about the possible consequences of their actions.

words.tr:
n. 侧面；侧翼；胁腹
v. 在…侧面（有）
words.ex: The soldiers moved to the flank to avoid the enemy.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们移动到侧翼以避开敌人。
words.en: The side of something, especially a part of the body between the ribs and the hip; to be situated on each side of or on one side of (something).

words.ex: The job position is still vacant.
words.ex_cn: 这个职位仍然空缺。
words.en: If something is vacant, it is not being used by anyone.

words.ex: A shudder ran through her when she saw the snake.
words.ex_cn: 当她看到蛇时，全身战栗了一下。
words.en: If you shudder, you shake with fear, horror, or disgust, or because you are cold.

words.ex: The country tried to devalue its currency.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家试图使本国货币贬值。
words.en: If you devalue something, you cause it to be thought less impressive or less deserving of respect.

words.ex: The child showed signs of talent in infancy.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子在婴儿期就表现出天赋。
words.en: The earliest period of childhood, especially before the ability to walk has been acquired.

words.tr:
n. 闪光；一刹那；
v. 闪光；闪现；
words.ex: The camera captured a sudden flash of light.
words.ex_cn: 相机捕捉到了一道突然的闪光。
words.en: A flash is a sudden bright light that quickly disappears. As a verb, it means to shine brightly for a short time or to appear or pass suddenly.

words.tr:
n. 针脚；缝线；一针
v. 缝；缝合
words.ex: She sews a stitch to fix the tear.
words.ex_cn: 她缝一针来补破洞。
words.en: A stitch is a piece of thread that has been used to sew the edges of a wound together. It can also refer to a loop of thread or yarn resulting from a single pass or movement of the needle in sewing, knitting, or crocheting.

words.ex: The frog is poisonous.
words.ex_cn: 这只青蛙是有毒的。
words.en: Something that is poisonous will kill you or make you ill if you eat it, drink it, or absorb it.

words.ex: He bought a luxury car as an extravagance.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一辆豪华汽车作为奢侈品。
words.en: Extravagance refers to the spending of more money than is reasonable or than you can afford, or the use of more of something than is necessary.

words.ex: They had a discord about the movie ending.
words.ex_cn: 他们对电影的结局有分歧。
words.en: Disagreement or strife between people or groups.

words.ex: He gave his mother a massage after work.
words.ex_cn: 他下班后给妈妈做了按摩。
words.en: The act of rubbing and pressing someone's body with the hands to reduce tension or pain in the muscles.

words.ex: They will dismantle the old bridge next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们下周将拆除这座旧桥。
words.en: To dismantle something means to take it to pieces.

words.ex: The city became post-industrial after the factories closed.
words.ex_cn: 工厂关闭后，这座城市进入了后工业时代。
words.en: relating to or denoting a period or society characterized by an economy that is no longer based on heavy industry and manufacturing, but on services and information

words.ex: The sun makes the puddle evaporate quickly.
words.ex_cn: 太阳使水坑很快蒸发。
words.en: If a liquid evaporates, or if something evaporates it, it changes from a liquid state to a gas, because its temperature has increased.

words.ex: The elephant is gigantic compared to a dog.
words.ex_cn: 这头大象相比狗来说是巨大的。
words.en: If you describe something as gigantic, you are emphasizing that it is extremely large in size, amount, or degree.

words.ex: The country uses metric units for weight and distance.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家使用米制单位来衡量重量和距离。
words.en: A metric is a system of measurement that uses meters, liters, and grams as its basic units.

words.tr:
v. 轻声笑；咯咯笑；暗自笑
n. 暗自发笑；咯咯声
words.ex: He chuckled when he saw the funny dog.
words.ex_cn: 他看到那只搞笑的狗时笑了起来。
words.en: To laugh quietly or inwardly.

words.tr: adj. 不断的；不停的；连续的
words.ex: The baby cried with incessant noise.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿不停地哭闹。
words.en: If you say that something is incessant, you are emphasizing that it continues without stopping.

words.ex: They tease him because he wears funny hats.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为他戴滑稽的帽子而戏弄他。
words.en: To tease someone means to make fun of them or try to provoke them in a playful way.

words.ex: His complacency made him lose the game.
words.ex_cn: 他的自满让他输掉了比赛。
words.en: A feeling of smug or uncritical satisfaction with oneself or one's achievements.

words.ex: The universe may be infinite.
words.ex_cn: 宇宙可能是无限的。
words.en: If you describe something as infinite, you are emphasizing that it is extremely great in amount or degree.

words.ex: High taxes are a disincentive to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 高税收是不愿更努力工作的障碍。
words.en: Something that discourages or prevents a particular action or behavior.

words.ex: He had to lug the heavy box across the room.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不用力拖动那个沉重的箱子穿过房间。
words.en: To carry or drag something heavy with great effort.

words.tr:
v. 喘气；喘息；倒抽气
n. 喘气；喘息
words.ex: He gasped when he saw the big snake.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到那条大蛇时，他倒吸了一口冷气。
words.en: To take a short, quick breath through the mouth, especially because of surprise, pain, or shock.

words.ex: The poison is lethal to humans.
words.ex_cn: 这种毒药对人类是致命的。
words.en: Something that is lethal can kill people or animals.

words.tr:
n. 奖品；裁定；
v. 授予；
words.ex: He received an award for best student.
words.ex_cn: 他获得了最佳学生奖。
words.en: An award is a prize or other mark of recognition given in honor of an achievement.

words.tr: v. （使）相互连接；（使）互相联系
words.ex: The cities are interconnect by high-speed trains.
words.ex_cn: 这些城市通过高速列车相互连接。
words.en: To connect with each other.

words.ex: The old temple is a relic from ancient times.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的寺庙是来自古代的遗迹。
words.en: An object surviving from an earlier time, especially one of historical or sentimental interest.

words.ex: She ate a prune for a healthy snack.
words.ex_cn: 她吃了一颗梅干作为健康零食。
words.en: To prune means to cut off some of the branches of a tree or bush to make it grow better. It can also mean to reduce the extent of something by removing superfluous or unwanted parts.

words.ex: He refines his writing every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天完善自己的写作。
words.en: To refine something means to make it purer or to improve it, especially by removing unwanted substances or by making small changes.

words.ex: Love is an intangible thing.
words.ex_cn: 爱是一种无形的东西。
words.en: Something that is intangible is not able to be touched or seen, but is still important or valuable.

words.tr:
v. 溢出；溅出
n. 溢出；溅出
words.ex: He spilled milk on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他把牛奶洒在了地上。
words.en: To cause or allow (a liquid, powder, etc.) to flow or fall out of a container, usually by accident.

words.tr:
v. 使不再抱幻想；使理想破灭
n. 幻灭；理想破灭
words.ex: The bad experience disillusioned him about politics.
words.ex_cn: 这次糟糕的经历让他对政治不再抱幻想。
words.en: If a person or thing disillusions you, they make you realize that something is not as good as you thought it was.

words.tr: adj. 可理解的；明白易懂的；清楚的
words.ex: His explanation was intelligible to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的解释人人都能听懂。
words.en: Capable of being understood; comprehensible.

words.ex: The company offers a defined-contribution pension plan to its employees.
words.ex_cn: 公司为其员工提供固定缴款退休金计划。
words.en: A defined-contribution plan is a type of retirement plan in which the employer, employee, or both make contributions on a regular basis. The final benefit depends on the amount contributed and the performance of the investments.

words.tr: v. 发誓放弃；断然丢弃
words.ex: He forswears lying to his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他发誓不再对朋友撒谎。
words.en: If you forswear something, you promise to stop doing it or having it, especially because you think it is bad or harmful.

words.ex: He uses inferential statistics to predict the result.
words.ex_cn: 他使用推断统计来预测结果。
words.en: Inferential means relating to or involving inference, which is the process of deriving logical conclusions from premises known or assumed to be true.

words.tr: v. 游移不定；踌躇；犹豫
words.ex: He vacillates between choosing tea or coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他在选择茶还是咖啡之间犹豫不决。
words.en: To vacillate means to waver between different opinions or actions; be indecisive.

words.tr:
n. 狂乱；狂暴；狂怒
v. 使狂乱；使狂怒
words.ex: The crowd went into a frenzy when the singer appeared.
words.ex_cn: 当歌手出现时，人群陷入了狂热。
words.en: A frenzy is a state of uncontrolled excitement or wild behavior.

words.ex: The lunatic was taken to the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 那个疯人被送到了医院。
words.en: A lunatic is someone who behaves in a crazy or very foolish way.

words.tr: adj. 值得注意的；显著的；著名的；
words.ex: This is a notable achievement.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个值得注意的成就。
words.en: Worthy of attention or notice; remarkable.

words.ex: He filed a complaint about the noisy neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 他投诉了吵闹的邻居。
words.en: A complaint is a statement in which you express your dissatisfaction with a particular situation.

words.ex: There was a scramble for the last ticket.
words.ex_cn: 大家争相抢购最后一张票。
words.en: If you scramble over rocks or up a hill, you move quickly over them or up it using your hands to help you. Scramble can also mean to compete or struggle with others for something that is in short supply.

words.ex: The class will commence at 9 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 课程将在上午9点开始。
words.en: To begin something; to start.

words.ex: He deceived his friend with a lie.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个谎言欺骗了朋友。
words.en: If you deceive someone, you make them believe something that is not true, usually in order to get some advantage for yourself.

words.tr: v. 沉思；闷闷不乐地想；n. 一窝幼崽；沉思的状态
words.ex: He sits by the window and broods over his failures.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在窗边，为自己的失败而忧思。
words.en: If someone broods over something, they think about it a lot, seriously and often unhappily. A brood is a group of young birds all born at the same time to the same mother.

words.tr:
v. 使安静；使肃静
n. 安静
words.ex: Please hush, the baby is sleeping.
words.ex_cn: 请安静，宝宝在睡觉。
words.en: If you hush someone or if they hush, they stop speaking or making a noise.

words.tr:
n. 运输；
v. 运输；
words.ex: He uses public transport to go to work.
words.ex_cn: 他乘坐公共交通去上班。
words.en: To transport something or someone is to move them from one place to another, especially over long distances.

words.ex: The sun descends behind the hills.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在山后落下。
words.en: If you descend or if you descend a staircase, you move downwards from a higher to a lower level.

words.tr:
v. 屠宰；屠杀
n. 屠宰；屠杀
words.ex: Farmers slaughter pigs for meat.
words.ex_cn: 农民宰猪取肉。
words.en: The killing of animals for food; the killing of a large number of people in a cruel or violent way.

words.tr: adj. 悲剧的；悲惨的；不幸的；
words.ex: The accident was a tragic event.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故是一场悲剧。
words.en: A tragic event or situation is extremely sad, usually because it involves death or suffering.

words.tr: v. 滥伐…的森林；乱砍…的树木
words.ex: They deforest the land to build houses.
words.ex_cn: 他们砍伐森林来建造房屋。
words.en: To deforest means to remove the trees from an area of land.

words.tr: v. 使带电；使电气化；使激动不已
words.ex: The new train system will electrify the entire region.
words.ex_cn: 新的火车系统将使整个地区电气化。
words.en: To electrify something means to make it operate using electricity or to make it more exciting or interesting.

words.ex: The math problem is complicated.
words.ex_cn: 这个数学问题很复杂。
words.en: Involving many different and confusing aspects.

words.tr:
adj. 浅薄的；庸俗的；格调低的
n. 教养不高的人
words.ex: He likes lowbrow comedy shows.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢低俗的喜剧节目。
words.en: If you say that something is lowbrow, you mean that it is easy to understand or appreciate rather than intellectual and is therefore perhaps inferior.

words.tr:
n. 抓痕；刮伤；
v. 抓搔；刮；
words.ex: The cat left a scratch on the door.
words.ex_cn: 猫在门上抓出了一道抓痕。
words.en: If you scratch something, you rub your fingernails or claws against it, often because it is itchy or irritating.

words.ex: The company will consolidate two departments next month.
words.ex_cn: 公司下个月将合并两个部门。
words.en: To consolidate something means to make it stronger, more secure, or more solid.

words.tr: adj. 美味的；使人愉快的
words.ex: The cake was delectable.
words.ex_cn: 这个蛋糕非常美味。
words.en: If you describe something, especially food or drink, as delectable, you mean that it is very pleasant.

words.ex: He finds peace through spiritual meditation.
words.ex_cn: 他通过精神上的冥想找到平静。
words.en: Relating to the human spirit or soul as opposed to material or physical things.

words.tr: v. 产生影响；形成结果；有助于；促进
words.ex: His hard work will redound to the benefit of his team.
words.ex_cn: 他的努力将对团队产生积极影响。
words.en: If an action or situation redounds to your benefit or advantage, it gives people a good impression of you or brings you something that you can take advantage of.

words.tr: n. 全体人员；人事部；职员；
words.ex: The company hired new personnel last month.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司上个月雇佣了新员工。
words.en: The people who are employed in a company or organization.

words.tr:
n. 小心；警告；注意；
v. 警告；劝...小心；
words.ex: He drove with caution on the icy road.
words.ex_cn: 他在结冰的道路上小心驾驶。
words.en: Caution is care that you take in order to avoid possible danger or trouble.

words.ex: He tries to restrain his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他努力克制自己的愤怒。
words.en: If you restrain someone, you stop them from doing what they intended or wanted to do, usually by using your physical strength.

words.ex: He has an appetite for spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢辛辣食物。
words.en: A desire or liking for something, especially food.

words.tr:
adj. 高位的；高尚的；欣喜的
v. 赞扬；提升；加强；“exalt”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The exalted king sat on a golden throne.
words.ex_cn: 这位高位的国王坐在一张金宝座上。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as exalted, you mean they are at a high level of honor, rank, or quality.

words.ex: Small commerce helps local towns grow.
words.ex_cn: 小商业有助于小镇的发展。
words.en: Commerce is the activity of buying and selling things, especially on a large scale.

words.tr:
n. 锻造车间；
v. 建立（联系等）；
words.ex: The blacksmith works in the forge every morning.
words.ex_cn: 铁匠每天早上都在锻造车间工作。
words.en: To forge something means to create it, especially by using considerable effort or skill. It can also mean to make or produce something, especially with some difficulty or effort. Additionally, it refers to the act of making a copy or imitation of something with the intent to deceive.

words.ex: He fastened the strap around his wrist.
words.ex_cn: 他把带子系在手腕上。
words.en: A strap is a narrow piece of leather, cloth, or other material that is used to fasten, secure, or carry something, or to hold onto something.

words.ex: Climbing the mountain was an arduous task.
words.ex_cn: 爬山是一项艰巨的任务。
words.en: Something that is arduous is difficult and tiring, and involves a lot of effort.

words.ex: The reception at the hotel was very friendly.
words.ex_cn: 酒店的接待非常友好。
words.en: The act of receiving or being received, especially in a formal or official context.

words.tr:
v. 阻碍；妨碍
n. （带盖）篮子
words.ex: Rain hampered our picnic plans.
words.ex_cn: 雨妨碍了我们的野餐计划。
words.en: If something hampers you, it makes it difficult for you to do something.

words.tr:
n. 猛跌；衰退；萧条期
v. 急剧下降；暴跌；重重地坐下（或倒下）
words.ex: The company's sales went into a slump last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月，这家公司的销售额下滑了。
words.en: If something such as the value of something slumps, it falls suddenly and by a large amount.

words.ex: We optimize the route to save time.
words.ex_cn: 我们优化路线以节省时间。
words.en: To optimize something means to make it as good or as effective as possible.

words.tr: v. 扩大；膨胀；更充分地阐述；
words.ex: The company plans to expand its business to other countries.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司计划将其业务扩大到其他国家。
words.en: To increase in size, number, or importance, or to make something increase in this way.

words.ex: He is amenable to new ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他愿意接受新想法。
words.en: If you are amenable to something, you are willing to do it or accept it.

words.tr:
adj. 不能治愈的；无可救药的
n. 患不治之症者；不能治愈的人
words.ex: The disease is incurable.
words.ex_cn: 这种病无法治愈。
words.en: If someone has an incurable disease, they cannot be cured of it.

words.ex: He punched the wall in anger.
words.ex_cn: 他生气地打了墙一拳。
words.en: To punch means to hit someone or something hard with your fist, or to make a hole in something using a tool.

words.ex: The teacher will assess your homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天会评估你的作业。
words.en: to judge or decide the amount, value, quality, or importance of something

words.tr: adj. 热情的；充满热情的；
words.ex: She is passionate about teaching children.
words.ex_cn: 她对教孩子充满热情。
words.en: Having, showing, or caused by strong feelings or beliefs.

words.ex: Honesty is the main tenet of his life.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是他生活的宗旨。
words.en: A tenet is a principle or belief, especially one that is part of a larger system of beliefs.

words.tr: n. 心智健全；神志清楚；神智健全
words.ex: The doctors questioned his sanity after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，医生们质疑他的精神是否健全。
words.en: The condition of having a healthy mind and not being mentally ill.

words.ex: The penal system aims to punish criminals.
words.ex_cn: 刑罚制度旨在惩罚罪犯。
words.en: Relating to, used for, or prescribing the punishment of offenders under the legal system.

words.ex: He tried to reconcile his work and family life.
words.ex_cn: 他试图调和工作与家庭生活。
words.en: If you reconcile two beliefs, facts, or demands that seem to be opposed or completely different, you find a way in which they can both be true or both be successful.

words.tr:
n. 成分；
adj. 构成的；
words.ex: Sugar is a constituent of soda.
words.ex_cn: 糖是苏打水的一种成分。
words.en: A constituent is a part of a whole. In politics, a constituent is a person who is represented by an elected official.

words.ex: He tried to repress his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抑制自己的愤怒。
words.en: If you repress a feeling, you deliberately do not express it, often because it is considered unacceptable or inappropriate.

words.ex: The doctor checked his daily intake of sugar.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了他每天的糖摄入量。
words.en: The process of taking something in, especially food, air, or information.

words.tr:
n. 法令；判决
v. 判决；颁布；裁定
words.ex: The king issued a decree to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 国王发布了一项法令来停止战争。
words.en: An official order issued by a legal authority.

words.ex: The mutation caused the plant to grow differently.
words.ex_cn: 这种突变使植物的生长方式发生了变化。
words.en: A mutation is a change in the structure of the genes of an organism that results in a variant form which may be transmitted to subsequent generations, caused by the alteration of single base units in DNA, or the deletion, insertion, or rearrangement of larger sections of genes or chromosomes.

words.ex: He worked hard and reaped the rewards.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作，获得了回报。
words.en: To reap means to cut and gather a crop, or to obtain something, especially as a result of effort.

words.ex: He is fortunate to have a good job.
words.ex_cn: 他很幸运拥有一份好工作。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is fortunate, you mean that they are lucky.

words.tr:
n. 反面；对立面；
adj. 对面的；
prep. 与…相对；
words.ex: The opposite of black is white.
words.ex_cn: 黑色的反面是白色。
words.en: If one thing is opposite another, it is on the other side of a space from it.

words.ex: You need to pay a 40-yuan deposit to rent the bike.
words.ex_cn: 租自行车需要支付40元押金。
words.en: A deposit is a sum of money which is part of the full price of something, and which you pay when you agree to buy it. It is also a sum of money that you pay into a bank account.

words.tr:
v. 闪烁；发微光
n. 微光；闪光
words.ex: The lake shimmers under the moonlight.
words.ex_cn: 湖面在月光下闪烁。
words.en: To shine with a soft, slightly wavering light.

words.tr:
n. 织布机；
v. 迫近；
words.ex: The old loom made a loud clicking sound.
words.ex_cn: 那台旧织布机发出很大的咔嗒声。
words.en: If something looms over you, it appears as a large or unclear shape, often in a way that is frightening or causes worry.

words.ex: He gave an explicit answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了明确的答案。
words.en: Something that is explicit is expressed or shown clearly and openly, without any attempt to hide anything.

words.ex: The apple will decompose in the soil.
words.ex_cn: 苹果会在土壤中分解。
words.en: If something decomposes, or if it is decomposed, it decays or breaks down into smaller parts or substances.

words.tr:
adj. 主要的；最重要的；
n. 校长；负责人；
words.ex: The principal reason for his success is hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他成功的主要原因是努力工作。
words.en: The person with the highest authority or most important position in an organization, institution, or group.

words.ex: It is advisable to wear a helmet when riding a bike.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔是明智的。
words.en: If something is advisable, it will avoid problems if you do it.

words.tr: adj. 杰出的；尚未处理的；
words.ex: He is an outstanding student who always gets top grades.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名杰出的学生，总是取得最高分。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as outstanding, you think that they are very remarkable and impressive.

words.tr:
n. 群；团；簇；
v. 聚集；
words.ex: The stars form a bright cluster in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 星星在夜空中形成了一群明亮的星群。
words.en: A cluster of things or people is a small group of them close together.

words.tr: n. 光泽；光彩；情致；荣光
words.ex: The antique vase had a beautiful lustre.
words.ex_cn: 这只古董花瓶有一种美丽的光泽。
words.en: Lustre refers to the gentle sheen or soft glow of a surface, especially one that is smooth and shiny. It can also denote the quality of being bright and radiant, often used metaphorically to describe something that adds distinction or glory.

words.tr: n. （身体或精神的）极度痛苦
words.ex: He felt deep anguish after losing his dog.
words.ex_cn: 失去狗后，他感到极度痛苦。
words.en: Anguish is extreme mental suffering or physical pain.

words.ex: He ignored the frivolous complaint and focused on the real issue.
words.ex_cn: 他忽略了这个无关紧要的投诉，专注于真正的问题。
words.en: If you describe someone as frivolous, you mean they behave in a silly or light-hearted way, rather than being serious and sensible.

words.tr: adj. 未工业化的；工业化前的；
words.ex: The village was still preindustrial in the 1800s.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄在19世纪仍然是未工业化的。
words.en: Relating to the time before industrialization, especially the period before the widespread use of machines in manufacturing.

words.ex: The clown amuses the children with funny tricks.
words.ex_cn: 小丑用滑稽的把戏娱乐孩子们。
words.en: If something amuses you, it makes you want to laugh or smile.

words.tr:
n. 下降；衰退；
v. 下降；衰退；
words.ex: There was a sharp decline in sales last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月销售额大幅下降。
words.en: If something declines, it becomes less in quantity, importance, or strength.

words.tr:
n. 污点；
v. 玷污；
words.ex: There is a coffee stain on the table.
words.ex_cn: 桌子上有一个咖啡污点。
words.en: A stain is a mark on something that is difficult to remove, especially one made by a liquid such as blood or coffee. To stain something means to leave a mark on it that is difficult to remove.

words.ex: The price of oil fluctuates every day.
words.ex_cn: 油价每天都在波动。
words.en: To fluctuate means to change or vary frequently and unpredictably.

words.tr:
n. 熊；
v. 承受；忍受；带有；生（孩子）；
words.ex: A bear walked near the campsite.
words.ex_cn: 一只熊在露营地附近走动。
words.en: If you bear something, you accept it and are able to deal with it, even though it is unpleasant or painful. A bear is a large, strong wild animal with thick fur and sharp claws.

words.tr: adj. 令人信服的； v. “compel”的现在分词；
words.ex: His story was compelling and made everyone listen.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事令人信服，让所有人都认真聆听。
words.en: A compelling argument or reason is one that makes you believe it or accept it because it is so strong.

words.ex: The manager will authorize the payment tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 经理明天将批准这笔付款。
words.en: To give official permission for something to happen, or to give someone official permission to do something.

words.tr:
n. 闪耀；闪烁；小发光物
v. 闪耀；闪亮；流露（感情）
words.ex: The glitter of the stars lit up the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 星星的闪耀照亮了夜空。
words.en: If something glitters, light comes from or is reflected off different parts of it.

words.tr:
v. 想要；
adj. 花哨的；昂贵的；
n. 爱好；
words.ex: I fancy a cup of tea.
words.ex_cn: 我想要一杯茶。
words.en: If you describe something as fancy, you mean that it is special, unusual, or elaborate, often because it has a lot of decoration or is very expensive.

words.ex: The buoyancy of the water helps the boat float.
words.ex_cn: 水的浮力帮助船漂浮。
words.en: Buoyancy is the ability of something to float in a liquid or to rise in air or gas.

words.tr: v. 使粉碎；使破碎；使破灭；
words.ex: The stone shattered when it hit the ground.
words.ex_cn: 石头撞到地面时碎裂了。
words.en: If something shatters or is shattered, it breaks into a lot of small pieces.

words.ex: The bonus is an incentive to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 奖金是努力工作的动机。
words.en: Something that encourages a person to do something or to work harder.

words.tr:
n. 名声；名誉；名望
v. 认为；以为
words.ex: He is of good repute in his town.
words.ex_cn: 他在镇上声誉很好。
words.en: The opinion generally held of someone or something; the state of being regarded in a particular way.

words.ex: He finally admit his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他终于承认了自己的错误。
words.en: If you admit that something bad, unpleasant, or embarrassing is true, you agree, often unwillingly, that it is true.

words.ex: He felt antipathy toward the loud neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对那个吵闹的邻居感到反感。
words.en: A deep-seated feeling of dislike; aversion.

words.ex: The boy resembles his father.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩长得像他父亲。
words.en: If one thing or person resembles another, they are similar to each other.

words.ex: The judge gave an unbiased decision.
words.ex_cn: 法官作出了无偏见的判决。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as unbiased, you mean they are fair and not likely to support one particular person or group involved in something.

words.ex: The hikers faced great peril in the storm.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者在风暴中面临巨大危险。
words.en: Peril refers to serious and immediate danger.

words.ex: The sweater shrinks in hot water.
words.ex_cn: 这件毛衣在热水中会收缩。
words.en: If something shrinks or you shrink it, it becomes smaller.

words.ex: His lecture was dry-as-dust and hardly anyone paid attention.
words.ex_cn: 他的讲座毫无生气，几乎没人注意听。
words.en: If you describe something such as a book, play, or activity as dry-as-dust, you are criticizing it because it is very dull and uninteresting.

words.tr:
v. （使）回旋；（使）旋转
n. 一连串的事；混乱；尝试
words.ex: The wind makes the leaves whirl around.
words.ex_cn: 风让树叶旋转飞舞。
words.en: To move or cause to move rapidly around and around.

words.tr: adj. 永久的；永恒的；经久不变的
words.ex: The love between them is everlasting.
words.ex_cn: 他们之间的爱是永恒的。
words.en: Something that is everlasting lasts forever or for a very long time.

words.ex: Children are often adaptable to new environments.
words.ex_cn: 孩子通常能适应新环境。
words.en: If someone or something is adaptable, they are able to change their ideas or behaviour in order to deal with new situations.

words.ex: He is a temperate person who never shouts.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个温和的人，从不大喊大叫。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as temperate, you mean that it is calm and reasonable, not extreme or emotional.

words.ex: His perception of the sound was very sharp.
words.ex_cn: 他对声音的感知非常敏锐。
words.en: Your perception of something is the way that you think about it or the impression you have of it.

words.tr: v. 照射；用放射线处理；使明亮
words.ex: The sun irradiates the earth every day.
words.ex_cn: 太阳每天照射地球。
words.en: To expose to radiation; to illuminate or enlighten.

words.ex: I recommend this book to you.
words.ex_cn: 我向你推荐这本书。
words.en: If someone recommends a person or thing to you, they suggest that you would find them good or useful.

words.tr:
v. 补充；
n. 补充物；附加费；
words.ex: He supplements his income by teaching part-time.
words.ex_cn: 他通过兼职教学来补充收入。
words.en: A supplement is something that is added to something else in order to make it complete or better.

words.ex: The child recites the poem every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子每天早上背诵这首诗。
words.en: To repeat aloud or declaim (a poem or passage) from memory before an audience.

words.ex: His affective response to the news was tears.
words.ex_cn: 他听到这个消息时的情感反应是流泪。
words.en: Relating to moods, feelings, and attitudes.

words.ex: He tried to integrate into the new school community.
words.ex_cn: 他试图融入新的学校群体。
words.en: If someone integrates into a social group, or is integrated into it, they behave in such a way that they become part of the group or are accepted into it.

words.ex: They communicate well with each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们彼此沟通得很好。
words.en: To communicate means to share or exchange information, news, or ideas, especially by speaking or writing.

words.ex: He remained unaffected by the noise.
words.ex_cn: 他没有受到噪音的影响。
words.en: If someone or something is unaffected by an event or occurrence, they are not changed by it in any way.

words.ex: The cream-of-the-crop students were selected for the advanced program.
words.ex_cn: 精英学生们被选入了高级课程。
words.en: The very best or top-quality among a group; the most excellent or superior.

words.tr: adj. 大量的；不吝惜的；浪费的
words.ex: He was profuse in thanks after the rescue.
words.ex_cn: 获救后，他表达了深深的感谢。
words.en: If you describe something as profuse, you mean that it is very plentiful or abundant.

words.tr: adj. 虔诚的；衷心的；诚挚的；
words.ex: He is a devout Christian who goes to church every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名虔诚的基督徒，每周日都去教堂。
words.en: If you describe someone as devout, you mean that they have a deep religious faith.

words.ex: The tiger has black stripes on its orange fur.
words.ex_cn: 老虎的橙色皮毛上有黑色条纹。
words.en: A stripe is a long, narrow band or strip differing in color or texture from the surface on either side of it.

words.tr: adj. 徒劳的；空虚的；自负的；爱慕虚荣的
words.ex: It's vain to try to fix what can't be fixed.
words.ex_cn: 试图修复无法修复的东西是徒劳的。
words.en: If you describe someone as vain, you are critical of their extreme pride in their own beauty, intelligence, or other good qualities.

words.ex: The loud thunder terrified the child.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的雷声吓坏了那个孩子。
words.en: If something terrifies you, it makes you feel extremely frightened.

words.ex: The court will prosecute him for theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院将因盗窃罪起诉他。
words.en: To prosecute means to institute legal proceedings against someone or to carry on a legal action against a defendant in a court of law. It also means to continue with or carry on an activity or enterprise.

words.tr: v. 充塞；充血；使拥挤；充满
words.ex: The traffic congests the city center during rush hour.
words.ex_cn: 高峰时段，交通堵塞了市中心。
words.en: If a place is congested, it is extremely crowded and blocked with traffic or people.

words.tr: adj. 攻击性的；有进取心的；侵略性的；
words.ex: The dog showed aggressive behavior toward strangers.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗对陌生人表现出攻击性行为。
words.en: An aggressive person or animal has a quality of anger and determination that makes them ready to attack others.

words.tr:
adj. 分散的；权力分散的
v. 分散；权力分散；“decentralize”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The government has decentralized power to regional authorities.
words.ex_cn: 政府已将权力下放到地方当局。
words.en: Decentralized refers to the distribution of functions, powers, people, or things away from a central location or authority.

words.ex: The president may be impeached for lying.
words.ex_cn: 总统可能因撒谎而被弹劾。
words.en: If a government official is impeached, they are formally charged with a serious crime in a special government court.

words.ex: He defecated after eating breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他吃完早餐后排便了。
words.en: To defecate means to discharge feces from the body.

words.tr: adj. 感激的；欣赏的；表示赞赏的
words.ex: She was appreciative of his help.
words.ex_cn: 她对他的帮助心怀感激。
words.en: If you are appreciative of something, you are grateful for it.

words.ex: He wore a big grin after winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得比赛后露出了灿烂的咧嘴笑容。
words.en: If you grin, you smile broadly, usually showing your teeth.

words.ex: The child imitates her mother's voice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子模仿她妈妈的声音。
words.en: If you imitate someone, you copy what they do or produce.

words.ex: I admire my teacher for her patience.
words.ex_cn: 我钦佩我的老师有耐心。
words.en: If you admire someone or something, you like and respect them very much.

words.tr: v. 割让（领土）；放弃（权力）
words.ex: He will cede his land to the government.
words.ex_cn: 他将把土地让给政府。
words.en: To give up control or possession of something, especially land or territory, often as a result of war or negotiation.

words.tr: v. 逐步渗透；逐渐灌输
words.ex: Parents try to instill good habits in their children.
words.ex_cn: 父母试图在孩子身上培养良好的习惯。
words.en: To instill something in someone means to gradually but firmly establish an idea or attitude in their mind.

words.tr:
v. 利用；
n. 马具；
words.ex: We must harness the power of the sun.
words.ex_cn: 我们必须利用太阳的能量。
words.en: A harness is a set of straps which fit under a person's arms and fasten round their body in order to keep a piece of equipment in place or to prevent the person moving from a place.

words.ex: He modulates his voice to sound calm.
words.ex_cn: 他调节自己的声音以显得平静。
words.en: To modulate means to change or adjust something, such as your voice or a piece of equipment, to achieve a desired effect or to make it suitable for a particular situation.

words.ex: The external wall of the house is painted blue.
words.ex_cn: 房子的外墙被刷成了蓝色。
words.en: External is used to indicate that something is on the outside of a surface or body, or that it exists, happens, or comes from outside.

words.ex: The satellite beams signals to Earth.
words.ex_cn: 卫星向地球发射信号。
words.en: A beam is a long, thick piece of wood, metal, or concrete that is used to support the roof of a building. It can also refer to a line of light that shines from a bright object, or a smile that shows someone is very happy.

words.ex: The teacher designated him as the group leader.
words.ex_cn: 老师指派他为组长。
words.en: If you designate someone or something as a particular thing, you formally give them that description or name.

words.ex: The captive man sat quietly in his cell.
words.ex_cn: 那个被监禁的人安静地坐在牢房里。
words.en: A captive is someone who is being kept as a prisoner or in a confined space, or something that is held or confined.

words.ex: It was an utter mistake.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个完全的错误。
words.en: To say something or to make a sound with your voice; complete or absolute.

words.ex: The soup was palatable after adding salt.
words.ex_cn: 加了盐后，汤变得可口美味了。
words.en: If you describe food or drink as palatable, you mean that it tastes pleasant.

words.tr: n. 有价值的人或物；长处；
words.ex: He is an asset to the team because he works hard.
words.ex_cn: 他是个有价值的人，因为他工作努力。
words.en: An asset is something valuable that an individual, corporation, or country owns or controls with the expectation that it will provide a future benefit.

words.ex: The rain dampened the sound of the drums.
words.ex_cn: 雨减弱了鼓声。
words.en: To dampen something means to make it slightly wet, or to make it less strong or intense.

words.ex: The accident traumatized him for life.
words.ex_cn: 那次事故使他终生受创。
words.en: If someone is traumatized by an event or situation, it shocks or upsets them very much, and may cause them psychological damage.

words.tr:
v. 抽出；节省；
adj. 备用的；多余的；空闲的；
words.ex: Can you spare a few minutes to help me?
words.ex_cn: 你能抽出几分钟帮我吗？
words.en: If you have something such as time, money, or space to spare, you have some extra time, money, or space that you have not used or which you do not need.

words.ex: He underestimated the difficulty of the test.
words.ex_cn: 他低估了考试的难度。
words.en: If you underestimate something, you do not realize how large, great, or serious it is.

words.tr:
n. 委员会；佣金；
v. 委托；
words.ex: The commission met to discuss the new law.
words.ex_cn: 委员会开会讨论新法律。
words.en: A commission is a group of people who have been appointed to find out about something or to control something, or the act of doing this. It can also refer to a sum of money that is paid to someone for selling something, which is usually a percentage of the value of the goods sold.

words.ex: The storm was destructive and broke many houses.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴具有破坏性，摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: Causing great and irreparable harm or damage.

words.tr: adj. 开创性的；突破性的；
words.ex: This is a groundbreaking discovery in medicine.
words.ex_cn: 这是医学领域的一项开创性发现。
words.en: If something is groundbreaking, it is very new and a big change from other things of its type.

words.ex: He is self-motivated and studies every day.
words.ex_cn: 他很有主动性，每天都学习。
words.en: Someone who is self-motivated is able to work hard and achieve their goals without needing encouragement from other people.

words.ex: The mirror creates an illusion of a bigger room.
words.ex_cn: 镜子制造出房间更大的错觉。
words.en: An illusion is a false idea or belief, especially about yourself or your situation.

words.ex: His deduction was based on the evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他的推论基于证据。
words.en: A deduction is a conclusion that you reach about something because of other things that you know to be true.

words.ex: He is a reliable friend who always helps.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个可靠的朋友，总是帮忙。
words.en: Able to be trusted to do or provide what is needed or right.

words.ex: He smashed the glass with a hammer.
words.ex_cn: 他用锤子把玻璃打碎了。
words.en: To break something into pieces violently and noisily, or to cause something to do this by dropping, throwing, or hitting it.

words.ex: Blood circulates in the body.
words.ex_cn: 血液在体内循环。
words.en: To move or cause to move continuously or freely through a closed system or area.

words.tr:
v. 移栽；移植；
n. 移植；
words.ex: He will transplant the flowers to the garden tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天要把这些花移栽到花园里。
words.en: To transplant something means to move it from one place to another. In medicine, to transplant an organ, piece of skin, etc. means to use it to replace a damaged part in someone's body.

words.ex: The ice melts in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 冰在阳光下融化。
words.en: If a solid substance melts or if you melt it, it changes to a liquid, usually because it has been heated.

words.ex: The accident was fatal.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故是致命的。
words.en: If an action or event is fatal, it causes someone's death.

words.ex: She showed great affection for her little dog.
words.ex_cn: 她对她的小狗非常钟爱。
words.en: A feeling of liking and caring for someone or something.

words.ex: This phone is superior to the old one.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机比旧的更好。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as superior, you mean that they are better than other people or things.

words.ex: The spy tried to infiltrate the enemy base.
words.ex_cn: 间谍试图渗透敌方基地。
words.en: To enter or gain access to (an organization, place, etc.) surreptitiously and gradually, especially in order to acquire secret information.

words.ex: He looked at the catalog to find the book.
words.ex_cn: 他翻看目录来找那本书。
words.en: A catalog is a list of things, such as the goods you can buy from a particular company, the objects in a museum, or the books in a library.

words.tr: phrase. 卡片目录（用于图书馆中按卡片索引图书的系统）
words.ex: He found the book using the card catalogue.
words.ex_cn: 他通过卡片目录找到了这本书。
words.en: A card catalogue is a system for organizing information about the books and other materials in a library, consisting of cards with information on them that are arranged in a particular order.

words.ex: Don't interfere when I am working.
words.ex_cn: 我工作时不要打扰。
words.en: To interfere means to involve oneself in a situation where one is not wanted or needed, often causing problems or hindering progress.

words.ex: The child let out a loud shriek when she saw the spider.
words.ex_cn: 当孩子看到蜘蛛时，发出了一声大叫。
words.en: If someone shrieks, they make a short, very loud cry, for example because they are suddenly surprised, are in pain, or are laughing.

words.ex: He cited a book in his essay.
words.ex_cn: 他在文章中引用了一本书。
words.en: To cite something means to quote it or mention it as evidence or proof of what you are saying.

words.ex: He is encumbered by too many debts.
words.ex_cn: 他被太多的债务拖累。
words.en: To encumber someone or something means to weigh them down or to block or hinder them.

words.tr:
adj. 瘸的；跛的；站不住脚的；无说服力的
v. 变跛；瘸行
words.ex: The lame dog walked slowly on three legs.
words.ex_cn: 那只瘸狗用三条腿慢慢走。
words.en: If someone is lame, they are unable to walk properly because of damage to one or both of their legs. A lame excuse, explanation, etc. is one that is weak and difficult to believe.

words.ex: A small fissure appeared in the wall.
words.ex_cn: 墙上出现了一道小裂缝。
words.en: A fissure is a long, narrow opening or line of breakage made by cracking or splitting, especially in rock or earth.

words.ex: The broken bridge is a menace to drivers.
words.ex_cn: 这座破桥对司机来说是个危险物。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is a menace, you mean that they are likely to cause serious harm.

words.ex: The angle of the roof helps rain run off.
words.ex_cn: 屋顶的角度有助于雨水流下。
words.en: An angle is the space between two lines or surfaces that meet, measured in degrees.

words.ex: He went to the consulate to get a visa.
words.ex_cn: 他去领事馆办理签证。
words.en: A consulate is the place where a consul works, which is an official who is sent by their country to live in a foreign city in order to help other citizens from their own country and to represent their country's commercial interests.

words.ex: He is an eccentric man who wears socks with sandals.
words.ex_cn: 他是个古怪的人，穿着袜子配凉鞋。
words.en: If you say that someone is eccentric, you mean that they behave in a strange way, and have habits or opinions that are different from those of most people.

words.ex: Henceforth, I will wake up early.
words.ex_cn: 从今以后，我会早起。
words.en: From this time on; from now on.

words.ex: The advent of smartphones changed how we communicate.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机的到来改变了我们的交流方式。
words.en: The arrival of a notable person, thing, or event.

words.ex: He felt discontent with his job.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的工作感到不满。
words.en: Discontent is a feeling of being unhappy because you are not satisfied with your situation or with what you have.

words.ex: He faced racial discrimination at work.
words.ex_cn: 他在工作中遭遇了种族歧视。
words.en: Relating to the common characteristics of different races of people, especially in the context of social or cultural differences.

words.ex: Drugs can alleviate pain.
words.ex_cn: 药物可以减轻疼痛。
words.en: To make something less severe or intense.

words.ex: I feel sympathy for the poor children.
words.ex_cn: 我对那些可怜的孩子感到同情。
words.en: If you have sympathy for someone who is in a bad situation, you are sorry for them, and show this in the way you behave towards them.

words.ex: The dark clouds looked ominous before the storm.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨来临前，乌云显得不祥。
words.en: If you describe something as ominous, you mean that it worries you because it makes you think that something unpleasant is going to happen.

words.tr:
n. 用力拉；拖拽；拖船
v. 用力拉；使劲拖；拖拽
words.ex: He gave a strong tug on the rope.
words.ex_cn: 他用力拉了绳子一下。
words.en: If you tug something or tug at it, you give it a quick and usually strong pull.

words.ex: The team was unanimous in choosing the new leader.
words.ex_cn: 团队在选择新领导时意见完全一致。
words.en: When a group of people are unanimous, they all agree about something or all vote for the same thing.

words.tr: adj. 坦率的；坦诚的；偷拍的
words.ex: He gave a candid answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了坦率的回答。
words.en: If you are candid, you are honest and say what you really think.

words.ex: He felt great woe after losing his dog.
words.ex_cn: 他失去狗后感到极大的悲伤。
words.en: Woe is great sadness.

words.tr: n. 中风；划水动作；一击；
words.ex: He had a stroke last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年中风了。
words.en: A stroke is a medical condition in which poor blood flow to the brain results in cell death. It can also refer to an act of hitting or striking someone or something, or a gentle movement of the hand over a surface.

words.tr: v. 使相混；使联结；交际
words.ex: He mingled the two colors to make a new one.
words.ex_cn: 他把两种颜色混合在一起，创造出一种新颜色。
words.en: If things such as sounds, smells, or feelings mingle, they mix or combine with each other, or if people mingle, they talk to each other at a social event.

words.ex: The hustle of the market filled the morning air.
words.ex_cn: 市场的熙攘充满了清晨的空气。
words.en: If you hustle, you work hard to do something quickly, especially in order to earn money.

words.tr: adj. 焦虑的；渴望的；担忧的；
words.ex: He feels anxious before every test.
words.ex_cn: 他每次考试前都感到焦虑。
words.en: If you are anxious to do something or anxious that something should happen, you very much want to do it or very much want it to happen.

words.ex: The operation of the machine is very smooth.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器的运行非常顺畅。
words.en: An operation is a planned activity involving many people performing various tasks.

words.ex: They conspire to cheat on the test.
words.ex_cn: 他们密谋在考试中作弊。
words.en: If two or more people or groups conspire to do something illegal or harmful, they make a secret agreement to do it.

words.tr: v. 劈砍；侵入（计算机等）
words.ex: He hacked the tree with an axe.
words.ex_cn: 他用斧头劈砍那棵树。
words.en: To hack means to cut or chop something with rough or heavy blows, or to gain unauthorized access to data in a system or computer.

words.ex: The child loves to play with fantasy stories about dragons.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子喜欢玩关于龙的幻想故事。
words.en: A fantasy is a pleasant situation or event that you imagine, which is unlikely to happen.

words.tr:
v. 使根深蒂固；“engrain”的过去式和过去分词
adj. 根深蒂固的
words.ex: Her engrained habits are hard to change.
words.ex_cn: 她根深蒂固的习惯很难改变。
words.en: If something is engrained, it is firmly established and therefore difficult to change.

words.ex: The temperature rose marginally yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 昨天温度略微上升了。
words.en: To a very small extent; slightly.

words.tr: v. 促进；推动；宣传；推销；
words.ex: Exercise can promote good health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以促进健康。
words.en: To promote means to help something to happen, develop, or increase, or to raise someone to a higher position or rank.

words.ex: The Magna Carta is an old charter of rights.
words.ex_cn: 《大宪章》是一份古老的权力宪章。
words.en: A charter is a formal document describing the rights, aims, or principles of an organization or group of people.

words.ex: The team was relegated to the second division after losing all their games.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍在输掉所有比赛后被降级到第二级别联赛。
words.en: If you relegate someone or something to a less important position, you give them this position.

words.tr:
n. 平方；广场；正方形；四方形；
adj. 正方形的；四方形的；平方的；成直角的；
v. 与...一致；
adv. 成直角地；
words.ex: The area of the room is 16 square.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间的面积是16平方米。
words.en: A square is a shape with four sides of equal length and four angles of 90 degrees. It can also refer to an open area in a town, often used for public events, or to the result of multiplying a number by itself.

words.ex: The two colors distinguish the two teams.
words.ex_cn: 这两种颜色使两个队伍有所不同。
words.en: If you can distinguish one thing from another, you can see or understand how they are different.

words.ex: He wants to apply for a job at the bank.
words.ex_cn: 他想申请银行的工作。
words.en: To make a formal request, usually in writing, for something such as a job, a place at a university, or permission to do something.

words.tr: adj. 首要的；主要的；基本的；最好的；
words.ex: This is the prime reason for the delay.
words.ex_cn: 这是延误的首要原因。
words.en: Prime is used to describe something that is of the best possible quality, or the most important or basic part of something.

words.ex: The movie shows too much violence.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了太多的暴力。
words.en: Violence is behavior which is intended to hurt, injure, or kill people.

words.tr: adj. 无关紧要的；不相关的；
words.ex: His opinion is irrelevant to the decision.
words.ex_cn: 他的意见与这个决定无关紧要。
words.en: If you describe something as irrelevant, you mean that it is not important to or not connected with the present situation or discussion.

words.ex: The two rooms adjoin each other.
words.ex_cn: 这两个房间彼此相邻。
words.en: If one room, place, or object adjoins another, they are next to each other.

words.tr: adj. 分不开的；形影不离的
words.ex: They are inseparable friends.
words.ex_cn: 他们是形影不离的朋友。
words.en: If two or more people are inseparable, they are such good friends that they spend most of their time together.

words.ex: The music accompanies the dance.
words.ex_cn: 音乐伴随舞蹈。
words.en: To go somewhere with someone as a companion or escort; to play a musical accompaniment for.

words.ex: The police opened an enquiry into the accident.
words.ex_cn: 警方对这起事故展开了调查。
words.en: An enquiry is a question you ask in order to get some information.

words.tr: v. 邀请；“invite”的现在分词； adj. 诱人的；吸引人的；
words.ex: He is inviting his friends to dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他正在邀请他的朋友来吃晚饭。
words.en: If you describe something as inviting, you mean that it has good qualities that attract you or make you want to experience it.

words.ex: The company's revenue increased last year.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司的收入去年增加了。
words.en: Revenue is the income that a company, organization, or government receives regularly.

words.tr:
v. 禁止；
n. 禁止；
words.ex: The school bans phones in class.
words.ex_cn: 学校禁止在课堂上使用手机。
words.en: If there is a ban on something, it is not allowed. If something is banned, it is not allowed to be done, shown, or used.

words.ex: His countenance showed surprise.
words.ex_cn: 他的面容流露出惊讶。
words.en: A person's face or facial expression; support or approval.

words.ex: The scientist tried to replicate the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家试图复制这个实验。
words.en: To replicate something means to do or make something again in exactly the same way.

words.tr:
v. 使目眩；使眼花；使惊叹
n. 耀眼；眩惑；灿烂
words.ex: The stars dazzle at night.
words.ex_cn: 夜晚的星星闪耀夺目。
words.en: If something dazzles you, it is so bright that you cannot see properly for a short time. It can also mean to greatly impress someone.

words.ex: The loud noise startle the bird.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音惊动了那只鸟。
words.en: If something or someone startles you, they surprise and frighten you slightly.

words.tr:
n. 怨恨；积怨；嫌隙
v. 勉强做；不情愿地给；吝惜
words.ex: He holds a grudge against his brother.
words.ex_cn: 他对他哥哥心怀怨恨。
words.en: A grudge is a persistent feeling of ill will or resentment resulting from a past insult or injury.

words.ex: The teacher will terminate the class at 5 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 老师将在下午5点结束课程。
words.en: To terminate something means to bring it to an end or to stop it from continuing.

words.ex: The boss appointed Tom as the new manager.
words.ex_cn: 老板任命汤姆为新经理。
words.en: If you appoint someone to a job or official position, you formally choose them for it.

words.ex: The glare of the sun made it hard to see.
words.ex_cn: 阳光的刺眼使我看不清。
words.en: If you glare at someone, you look at them with an angry expression on your face. Glare is also a very bright light that is uncomfortable to look at.

words.ex: The movie aroused his curiosity.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影激起了他的好奇心。
words.en: If something arouses a particular reaction or attitude in people, it causes them to have that reaction or attitude.

words.tr: adj. 油腔滑调的；口齿伶俐的；圆滑的
words.ex: He gave a glib answer to the difficult question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个难题给出了一个轻率的回答。
words.en: If you describe what someone says as glib, you disapprove of it because it implies that something is simple or easy, or that there are no problems involved, when this is not the case.

words.tr: adj. 诱导的；归纳的；感应的
words.ex: The scientist used inductive reasoning to form a hypothesis.
words.ex_cn: 科学家使用归纳推理来形成一个假设。
words.en: Inductive reasoning involves making broad generalizations from specific observations.

words.ex: He shoved his way through the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他挤过人群。
words.en: To push someone or something in a rough or careless way.

words.ex: The mistake was trivial and didn't affect the result.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误不重要，没有影响结果。
words.en: If you describe something as trivial, you mean that it is not important or significant, or is not worth serious consideration.

words.ex: The two countries signed a pacific agreement.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家签署了一项和平协议。
words.en: A pacific person, country, or policy is peaceful and seeks to avoid conflict.

words.tr:
n. 幻灯片；滑梯；
v. （使）滑动；下滑；
words.ex: He showed a slide of his vacation photos.
words.ex_cn: 他展示了一张他度假照片的幻灯片。
words.en: To move smoothly along a surface while maintaining continuous contact with it; to pass or move quietly or smoothly; a structure with a smooth sloping surface for children to slide down; a decline from a higher to a lower level or status.

words.ex: The concrete mix was designed to maximize pumpability.
words.ex_cn: 这种混凝土混合物被设计成具有最大泵送能力。
words.en: The capability of a material to be pumped or the ease with which it can be pumped.

words.ex: His neglect of the project caused delays.
words.ex_cn: 他对项目的疏忽导致了延误。
words.en: If you neglect someone or something, you fail to give them the attention or care that they need.

words.ex: The Senate will ratify the treaty next week.
words.ex_cn: 参议院下周将批准这项条约。
words.en: If a country or organization ratifies a treaty or agreement, they make it official by giving their formal approval to it, usually by signing it or voting for it.

words.tr: adj. 失业的；待业的；下岗的；
words.ex: He is unemployed after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业了，因为失去了工作。
words.en: If someone is unemployed, they do not have a job.

words.ex: He looked at her with suspicion.
words.ex_cn: 他带着怀疑的眼神看着她。
words.en: A feeling or thought that something is possible, likely, or true, especially something bad or wrong, without having proof.

words.ex: Fish abound in this river.
words.ex_cn: 这条河里鱼很多。
words.en: If things abound, or if a place abounds with things, there are very large numbers of them.

words.ex: He felt so sad that he thought about suicide.
words.ex_cn: 他感到非常难过，以至于想到了自杀。
words.en: Suicide is the act of deliberately killing oneself.

words.ex: He flipped the pancake with a spatula.
words.ex_cn: 他用铲子快速翻转了煎饼。
words.en: To flip something means to turn it over quickly one or more times, or to make something do this.

words.ex: The prophet told the people about the coming storm.
words.ex_cn: 预言者告诉人们即将到来的风暴。
words.en: A prophet is a person who is believed to be chosen by God to lead the people and to tell them what God wants them to do.

words.tr: v. 将…分类；把…加以归类
words.ex: We categorize books by genre.
words.ex_cn: 我们按类型对书籍进行分类。
words.en: To categorize means to put people or things into groups according to their type or characteristics.

words.ex: The big rock was an obstacle on the road.
words.ex_cn: 那块大石头是路上的障碍。
words.en: An obstacle is something which makes it difficult for you to go forward or to achieve something.

words.ex: The project involves the contiguity of several different disciplines.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目涉及几个不同学科的连续性。
words.en: The state of bordering or being in contact with something.

words.ex: The roller coaster gave her a thrill.
words.ex_cn: 过山车让她感到兴奋。
words.en: A thrill is a sudden feeling of great excitement, pleasure, or fear.

words.ex: I saw him yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 我昨天看见他了。
words.en: You use him to refer to a man, boy, or male animal that has already been mentioned or is easily identified.

words.tr: adj. 令人惊奇的；奇妙的
words.ex: The sunset looked wondrous over the sea.
words.ex_cn: 夕阳在海面上看起来奇妙无比。
words.en: If you describe something as wondrous, you mean it is strange and beautiful or impressive.

words.ex: The fish spawn in the river each spring.
words.ex_cn: 鱼每年春天在河里产卵。
words.en: To spawn means to produce or deposit eggs, especially in large quantities, as fish, frogs, etc. do. It can also mean to give rise to or generate something.

words.ex: He believes in capitalism and owns a small business.
words.ex_cn: 他相信资本主义，并拥有一家小企业。
words.en: Capitalism is an economic system in which the means of production are privately owned and operated for profit in a competitive market.

words.ex: His motive was to help his family.
words.ex_cn: 他的动机是帮助家人。
words.en: Your motive for doing something is your reason for doing it.

words.ex: The magic trick astounded the children.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术让孩子们惊呆了。
words.en: If something astounds you, it surprises or shocks you very much.

words.ex: He overestimated his ability to finish the task in one day.
words.ex_cn: 他过高估计了自己一天内完成任务的能力。
words.en: If you overestimate something, you think it is greater in amount or more important than it really is.

words.tr: adj. 谨慎的；慎重的；精明的
words.ex: He is prudent with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他在花钱时很谨慎。
words.en: If you are prudent, you are careful and avoid taking unnecessary risks.

words.tr: n. 药物；药物治疗；药物处理；
words.ex: He took his medication every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃药。
words.en: Medication refers to a substance used for medical treatment, especially a medicine or drug.

words.tr:
v. 伸展；延伸；持续；
n. 一段；伸展；
words.ex: He stretches his arms every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上伸展手臂。
words.en: To stretch is to extend your body or a part of your body to its full length, or to extend something else to its full length or beyond its normal limits.

words.tr:
n. （鸟或羊）群；（人）群；
v. 聚集；群集；
words.ex: A flock of birds flew over the field.
words.ex_cn: 一群鸟飞过田野。
words.en: A flock is a group of birds, sheep, or goats, or a large group of people. It can also refer to a soft material for stuffing cushions, quilts, etc., made from wool or cotton. As a verb, it means to gather or move in a flock.

words.ex: The celebrity smiled at the fans outside the theater.
words.ex_cn: 这位名人向剧院外的粉丝微笑。
words.en: A celebrity is a famous person, especially in entertainment or sports.

words.tr: n. 机械（总称）；机械装置；
words.ex: The factory uses old machinery to produce goods.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂使用旧机械来生产产品。
words.en: Machinery refers to machines in general or the parts of a machine that make it work.

words.ex: The riot broke out after the game.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束后爆发了骚乱。
words.en: A riot is a violent disturbance of the peace by a crowd.

words.tr:
v. 潦草地写；匆匆地写；乱涂乱画
n. 潦草的字迹；涂鸦
words.ex: He scribbled his name on the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他在纸上潦草地写了名字。
words.en: To scribble means to write or draw something quickly or carelessly.

words.tr: adj. 无害的；不触犯人的；不讨厌的
words.ex: He gave an inoffensive answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个无害的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as inoffensive, you mean that they are not unpleasant or unacceptable in any way.

words.ex: Don't overrate his skills; he is not that good.
words.ex_cn: 不要高估他的能力；他没那么好。
words.en: If you say that something or someone is overrated, you mean that people consider them to be better or more important than they really are.

words.tr:
v. 放电；放出；
