words.tr: adj. 游历的；游离不定的；行为不当的；出轨的
words.ex: The errant knight traveled far across the land.
words.ex_cn: 这位游历的骑士穿越了广袤的土地。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as errant, you mean that they have strayed from the proper course or standards.

words.ex: The desert has a harsh climate.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠的气候非常严酷。
words.en: If you describe something as harsh, you mean that it is extremely difficult and unpleasant to live in, do, or experience, especially because it is very cold, hot, or violent.

words.tr:
n. 媒介；方法；
adj. 中等的；适中的；
words.ex: TV is a popular medium for advertising.
words.ex_cn: 电视是一种流行的广告媒介。
words.en: A medium is a method or way of expressing something.

words.ex: The invasion of privacy is a serious problem.
words.ex_cn: 侵犯隐私是一个严重的问题。
words.en: An invasion is an instance of invading a country or region with an armed force.

words.ex: The police enforce the law.
words.ex_cn: 警察强制执行法律。
words.en: If people in authority enforce a law or a rule, they make sure that it is obeyed, usually by punishing people who do not obey it.

words.tr: n. 引人注目的人或物；溅污的斑点；
words.ex: The new singer became a splash on the music scene.
words.ex_cn: 这位新歌手成为了音乐界引人注目的人物。
words.en: To cause (a liquid) to scatter in drops or small quantities, especially by striking or moving suddenly; to move or strike so as to cause a liquid to scatter in this way.

words.ex: He wants to study psychology at university.
words.ex_cn: 他想在大学学习心理学。
words.en: Psychology is the scientific study of the human mind and the reasons for people's behaviour.

words.tr:
n. 聚光灯；
v. 使公众注意；
words.ex: The spotlight shone on the singer during the concert.
words.ex_cn: 演唱会上，聚光灯照在歌手身上。
words.en: A spotlight is a powerful light, for example in a theatre, which can be directed so that it lights up a small area. If someone or something is in the spotlight, they are getting a lot of attention from the public and the media.

words.ex: The doctor prescribed medicine for my cold.
words.ex_cn: 医生给我开了治疗感冒的药。
words.en: If a doctor prescribes medicine or treatment for you, he or she tells you what medicine or treatment to have.

words.tr: adj. 广大的；广阔的；广泛的；大量的；
words.ex: He has extensive knowledge of history.
words.ex_cn: 他拥有广博的历史知识。
words.en: Something that is extensive covers a wide area or includes a lot of things.

words.tr:
n. 水平；程度；等级；
adj. 平齐的；
v. 使平坦；
words.ex: His English level is very high.
words.ex_cn: 他的英语水平很高。
words.en: A level is a point on a scale, for example a scale of amount, quality, or difficulty.

words.ex: The gland secrete sweat to cool the body.
words.ex_cn: 腺体分泌汗液来降温。
words.en: If part of a plant, animal, or human secretes a liquid or substance, it produces it.

words.ex: The two notes sound harmonic together.
words.ex_cn: 这两个音听起来很和谐。
words.en: Relating to or characterized by harmony; pleasing to the ear; melodious.

words.ex: The hero in the story is an archetype of courage.
words.ex_cn: 故事中的英雄是勇气的原型。
words.en: An archetype is a very typical example of a certain person or thing.

words.ex: There is strife between the two neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 这两个邻居之间有争执。
words.en: Strife is angry or violent conflict between two people or groups.

words.tr: adj. 相关的；有联系的； v. 关联；“relate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: This book is related to science.
words.ex_cn: 这本书与科学相关。
words.en: If two or more things are related, there is a connection between them.

words.ex: The Earth revolves around the Sun.
words.ex_cn: 地球围绕太阳转。
words.en: If something revolves or if you revolve something, it moves or turns around a central point or line.

words.tr:
n. 最高统治者；君主；元首
adj. 独立自主的；拥有最高统治权的
words.ex: The sovereign makes important decisions for the country.
words.ex_cn: 君主为国家做出重要决定。
words.en: A sovereign is a king, queen, or other supreme ruler.

words.tr:
n. 崇拜；崇敬；礼拜；
v. 崇拜；尊崇；做礼拜；
words.ex: The ancient people showed worship to the sun.
words.ex_cn: 古人对太阳进行崇拜。
words.en: The feeling or expression of reverence and adoration for a deity.

words.tr: n. 替代选择；替代选择（alternative 的复数）；
words.ex: We need to find better alternatives to plastic.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要找到比塑料更好的替代选择。
words.en: An alternative is something that you can choose to do or use instead of something else.

words.tr:
n. 振动；剧跳；极度的紧张不安；抽搐；痉挛；“jitter”的复数
v. 颤抖；战战兢兢；紧张不安；紧张地说；使…惶恐不安；“jitter”的第三人称单数
words.ex: The old bridge began to show jitters when the truck passed over it.
words.ex_cn: 当卡车驶过时，这座旧桥开始出现振动。
words.en: A feeling of extreme nervousness.

words.tr:
v. 计算；看作；清点；
n. 计数；计算；
words.ex: He counts the apples on the table.
words.ex_cn: 他计算桌子上的苹果数量。
words.en: To determine the total number of a collection of items.

words.tr:
n. 纪律；学科；科目；训练；惩戒；
v. 约束自己；
words.ex: The teacher enforced discipline in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 老师在教室里维持纪律。
words.en: Discipline is the practice of making people obey rules or standards of behaviour, and punishing them when they do not.

words.ex: The teacher will notify the students about the test.
words.ex_cn: 老师会通知学生们关于考试的事。
words.en: If you notify someone of something, you officially inform them about it.

words.ex: Exercise can elevate your mood.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提升你的情绪。
words.en: To elevate something means to raise it to a higher position or level, either physically or in terms of its status or importance.

words.ex: The soil is too infertile to grow crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片土地太贫瘠了，无法种植庄稼。
words.en: Infertile land or soil is not able to produce good crops or plants. An infertile person, animal, or plant cannot have babies, eggs, or seeds.

words.ex: The glass is brittle and breaks easily.
words.ex_cn: 这种玻璃很硬但容易碎。
words.en: If something is brittle, it is hard and easily broken.

words.ex: The company wants centralization for better control.
words.ex_cn: 公司希望集中管理以更好地控制。
words.en: The process or policy of concentrating control of an organization or activity under a single authority.

words.ex: The recalcitrant student refused to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这个顽抗的学生拒绝遵守规则。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as recalcitrant, you mean that they are unwilling to obey orders or are difficult to deal with.

words.ex: The child's recovery was a miracle.
words.ex_cn: 孩子的康复是个奇迹。
words.en: A miracle is an event that cannot be explained by the laws of nature and is therefore considered to be the work of a divine agency.

words.ex: She stayed in a luxurious hotel with gold faucets.
words.ex_cn: 她住进了一家有金色水龙头的奢侈酒店。
words.en: Something that is luxurious is very comfortable and expensive, and often involves great pleasure or indulgence.

words.ex: He gave a sincere apology.
words.ex_cn: 他真诚地道歉了。
words.en: If you say that someone is sincere, you approve of them because they really mean the things they say.

words.tr: adj. 令人厌恶的；讨厌的；抵触的
words.ex: The smell was repugnant.
words.ex_cn: 那气味令人厌恶。
words.en: If you think that something is horrible and disgusting, you can say that it is repugnant.

words.ex: He tried to detach himself from the group.
words.ex_cn: 他试图脱离这个群体。
words.en: If you detach one thing from another that it is fixed to, you remove it. If one thing detaches from another, it becomes separated from it.

words.ex: The accident caused severe mutilation of his hand.
words.ex_cn: 这次事故导致他的手严重切断。
words.en: The act of damaging someone's body, especially by cutting off or damaging a part of it.

words.tr: v. 遗赠；遗留；把…传下去
words.ex: He bequeathed his house to his daughter.
words.ex_cn: 他把房子遗赠给了他的女儿。
words.en: If you bequeath your money or property to someone, you legally state that they should have it when you die.

words.ex: The smell of bread pervades the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 面包的香味弥漫在整个厨房里。
words.en: If something pervades a place or thing, it is present throughout it.

words.ex: The minority group voted for change.
words.ex_cn: 少数群体投票支持变革。
words.en: A minority is a group of people within a community or country who are different from the majority of the people there in race, religion, or political beliefs.

words.ex: The storm deprived us of electricity.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴剥夺了我们的电力。
words.en: If you deprive someone of something that they want or need, you take it away from them, or you prevent them from having it.

words.ex: He is gullible and believes every story he hears.
words.ex_cn: 他很容易受骗，相信每一个他听到的故事。
words.en: If you describe someone as gullible, you mean they are easily tricked because they are too trusting.

words.ex: The army besiege the small town.
words.ex_cn: 军队围攻这座小镇。
words.en: To surround a place with armed forces in order to capture it or force its surrender; to overwhelm someone with requests or complaints.

words.ex: I assume it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我假定明天会下雨。
words.en: If you assume that something is true, you accept that it is true without proof.

words.tr:
adj. 主要的；首要的；
n. 领袖；首领；
words.ex: He is the chief reason for the team's success.
words.ex_cn: 他是球队成功的主要原因。
words.en: The chief is the leader of a group or organization, or the main part of something.

words.tr:
v. 覆盖；叠加；铺；镀
n. 覆盖物；涂层
v. 躺在…上面；把（婴儿）覆闷致死；“overlie”的过去式
words.ex: He put an overlay on the photo to add text.
words.ex_cn: 他在照片上叠加了一层以添加文字。
words.en: To cover something with a layer of another material, or to lie on top of something else.

words.tr:
adv. 头向前地；倒栽葱地；急速地；鲁莽地
adj. 头向前的；倒栽葱的；急速的；急骤的
words.ex: He jumped headlong into the pool.
words.ex_cn: 他头向前地跳进了泳池。
words.en: If you move headlong in a particular direction, you move there very quickly and without thinking carefully about what you are doing.

words.ex: His answer was pertinent to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答与问题相关。
words.en: Something that is pertinent is relevant to a particular subject.

words.ex: The king abrogated the old law.
words.ex_cn: 国王废除了旧法律。
words.en: If someone in a position of authority abrogates something such as a law, agreement, or practice, they put an end to it.

words.ex: The old man looked gaunt after his illness.
words.ex_cn: 这场病后，老人显得消瘦。
words.en: If someone looks gaunt, they look very thin, usually because they have been ill or worried.

words.tr:
adj. 动态的；有活力的；不断变化的；
n. 活力；动力；
words.ex: The game has dynamic weather that changes every hour.
words.ex_cn: 这个游戏有每小时变化的动态天气。
words.en: If you describe someone as dynamic, you approve of them because they are full of energy or full of new ideas.

words.tr: v. 沉思；冥想；考虑；仔细计划
words.ex: He meditates every morning to feel calm.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上冥想以保持平静。
words.en: To meditate means to spend time in quiet thought for religious purposes or relaxation.

words.ex: The car stopped in an instantaneous moment.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在瞬间停了下来。
words.en: Happening or done immediately.

words.ex: He has a delusion that he is a famous singer.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种错觉，认为自己是一位著名歌手。
words.en: A delusion is a belief or impression that is firmly maintained despite being contradicted by what is generally accepted as reality or rational argument, typically a symptom of mental disorder.

words.ex: He was accused of complicity in the theft.
words.ex_cn: 他被指控参与了这起盗窃案。
words.en: Complicity is involvement with other people in an illegal activity or wrongdoing.

words.tr:
n. 度假胜地；手段；
v. 求助于；
words.ex: They went to a beach resort for their vacation.
words.ex_cn: 他们去一个海滨度假胜地度假。
words.en: If you resort to a particular course of action, you do it because you cannot see any other way of achieving what you want.

words.ex: The latent talent in the child became clear after years of practice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子潜在的才能在多年练习后显现出来。
words.en: Latent is used to describe something which is hidden and not obvious at the moment, but which may develop further in the future.

words.tr: n. （有条件的）投降；投降条约
words.ex: The capitulation of the city marked the end of the war.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市的投降标志着战争的结束。
words.en: The act of surrendering or yielding under specified conditions; a document containing the terms of surrender.

words.ex: Honesty is a great virtue.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是一种伟大的美德。
words.en: A virtue is a good quality or way of behaving.

words.ex: The remainder of the cake was given to the neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 蛋糕的剩余部分给了邻居。
words.en: The remainder is what is left over after other parts have been taken away or used.

words.ex: The school used to segregate students by race.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校过去按种族隔离学生。
words.en: To segregate means to separate one group of people, animals, or things from another, especially because they are of different types or belong to different categories.

words.ex: Salt water causes corrosion on metal.
words.ex_cn: 盐水会导致金属腐蚀。
words.en: Corrosion is the process in which a metal is gradually destroyed by a chemical reaction, usually with oxygen or water.

words.tr: n. 外观；样子；相似；表象
words.ex: She tried to maintain a semblance of normality.
words.ex_cn: 她试图维持一种正常的假象。
words.en: The outward appearance or apparent form of something, especially when the reality is different.

words.tr:
v. 防止；战斗；抑制；
n. 战斗；
words.ex: The new law aims to combat pollution.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律旨在防止污染。
words.en: Combat refers to fighting, especially during a war. It can also mean to try to stop something harmful from happening or increasing.

words.ex: Birds inhabit the forest near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类居住在湖边的森林里。
words.en: If a place or region is inhabited by a group of people or a species of animal, those people or animals live there.

words.ex: She uses moisturizer every morning.
words.ex_cn: 她每天早上使用保湿霜。
words.en: A moisturizer is a cosmetic preparation used to prevent dryness in the skin.

words.tr: adj. 角的；有角的；尖角的；
words.ex: The angular shape of the triangle is clear.
words.ex_cn: 三角形的角形很清晰。
words.en: having angles or sharp corners; lean and bony

words.ex: The concept of freedom is important in many countries.
words.ex_cn: 自由这个观念在许多国家都很重要。
words.en: A concept is an idea or abstract principle.

words.ex: The storm disrupted the train service.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴中断了火车服务。
words.en: To disrupt a system, process, or event means to prevent it from continuing or operating in a normal way.

words.ex: The sensory experience of eating chocolate is wonderful.
words.ex_cn: 吃巧克力的感觉体验很棒。
words.en: Sensory means relating to the physical senses of touch, smell, taste, hearing, and sight.

words.ex: The storm personifies anger with loud thunder.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴用雷声拟人化了愤怒。
words.en: To represent a thing or abstraction as a person; to embody in a person.

words.tr:
v. 喷射；迸发；突然加速努力
n. 迸发；喷出；突然一阵
words.ex: The pipe spurted water everywhere.
words.ex_cn: 管道喷出了水，四处都是。
words.en: A spurt is a sudden burst of activity, speed, or growth. It can also refer to a sudden stream of liquid that comes out quickly and forcefully.

words.tr:
v. 惊异于；惊异；
n. 令人惊异的人（或事）；
words.ex: I marvel at how fast she runs.
words.ex_cn: 我惊异于她跑得有多快。
words.en: If you marvel at something, you express your great surprise, wonder, or admiration.

words.ex: The rainwater drains into the street.
words.ex_cn: 雨水排入街道。
words.en: If you drain something, you remove the liquid from it, usually by pouring it away or by allowing it to flow away. If something drains, the liquid flows away from it.

words.tr:
v. 见证；
n. 证人；目击者；
words.ex: He witnessed the accident yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 他昨天目睹了那起事故。
words.en: A witness is someone who sees an event happen, especially a crime or an accident. Witnesses are often called upon to give evidence in court.

words.ex: The doctor gave him proper treatment for the infection.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他提供了针对感染的适当治疗。
words.en: The act or manner of treating someone or something, especially in a medical context.

words.ex: He tries to belittle his brother's success.
words.ex_cn: 他试图贬低他哥哥的成功。
words.en: To belittle someone or something means to make them seem less important or less good than they really are.

words.tr:
n. 降落伞
v. 跳伞；用降落伞空投
words.ex: He jumped from the plane and opened his parachute.
words.ex_cn: 他从飞机上跳下并打开了降落伞。
words.en: A parachute is a device used to slow the motion of an object through an atmosphere by creating drag.

words.ex: He must confront his fears.
words.ex_cn: 他必须面对自己的恐惧。
words.en: If you confront a difficult situation or issue, you accept the fact that it exists and try to deal with it.

words.ex: The virus can mutate quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒可以迅速变异。
words.en: If an animal or plant mutates, or something mutates it, it develops different characteristics as the result of a change in its genes.

words.tr: n. 有文化修养的人；有高雅趣味的人；
words.ex: He is a highbrow who loves classical music and old novels.
words.ex_cn: 他是个有文化修养的人，喜欢古典音乐和古典小说。
words.en: A highbrow person or thing is interested in or concerned with intellectual or cultural matters, often to the exclusion of more practical or popular interests.

words.ex: The troop marched into the town at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 部队在黎明时分进入城镇。
words.en: A troop is a group of soldiers or a large group of people or animals.

words.ex: The loud music distract me from my homework.
words.ex_cn: 嘈杂的音乐让我无法专心做作业。
words.en: If something distracts you or your attention, it makes you stop concentrating on what you are doing.

words.ex: The new plan incorporates feedback from students.
words.ex_cn: 新计划包含了学生的反馈。
words.en: If one thing incorporates another thing, it includes the other thing.

words.ex: The exterior of the house is painted white.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子的外观是白色的。
words.en: The outer surface or structure of something.

words.ex: Her perspicacity helped her solve the problem quickly.
words.ex_cn: 她的洞察力帮助她迅速解决了问题。
words.en: The ability to understand and judge things quickly and accurately.

words.ex: The rain was unavoidable during the storm.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨期间，下雨是不可避免的。
words.en: If something is unavoidable, it cannot be avoided or prevented.

words.ex: The strange noise confounded the children.
words.ex_cn: 奇怪的声音让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: To confuse and surprise someone, especially by being difficult to understand or deal with.

words.tr:
v. 奉承；讨好
adj. 更平坦的；更扁平的；“flat”的比较级
adv. 更平直地；更直截了当地；“flat”的比较级
words.ex: He flatters his boss to get a raise.
words.ex_cn: 他奉承老板以获得加薪。
words.en: If someone flatters you, they praise you in an exaggerated way that may be sincere or may be intended to persuade you to do something.

words.ex: He refused to disclose the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝透露这个秘密。
words.en: To disclose information means to make it known to the public.

words.ex: He is a competent teacher who helps students easily.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有能力的老师，能轻松帮助学生。
words.en: If you are competent to do something, you have the skills, abilities, or experience necessary to do it well.

words.ex: The company wants diversification to reduce risk.
words.ex_cn: 公司希望通过多元化来降低风险。
words.en: Diversification is the act of making something more diverse or varied, especially in business contexts where it refers to expanding into new markets or products.

words.ex: The mobile table can be moved easily.
words.ex_cn: 这个可移动的桌子很容易搬动。
words.en: A mobile is something that can move or be moved easily.

words.ex: Water is a basic necessity for life.
words.ex_cn: 水是生命的基本必需品。
words.en: Something that is necessary or indispensable.

words.tr:
n. 指挥；命令；
v. 掌握；
words.ex: The general has command of the army.
words.ex_cn: 将军指挥着军队。
words.en: If someone in authority commands you to do something, they tell you that you must do it.

words.tr: adj. 谦逊的；不夸耀的；不矫饰的
words.ex: The house had an unpretentious charm that made it feel welcoming.
words.ex_cn: 这座房子有一种不炫耀的魅力，让人感到宾至如归。
words.en: If you describe a place, person, or thing as unpretentious, you approve of them because they are simple in appearance or character, rather than sophisticated or luxurious.

words.ex: The punishment was disproportionate to the crime.
words.ex_cn: 惩罚与罪行不成比例。
words.en: Something that is disproportionate is surprisingly large or small in comparison to something else.

words.ex: He made a strategic decision to save money.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了一个有战略性的决定来省钱。
words.en: Relating to the identification of long-term or overall aims and interests and the means of achieving them.

words.ex: She picked up a thread from the fabric.
words.ex_cn: 她从布料上捡起一根线。
words.en: A thread is a long, thin strand of cotton, nylon, or other fibers used in sewing or weaving. It can also refer to a theme or idea that connects parts of a story or discussion.

words.tr: adj. 根本的；彻底的；激进的；
words.ex: The government made radical changes to the education system.
words.ex_cn: 政府对教育系统进行了根本性的改革。
words.en: A radical change or difference is very big and important.

words.ex: The doctor will transfuse blood to the patient.
words.ex_cn: 医生将给病人输血。
words.en: To transfer (as a fluid) into a vein or an artery of a person or animal; to instill or communicate gradually.

words.ex: The forest has abundant water and trees.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林水源和树木都很丰富。
words.en: If something is abundant, there is a lot of it or it is very common.

words.ex: The mechanic tightened the bolt with a wrench.
words.ex_cn: 机械师用扳手拧紧了螺栓。
words.en: A bolt is a type of fastener consisting of a threaded pin or rod with a head at one end, designed to be inserted through holes in assembled parts and tightened by a nut from the other end. It can also refer to a sudden dash or run, or to eat food quickly and without chewing.

words.ex: The teacher did normalization of the test scores.
words.ex_cn: 老师对考试成绩进行了正常化。
words.en: The process of making something normal or standard, especially in the context of social or political relations.

words.tr: v. 断言；宣称；坚持；维护
words.ex: He asserts that the answer is correct.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持认为答案是正确的。
words.en: To state a fact or belief confidently and forcefully.

words.ex: He tried to smuggle cigarettes across the border.
words.ex_cn: 他试图走私香烟过境。
words.en: To smuggle goods or people means to move them into or out of a country illegally.

words.ex: The library keeps old newspapers in an archive.
words.ex_cn: 图书馆把旧报纸保存在档案馆里。
words.en: A collection of historical documents or records providing information about a place, institution, or group of people.

words.ex: The company listened to the stakeholders before making the decision.
words.ex_cn: 公司在做决定前听取了利益相关者的意见。
words.en: A stakeholder is a person, group, or organization that has an interest or concern in an organization, project, or business.

words.ex: He twitched the rope to pull the box closer.
words.ex_cn: 他猛地一拉绳子，把箱子拉近了些。
words.en: To make a sudden, small movement with a part of your body, especially because you are nervous or in pain.

words.ex: Sugar is an ingredient in this cake.
words.ex_cn: 糖是这个蛋糕的一个成分。
words.en: An ingredient is one of the substances that are combined to make something, especially in cooking.

words.tr: adj. 该受责备的；应受谴责的
words.ex: He is blameworthy for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他因这个错误而应受责备。
words.en: If someone or something is blameworthy, they deserve to be blamed for something bad that has happened.

words.tr:
v. 牺牲；
n. 牺牲（品）；
words.ex: He sacrificed his time to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他牺牲了自己的时间来帮助朋友。
words.en: If you sacrifice something that is valuable or important, you give it up, usually to obtain something else for yourself or for other people.

words.ex: This temperature is the optimum for growing plants.
words.ex_cn: 这个温度是最适宜植物生长的。
words.en: The optimum is the best or most favorable condition, degree, amount, etc., for achieving a particular result.

words.tr:
n. 谷歌（网络搜索引擎）；
vt. 用搜索引擎搜索（尤指用谷歌搜索引擎）；
words.ex: I use Google to find information online.
words.ex_cn: 我使用谷歌在网上查找信息。
words.en: To use the Google search engine to find information on the internet.

words.ex: The knight held up his shield to block the arrow.
words.ex_cn: 骑士举起盾牌来挡箭。
words.en: A shield is a piece of armor held in the hand or worn on the arm to protect the body from missiles or blows. It can also refer to something that protects or defends someone or something from harm or danger.

words.ex: The car consumes a lot of gas.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车消耗很多汽油。
words.en: To consume something means to eat or drink it, or to use it up in some way.

words.tr:
adj. 安详的；安静的；镇静的
v. 给…服镇静剂
words.ex: The sedate old man sat quietly by the window.
words.ex_cn: 那位安详的老人安静地坐在窗边。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as sedate, you mean that they are quiet, calm, and dignified.

words.tr: n. 律师；辩护律师；代理人
words.ex: The attorney helped the man with his case.
words.ex_cn: 律师帮助那个人处理了他的案件。
words.en: An attorney is a lawyer who is qualified to represent a client in court.

words.tr:
n. 洗涤槽；水槽；
v. （使）沉没；
words.ex: The dirty dishes are in the sink.
words.ex_cn: 脏盘子在水槽里。
words.en: If a boat sinks, or if something sinks it, it disappears below the surface of a mass of water.

words.tr: n. 含意；可能的影响（或后果）；暗示；
words.ex: The implication of his words was that he was sorry.
words.ex_cn: 他话中的含意是他很抱歉。
words.en: An implication is a possible future effect or result of an action or decision, often one that is not immediately obvious.

words.tr:
n. 探测器；
v. 探查；
words.ex: The probe sent back photos from Mars.
words.ex_cn: 探测器从火星传回了照片。
words.en: If you probe into something, you ask questions or try to discover facts about it. A probe is also a long thin instrument that doctors and dentists use to examine parts of the body.

words.tr:
v. 睡眠
n. 睡眠（常复数）
words.ex: The baby fell into a deep slumber after feeding.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝喂完奶后进入了深深的睡眠。
words.en: Slumber is a state of sleep, especially one that is peaceful and restful.

words.tr: adj. 奇怪的；奇数的；余的；
words.ex: He wore an odd hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶奇怪的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as odd, you mean that they are strange or unusual.

words.ex: The two lines intersect at point A.
words.ex_cn: 两条线在点A相交。
words.en: If two or more lines or roads intersect, they meet or cross each other.

words.ex: The machine makes a perpetual noise.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器发出持续的噪音。
words.en: Something that is perpetual continues indefinitely or for a very long time without interruption.

words.tr:
n. 禁止贸易令；禁运
v. 禁止…的贸易；禁运
words.ex: The country placed an embargo on imported goods.
words.ex_cn: 该国对进口商品实施了禁运。
words.en: An embargo is an official order to stop trade with another country.

words.ex: He read the previous chapter last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚读了前一章。
words.en: Existing or occurring before in time or order.

words.tr:
n. 群；蜂群
v. 云集；充满
words.ex: Bees swarm around the flower.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂围绕着花朵成群飞舞。
words.en: A swarm is a large group of insects, especially bees, moving together. As a verb, it means to move in or form a swarm.

words.ex: The child mimics her mother's voice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子模仿她妈妈的声音。
words.en: If someone or something mimics another person or thing, they try to be like them or copy their behavior or characteristics.

words.ex: The doctor ran a trial to test the new medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生进行了试验来测试这种新药。
words.en: A trial is a formal meeting in a law court, at which a judge and jury listen to evidence and decide whether a person is guilty of a crime.

words.ex: He went back to retrieve his keys.
words.ex_cn: 他回去取回他的钥匙。
words.en: To retrieve something means to get it back from somewhere, especially after it has been lost or taken away.

words.ex: This plan is viable and can be done with little money.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划是可行的，而且用很少的钱就能完成。
words.en: If something is viable, it is capable of doing what it is intended to do.

words.ex: The restaurant has a calm ambience.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅有一种宁静的氛围。
words.en: The character and atmosphere of a place.

words.tr: n. 怀疑论者；怀疑宗教主张的人；无神论者
words.ex: He is a skeptic about new health claims.
words.ex_cn: 他对新的健康说法持怀疑态度。
words.en: A skeptic is a person who questions the validity or authenticity of something purporting to be factual.

words.tr: adj. 逃避的；推托的；闪烁其辞的
words.ex: He gave an evasive answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个回避的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone as evasive, you mean that they deliberately avoid giving clear direct answers to questions.

words.tr: adj. 精力充沛的；茂盛的；
words.ex: He is a vigorous man who runs every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个精力充沛的人，每天早上都跑步。
words.en: A vigorous person does things with great energy and enthusiasm. A vigorous campaign or activity is done with great energy and enthusiasm.

words.ex: He tried to bribe the officer with money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用钱贿赂官员。
words.en: A bribe is a sum of money or something valuable that one person offers or gives to another in order to persuade them to do something, usually something dishonest.

words.ex: He was deferential to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他对老师很恭敬。
words.en: If you are deferential, you are polite and respectful towards someone, especially because they have a higher position or status than you.

words.ex: His ambition is to become a president.
words.ex_cn: 他的野心是成为总统。
words.en: An ambition is a strong desire to achieve something, typically requiring determination and hard work.

words.ex: The mirage in the desert is an illusive image.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠中的海市蜃楼是一个虚幻的景象。
words.en: If something is illusive, it is based on an illusion and is not real or true.

words.tr: n. 黄昏；薄暮；暮光；衰退期
words.ex: The birds fly home at twilight.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在黄昏时飞回家。
words.en: The time of day immediately following sunset, or the period of time at the end of the day when the sun is just below the horizon, especially the period between sunset and dark.

words.ex: He is aware of the danger.
words.ex_cn: 他意识到危险。
words.en: If you are aware of something, you know about it.

words.ex: He is martially trained in karate.
words.ex_cn: 他接受过武术训练，擅长空手道。
words.en: In a manner that is characteristic of or befitting a warrior; bravely.

words.ex: The car stopped at the verge of the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车停在了道路的边缘。
words.en: The edge or border of something; to be close to a certain state or condition.

words.tr:
adj. 热诚的；友好的
n. 甜露酒
words.ex: He gave a cordial smile to his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对着邻居露出了热情的微笑。
words.en: warm and friendly

words.ex: The water in the pond dwindles in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天时，池塘里的水逐渐减少。
words.en: If something dwindles, it becomes smaller, weaker, or less in number.

words.ex: We should conserve water in daily life.
words.ex_cn: 我们应在日常生活中节约用水。
words.en: To conserve something means to protect it from harm, loss, or change, especially in order to preserve it for the future.

words.tr:
adj. 破旧不堪的；受虐待的
v. 连续猛击；殴打；严重破坏；“batter”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He had a battered old bike.
words.ex_cn: 他有一辆破旧的自行车。
words.en: Damaged by being used a lot or hit repeatedly; also, subjected to physical violence.

words.tr:
v. 发抖；打颤；战栗；焦虑
n. 震颤；发抖；战栗
words.ex: The old man tremble in the cold wind.
words.ex_cn: 老人在寒风中发抖。
words.en: If you tremble, you shake slightly because you are frightened or cold.

words.ex: The teacher asked a simple question to elicit answers from students.
words.ex_cn: 老师问了一个简单的问题来引出学生的回答。
words.en: To elicit a response or a reaction means to cause it to happen by something that you say or do.

words.ex: He accustoms himself to waking up early.
words.ex_cn: 他让自己习惯早起。
words.en: If you accustom yourself or someone else to something, you make yourself or them familiar with it or used to it.

words.ex: The school needs more resources for students.
words.ex_cn: 学校需要为学生提供更多的资源。
words.en: A resource is a source or supply from which benefit is produced. Typically resources are materials, energy, services, staff, knowledge, or other assets that are transformed to produce benefit and in the process may be consumed or made unavailable.

words.ex: He hastened to finish his homework before dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他赶紧在晚饭前写完作业。
words.en: If you hasten to do something, you quickly do it or quickly go somewhere.

words.ex: He obsesses over small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他 obsesses 于微小的错误。
words.en: If something or someone obsesses you, you think or worry about them all the time and you cannot think about anything else.

words.tr: n. 多余物；过剩品；多余
words.ex: The superfluity of clothes made her room messy.
words.ex_cn: 过多的衣服让她的房间乱糟糟的。
words.en: Superfluity refers to an unnecessarily large amount of something, more than is needed.

words.ex: The audience clapped loudly after the show.
words.ex_cn: 演出结束后，观众热烈鼓掌。
words.en: The group of spectators at a public event; listeners or viewers collectively, especially those attending a performance or reading a particular work.

words.ex: The stray dog wandered into the backyard.
words.ex_cn: 这只走失的狗走进了后院。
words.en: If someone or something strays, they wander away from where they are supposed to be.

words.ex: The farmer tried to exterminate the rats.
words.ex_cn: 农夫试图消灭老鼠。
words.en: To exterminate means to kill all the members of a group of people or animals, or to destroy something completely.

words.ex: The dimension of the box is 10 cm by 5 cm.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子的尺寸是10厘米乘5厘米。
words.en: A dimension is a measurement of something in a particular direction, or the scope or scale of something.

words.ex: The old computer is antiquated and slow.
words.ex_cn: 这台旧电脑过时且缓慢。
words.en: Something that is antiquated is old-fashioned or outdated and no longer suitable for modern conditions or purposes.

words.tr: v. 切断；脱离；切成两段
words.ex: He severed the rope with a knife.
words.ex_cn: 他用刀把绳子割断了。
words.en: To sever something means to cut through it or to break it off completely.

words.ex: The teacher gave us a questionnaire about our habits.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了我们一份关于我们习惯的问卷。
words.en: A questionnaire is a written list of questions which are answered by a lot of people in order to provide information for a report or a survey.

words.tr:
n. 鞭策；
v. 刺激；
words.ex: The competition served as a spur to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 竞争成了推动他更努力工作的鞭策。
words.en: A spur is something that makes you want to do something or that encourages you to do it. It can also refer to a sharp device worn on the heel of a rider's boot to urge a horse forward.

words.tr: adv. 强调地；断然地；显然地
words.ex: She emphatically denied the accusation.
words.ex_cn: 她坚决否认了这项指控。
words.en: In a forceful way that shows emphasis.

words.ex: He could not conceive a world without technology.
words.ex_cn: 他无法设想一个没有科技的世界。
words.en: To conceive means to form or devise a plan or idea in the mind; to become pregnant.

words.tr:
v. 喜欢；享受；从…获得乐趣
n. 享受；乐趣；调味品
words.ex: He relishes every bite of his favorite food.
words.ex_cn: 他享受着每一口他最喜欢的食物。
words.en: If you relish something, you enjoy it very much.

words.tr: adj. 悲惨的；不幸的；难过的；恶劣的
words.ex: He felt wretched after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到很悲惨。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as wretched, you mean that they are in a very bad or unfortunate situation.

words.tr:
n. 蔑视
v. 蔑视
words.ex: He looked at the lie with scorn.
words.ex_cn: 他轻蔑地看着这个谎言。
words.en: If you scorn someone or something, you feel or show contempt for them.

words.ex: He has a considerable amount of money.
words.ex_cn: 他有相当多的钱。
words.en: Considerable means large in size, amount, or extent.

words.ex: He took a remedial math course to improve his skills.
words.ex_cn: 他上了一门补救数学课程来提高自己的技能。
words.en: Remedial actions or activities are intended to correct something that is wrong or to improve a bad situation.

words.ex: The factory will mechanize its production line next year.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂明年将使生产线实现机械化。
words.en: To mechanize something means to change it so that it is done by machines or mechanical processes rather than by human labor.

words.ex: The mortuary was filled with the bodies of the victims.
words.ex_cn: 停尸房里堆满了受害者的尸体。
words.en: A mortuary is a building or a room in a hospital where dead bodies are kept before they are buried or cremated.

words.ex: The village by the lake is picturesque.
words.ex_cn: 湖边的村庄如画般美丽。
words.en: A picturesque place is attractive and interesting, especially in a way that is old-fashioned or unusual.

words.ex: It is feasible to finish the project in one week.
words.ex_cn: 一周内完成这个项目是可行的。
words.en: If something is feasible, it can be done, made, or achieved.

words.ex: The shepherd walks with his sheep every morning.
words.ex_cn: 牧羊人每天早上都带着他的羊走路。
words.en: A shepherd is a person whose job is to look after sheep. As a verb, it means to guide or direct someone or something in a particular direction.

words.ex: He is proficient in playing the piano.
words.ex_cn: 他弹钢琴很熟练。
words.en: If you are proficient in something, you can do it well because you have learned how to do it.

words.tr:
n. 审查员；检查员
v. 检查；审查
words.ex: The censor removed the bad words from the movie.
words.ex_cn: 审查员从电影中删除了粗俗用语。
words.en: A censor is a person who supervises conduct and morals: in particular, one who examines books, films, or other material for objectionable matter.

words.ex: His decisive action saved the team.
words.ex_cn: 他果断的行动拯救了团队。
words.en: If a fact, action, or event is decisive, it makes it certain that there will be a particular result.

words.tr:
n. 黑暗；忧郁；幽暗
v. 变阴暗；变忧郁
words.ex: The room was filled with gloom after the power went out.
words.ex_cn: 停电后，房间里一片黑暗。
words.en: Gloom is a feeling of sadness and lack of hope.

words.tr:
v. 蹲；蹲坐；擅自占住
n. 蹲；偷住的房子；蹲坐
adj. 矮而宽的；矮胖的
words.ex: He does a squat every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上做深蹲。
words.en: If you squat, you lower yourself towards the ground, balancing on your feet with your legs bent.

words.ex: He spoke in a hoarse voice after shouting all day.
words.ex_cn: 他喊了一整天后，声音变得沙哑。
words.en: If your voice is hoarse or if you are hoarse, your voice sounds rough and unclear, for example because your throat is sore.

words.ex: The car turned at the roundabout near the park.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在公园附近的环形交叉路口转弯。
words.en: A roundabout is a circular area at a place where several roads meet. You drive round it until you come to the road that you want.

words.ex: The monarch ruled the country for 50 years.
words.ex_cn: 这位君主统治这个国家长达50年。
words.en: A monarch is a king, queen, emperor, or empress.

words.ex: She sifts flour through a fine mesh.
words.ex_cn: 她用细网筛面粉。
words.en: To sift means to put a fine, loose, or powdery substance through a sieve so as to remove lumps or large particles. It can also mean to examine something thoroughly so as to isolate that which is most important or useful.

words.tr:
n. 信用；赊账；赞扬；贷款；荣誉；
v. 相信；
words.ex: He has good credit with the bank.
words.ex_cn: 他在银行有良好的信用。
words.en: If you are allowed credit, you are allowed to pay for goods or services several weeks or months after you have received them.

words.ex: Nike is a famous brand.
words.ex_cn: 耐克是一个著名品牌。
words.en: A brand is a name, term, design, symbol, or any other feature that identifies one seller's good or service as distinct from those of other sellers.

words.tr: n. 被排斥者；被抛弃者；
words.ex: He became an outcast after speaking the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他因为说出真相而被排斥。
words.en: An outcast is someone who is not accepted by a group of people or by society.

words.ex: The scientist studied genetic traits in plants.
words.ex_cn: 科学家研究了植物的基因特征。
words.en: relating to genes or heredity

words.ex: His outlook on life is very positive.
words.ex_cn: 他对生活的观点非常积极。
words.en: Your outlook is your general attitude towards life.

words.tr: adj. 刺鼻的；一语道破的
words.ex: The cheese has a pungent smell.
words.ex_cn: 这种奶酪有刺鼻的气味。
words.en: Having a sharply strong taste or smell.

words.ex: The government subsidize small businesses to help them grow.
words.ex_cn: 政府资助小企业以帮助它们发展。
words.en: To subsidize something means to pay part of the cost of it, usually as a way of helping people or organizations that cannot afford to pay the full cost themselves.

words.ex: His legacy includes many charity schools.
words.ex_cn: 他的遗产包括许多慈善学校。
words.en: Something handed down from an ancestor or a predecessor or from the past.

words.tr: n. 效用；实用；公用事业；
words.ex: The utility of this tool is very high.
words.ex_cn: 这个工具的效用非常高。
words.en: Utility refers to the state of being useful, profitable, or beneficial.

words.tr: adj. 有帮助的；乐器的；仪器的；
words.ex: Her advice was instrumental in helping me pass the exam.
words.ex_cn: 她的建议对帮助我通过考试很有帮助。
words.en: If someone or something is instrumental in a process, plan, or system, they are one of the most important influences in causing it to happen.

words.tr: adj. 人道的；仁慈的；人文的
words.ex: The shelter treats animals in a humane way.
words.ex_cn: 这个收容所以人道的方式对待动物。
words.en: If you describe something as humane, you mean that it is good and kind, especially because it decreases suffering.

words.tr: v. 解释；把…逐字译出；作句法分析
words.ex: He construes her silence as a yes.
words.ex_cn: 他把她的沉默理解为同意。
words.en: If you construe something in a particular way, you interpret it in that way.

words.ex: He has an insatiable hunger for knowledge.
words.ex_cn: 他对知识有着无法满足的渴望。
words.en: If someone is insatiable, they always want more of something and are never satisfied.

words.tr: v. 跛行；蹒跚；捆绑（马等的）两腿
words.ex: The old man hobbled along the street.
words.ex_cn: 那位老人一瘸一拐地走在街上。
words.en: If you hobble, you walk in an awkward way, usually because your feet or legs hurt.

words.ex: The teacher gave an explanatory note to help students.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个解释性的笔记来帮助学生。
words.en: Serving or intended to explain or make clear.

words.ex: The announcement caused an uproar in the town.
words.ex_cn: 这个公告在小镇上引起了轩然大波。
words.en: A loud and impassioned noise or disturbance.

words.tr: v. 吞食；吞噬；狼吞虎咽地吃；如饥似渴地看
words.ex: The dog devoured the meat quickly.
words.ex_cn: 狗很快地把肉吃光了。
words.en: To eat something quickly and eagerly, especially because you are very hungry; to destroy something quickly and completely.

words.tr: n. 权衡；折衷；（公平）交易（同 trade-off）
words.ex: There is a tradeoff between speed and accuracy.
words.ex_cn: 速度和准确性之间存在权衡。
words.en: A tradeoff is a situation where you must accept something you do not like or want in order to get something that you do like or want.

words.ex: His infirmity made it hard to walk.
words.ex_cn: 他的虚弱使他走路困难。
words.en: An infirmity is a physical or mental weakness.

words.ex: The old song is reminiscent of my childhood.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌让人想起我的童年。
words.en: If you say that one thing is reminiscent of another, you mean that it reminds you of it.

words.ex: The allure of money made him take the risky job.
words.ex_cn: 金钱的诱惑让他接受了这份高风险的工作。
words.en: The quality of being powerfully and mysteriously attractive or fascinating.

words.ex: The horse-drawn carriage was a forerunner of the car.
words.ex_cn: 马车是汽车的先驱。
words.en: A forerunner is someone or something that comes before another and is often considered as a sign of what is to follow.

words.tr: adj. 宽厚的；仁慈的；不严格的；
words.ex: The teacher was lenient with students who were late.
words.ex_cn: 老师对迟到的学生很宽厚。
words.en: If you are lenient with someone, you are not strict in the way you treat them, especially when they have done something wrong.

words.ex: The flowers will perish if you don't water them.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不给花浇水，它们会死。
words.en: If people or animals perish, they die as a result of very harsh conditions or as the result of an accident.

words.ex: He lingered by the door, not wanting to leave.
words.ex_cn: 他逗留在门口，不想离开。
words.en: If you linger somewhere, you stay there for a longer time than is necessary, for example because you are enjoying yourself.

words.ex: The problem recurs every week.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题每周都会再次出现。
words.en: If something recurs, it happens again, either once or several times.

words.ex: The candle's flicker lit up the dark room.
words.ex_cn: 蜡烛的闪现照亮了黑暗的房间。
words.en: If a light or flame flickers, it shines unsteadily.

words.ex: The machine can perforate the paper quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器可以快速地在纸上打孔。
words.en: To make a hole or holes through something, especially by piercing or drilling.

words.ex: I reckon it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我认为明天会下雨。
words.en: If you reckon that something is true, you think that it is true.

words.tr: adj. 卓越的；杰出的；罕见的；特别的；
words.ex: She is an exceptional student who always gets top grades.
words.ex_cn: 她是一名卓越的学生，总是取得最高分。
words.en: An exceptional person or thing has some unusual quality or ability that makes them different from others.

words.ex: He failed the test, but subsequent efforts helped him pass.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格，但随后的努力让他通过了。
words.en: Following in time or order; succeeding.

words.tr:
n. 谜语；费解的事
v. 解谜；出谜；使布满窟窿；打洞
words.ex: He told me a riddle and I solved it.
words.ex_cn: 他给我出了一道谜语，我解出来了。
words.en: A riddle is a question or statement that is deliberately very confusing and has a clever or amusing answer.

words.ex: He tries to procure food for his family.
words.ex_cn: 他努力为家人获取食物。
words.en: To obtain something, especially with care or effort.

words.ex: He adheres to his principles even when it's hard.
words.ex_cn: 即使很难，他仍然坚持自己的原则。
words.en: If you adhere to a rule or agreement, you act in the way that it says you should.

words.ex: She bought a new outfit for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对买了一套新衣服。
words.en: An outfit is a set of clothes worn together, especially for a particular occasion or purpose.

words.ex: His pride begets conflict.
words.ex_cn: 他的骄傲招致了冲突。
words.en: To beget means to cause something to happen or exist.

words.ex: He expressed dissent about the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 他对新规定提出了异议。
words.en: Dissent is strong disagreement or dissatisfaction with a decision or opinion, especially one that is supported by most people or by people in authority.

words.tr: v. 迅速生长；急速增长
words.ex: The flowers burgeon in spring.
words.ex_cn: 春天时，花朵绽放。
words.en: To grow or develop quickly; to flourish.

words.tr: v. 抢劫；掠夺；蹂躏；破坏
words.ex: The invaders despoiled the village.
words.ex_cn: 入侵者抢劫了村庄。
words.en: To despoil something means to steal from it or damage it, especially in a violent or destructive way.

words.ex: The accident looked horrendous.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故看起来很可怕。
words.en: If you describe something as horrendous, you are emphasizing that it is very unpleasant or shocking.

words.ex: She lamented the death of her dog.
words.ex_cn: 她哀悼她狗的去世。
words.en: If you lament something, you express your sadness, regret, or disappointment about it.

words.ex: Wear a helmet as a precaution when riding a bike.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔作为一种预防措施。
words.en: A precaution is an action that is intended to prevent something dangerous or unpleasant from happening.

words.ex: There is a large variance between the budget and the actual cost.
words.ex_cn: 预算与实际成本之间有很大的差额。
words.en: Variance refers to the fact or quality of being different, divergent, or inconsistent.

words.ex: The rocket's blast-off was spectacular.
words.ex_cn: 火箭的发射场面非常壮观。
words.en: The moment when a spacecraft or rocket leaves the ground.

words.tr: adj. 不乐意的；不情愿的；
words.ex: He is loath to apologize for his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他不乐意为自己的错误道歉。
words.en: If you are loath to do something, you do not want to do it.

words.ex: The law compels drivers to wear seat belts.
words.ex_cn: 法律强迫司机系安全带。
words.en: If a situation, a rule, or a person compels you to do something, they force you to do it.

words.ex: He interprets the poem as a love story.
words.ex_cn: 他把这首诗解释为一个爱情故事。
words.en: If you interpret something in a particular way, you decide that this is its meaning or significance.

words.tr: v. 兑现；递送；交付；发表；为…接生；
words.ex: He promised to deliver on his goal.
words.ex_cn: 他承诺要兑现自己的目标。
words.en: To bring and hand over (a letter, parcel, or ordered goods) to the proper recipient or address.

words.ex: He embeds the photo in the document.
words.ex_cn: 他把照片插入到文档中。
words.en: To fix something firmly and deeply in a surrounding mass.

words.ex: The rebel fought against the king's rules.
words.ex_cn: 这位叛逆者反抗国王的法令。
words.en: A rebel is a person who opposes or fights against people in authority.

words.tr: n. 偶然事故；意外事件
words.ex: He saved money for a contingency.
words.ex_cn: 他存钱以备不时之需。
words.en: A contingency is an event or situation that might happen in the future, especially one that could cause problems.

words.tr:
n. 库存；股票；家畜；
v. 备有；贮存；
words.ex: The store has low stock of winter coats.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店的冬衣库存很少。
words.en: The supply of goods available for sale in a store; the capital raised by a company through the issue of shares.

words.ex: He has a positive attitude toward life.
words.ex_cn: 他对生活持积极的态度。
words.en: If you are positive about things, you are hopeful and confident, and think of the good aspects of a situation rather than the bad ones.

words.ex: The witness corroborated his story with photos.
words.ex_cn: 证人用照片证实了他的说法。
words.en: To corroborate something that has been said or reported means to provide evidence or information that supports it.

words.ex: The blind man walks with a white cane.
words.ex_cn: 这位失明的男人用白色手杖走路。
words.en: Unable to see; lacking the sense of sight.

words.tr: v. 捐赠；订阅；订购；签署；认购（股份）
words.ex: He decided to subscribe $50 to the charity each month.
words.ex_cn: 他决定每月向慈善机构捐赠50美元。
words.en: If you subscribe to a magazine or a service, you pay to receive it regularly.

words.ex: He is a scientist of great renown.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位享有盛誉的科学家。
words.en: Renown is the state of being known and talked about by many people because of your achievements, qualities, or actions.

words.tr: n. 层次体系；等级制度；
words.ex: The company has a clear hierarchy from manager to worker.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司有一个从经理到员工的明确层次体系。
words.en: A hierarchy is a system in which people or things are arranged according to their importance.

words.ex: I cannot foresee what will happen tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我无法预知明天会发生什么。
words.en: If you foresee something, you expect and believe that it will happen.

words.ex: Children learn self-regulatory skills to control their emotions.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们学习自我调节技能来控制自己的情绪。
words.en: A self-regulatory system, organization, or activity is one that controls itself, rather than having an outside organization or law control it.

words.ex: The sponge is porous and absorbs water easily.
words.ex_cn: 海绵是多孔的，容易吸水。
words.en: If something is porous, it has a lot of tiny holes in it that allow water or air to pass through slowly.

words.ex: The fishing vessel sailed out at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 那艘渔船在黎明时出海。
words.en: A vessel is a large boat or a container for holding liquids.

words.tr:
n. 微粒；斑点；少量
v. 使有斑点
words.ex: There is a speck of dust on the table.
words.ex_cn: 桌子上有一粒灰尘。
words.en: A speck is a very small stain, mark, or container of something.

words.ex: Her infatuation with the movie star lasted only a few weeks.
words.ex_cn: 她对那位电影明星的迷恋只持续了几个星期。
words.en: An infatuation is an intense but short-lived passion or admiration for someone or something.

words.tr:
n. 熊；
v. 承受；忍受；带有；生（孩子）；
words.ex: A bear walked near the campsite.
words.ex_cn: 一只熊在露营地附近走动。
words.en: If you bear something, you accept it and are able to deal with it, even though it is unpleasant or painful. A bear is a large, strong wild animal with thick fur and sharp claws.

words.tr: adj. 不能生育的；贫瘠的；
words.ex: The doctor said the man is sterile.
words.ex_cn: 医生说这个人不能生育。
words.en: Something that is sterile is completely clean and free from bacteria or other microorganisms.

words.tr:
adj. 文盲的；无知的；
n. 文盲；无知识的人；
words.ex: He is illiterate and cannot read simple signs.
words.ex_cn: 他是文盲，无法阅读简单的标识。
words.en: Someone who is illiterate cannot read or write.

words.ex: The doctor checked his pulse with his fingers.
words.ex_cn: 医生用手指检查了他的脉搏。
words.en: A pulse is the regular beating of the heart, especially when it is felt at the wrist or neck. It can also refer to a single vibration or short burst of sound, electric current, light, etc.

words.ex: The judge made an equitable decision.
words.ex_cn: 法官做出了一个公平的决定。
words.en: Fair and impartial; treating everyone equally.

words.ex: The pink hat on the man looked like an incongruity.
words.ex_cn: 男人头上的粉红色帽子显得很不协调。
words.en: The state of being incongruous; incompatibility.

words.tr: n. 对手；对立者；对抗者
words.ex: The antagonist in the story is a greedy king.
words.ex_cn: 故事中的反派是一个贪婪的国王。
words.en: An antagonist is someone who opposes another person.

words.tr:
n. 弹跳；跳动；
v. 弹跳；反弹；
words.ex: The ball had a high bounce on the concrete.
words.ex_cn: 球在混凝土上弹跳得很高。
words.en: If something bounces or if you bounce it, it moves away from a surface after hitting it.

words.ex: He turned his head to avert the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他转过头去避免了事故。
words.en: If you avert something unpleasant, you prevent it from happening.

words.ex: The sunset over the mountains was magnificent.
words.ex_cn: 山上的日落壮丽极了。
words.en: If you say that something or someone is magnificent, you mean that you think they are extremely good, beautiful, or impressive.

words.ex: The team comprises five players and one coach.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队包括五名球员和一名教练。
words.en: If you say that something comprises or is comprised of a number of things or people, you mean it has them as its parts or members.

words.tr: v. 使全神贯注；独占；垄断
words.ex: He is engrossed in reading a novel.
words.ex_cn: 他正全神贯注地读一本小说。
words.en: If something engrosses you, it interests you so much that you do not notice anything else.

words.ex: The fence shows the demarcation between the two yards.
words.ex_cn: 这道篱笆标明了两个院子的界限。
words.en: The act or process of marking the limits or boundaries of something.

words.ex: The local company is an affiliate of the big global brand.
words.ex_cn: 这家本地公司是这个全球大品牌的分公司。
words.en: If an organization is affiliated with another larger organization, it is officially connected with the larger organization or is a member of it.

words.ex: He tried to counterfeit money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图伪造货币。
words.en: Made in exact imitation of something valuable with the intention to deceive or defraud.

words.ex: The teacher believed that every child was educable.
words.ex_cn: 老师相信每个孩子都是可教育的。
words.en: Capable of being educated or trained.

words.ex: He spoke with certitude about the answer.
words.ex_cn: 他对于这个答案说话时充满确信。
words.en: A feeling of being certain or convinced about something.

words.tr:
v. 发牢骚；抱怨；轰鸣
n. 怨言；牢骚；轰隆声
words.ex: He grumbles when he has to wake up early.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不早起时就会抱怨。
words.en: If someone grumbles, they complain about something in a bad-tempered way.

words.ex: The red team played versus the blue team.
words.ex_cn: 红队与蓝队比赛。
words.en: Used to indicate the two sides in a competition or conflict.

words.tr:
adv. 纵长地；纵向地
adj. 纵长的；纵向的
words.ex: Cut the bread lengthwise.
words.ex_cn: 沿着长度方向切面包。
words.en: In the direction of the length of something.

words.ex: He posits that the earth is round.
words.ex_cn: 他提出地球是圆的。
words.en: To posit something is to suggest it as a basic fact or principle from which a further idea is formed or developed.

words.tr:
adj. 崇高的；壮丽的；极端的；过分的
v. 变高尚；升华
n. 庄严；崇高；顶点
words.ex: The view from the mountain is sublime.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色是壮丽的。
words.en: If you describe something as sublime, you mean that it has a wonderful quality that affects you deeply.

words.ex: He felt awkward when he forgot his friend's name.
words.ex_cn: 当他忘记朋友的名字时，他感到很尴尬。
words.en: If you describe a situation as awkward, you mean that it is embarrassing or difficult to deal with.

words.ex: The soldiers raided the enemy camp at night.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在夜间突袭了敌人的营地。
words.en: A raid is a sudden attack on a place by soldiers, police, or other officials, in order to search for something or to arrest someone.

words.ex: The water will solidify when it gets very cold.
words.ex_cn: 水在非常冷的时候会变凝固。
words.en: If something solidifies or is solidified, it becomes solid or hard.

words.tr: v. 自夸；夸耀；自豪地拥有
words.ex: He boasts about his new car.
words.ex_cn: 他夸耀自己的新车。
words.en: If someone boasts about something that they have done or that they own, they talk about it very proudly, in a way that other people may find irritating or offensive.

words.ex: The movie was tame and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影枯燥无味。
words.en: If you describe an animal as tame, you mean that it is not afraid of humans and is not dangerous. If you describe a person or their behavior as tame, you mean that they are not very exciting or interesting.

words.ex: The price of oil soared last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月石油价格骤升。
words.en: To rise or increase dramatically in amount or level.

words.ex: He assists his brother with homework.
words.ex_cn: 他帮助弟弟做作业。
words.en: If you assist someone, you help them to do a job or task by doing part of the work for them.

words.ex: He tried to mollify his angry friend with an apology.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用道歉来安抚他生气的朋友。
words.en: To mollify someone means to make them feel calmer and less angry, upset, or worried.

words.ex: The soil shows clear stratification in layers.
words.ex_cn: 土壤呈现出明显的分层。
words.en: The process or state of being divided into strata or layers, especially in society or geology.

words.tr: adj. 最低限度的；极少的；最小的；
words.ex: He made minimal changes to the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他对计划做了最低限度的修改。
words.en: Something that is minimal is very small in quantity, value, or degree.

words.tr:
n. 厄运；毁灭；死亡
v. 注定；判决
words.ex: The old prophecy spoke of doom for the kingdom.
words.ex_cn: 古老的预言说这个王国将遭遇厄运。
words.en: Doom is a terrible fate or destiny that you cannot avoid, especially death or destruction.

words.tr: adj. 自发的；自然产生的；
words.ex: The children gave a spontaneous cheer.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们自发地欢呼起来。
words.en: Something that is spontaneous is not planned but happens or is done because of a sudden impulse or natural feeling.

words.tr:
n. （军队的）团；大群；大量
v. 把...编组；严格管制
words.ex: He joined the army and was in a regiment.
words.ex_cn: 他参军了，被编入一个团。
words.en: A regiment is a large group of soldiers that is commanded by a colonel.

words.tr: adj. 重大的；重要的；影响明显的；
words.ex: This discovery is a significant step forward.
words.ex_cn: 这一发现是一个重大的进步。
words.en: Something that is significant is important or large enough to be noticed or to have an effect.

words.ex: He did not avail himself of the opportunity.
words.ex_cn: 他没有利用这个机会。
words.en: If you avail yourself of something, you use it or take advantage of it.

words.ex: The ground began to subside after the heavy rain.
words.ex_cn: 大雨之后，地面开始下陷。
words.en: If a feeling or noise subsides, it becomes less strong or loud.

words.tr:
adj. 总的；全面的；总体的；
adv. 总计；大致上；
words.ex: The overall cost is too high.
words.ex_cn: 总成本太高了。
words.en: You use overall to indicate that you are talking about a situation in general or about the whole of something.

words.tr:
adj. 辐射状的；放射式的；径向的；星形的
n. 子午线轮胎；辐射式轮胎
words.ex: The wheels have radial tires.
words.ex_cn: 这些车轮装有径向轮胎。
words.en: Relating to or situated near the radius or the radial side of the forearm or hand.

words.ex: He lost all his property in the fire.
words.ex_cn: 他在火灾中失去了所有财产。
words.en: Something owned; a possession.

words.tr:
adj. 首要的；大红色的
n. 红衣主教；枢机主教；基数
words.ex: This is a cardinal rule in our school.
words.ex_cn: 这是我们学校的一项首要规则。
words.en: A cardinal rule or quality is the most important one.

words.tr: v. 举例说明；例证；例示
words.ex: This example exemplifies the rule clearly.
words.ex_cn: 这个例子清楚地说明了这条规则。
words.en: To exemplify means to be a typical example of something or to give an example of something.

words.ex: She blends flour and water to make dough.
words.ex_cn: 她把面粉和水混合在一起做面团。
words.en: To mix substances together so that they combine into a single substance.

words.ex: He is an emigrant from China.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名来自中国的移民。
words.en: An emigrant is a person who leaves their own country to live permanently in another country.

words.ex: He lost his job, which was a great misfortune.
words.ex_cn: 他丢了工作，这是一场巨大的不幸。
words.en: An unfortunate condition or event.

words.ex: He submitted his application for the job last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周提交了那份工作申请。
words.en: An application is a formal request, often written, for something such as a job, a place at a university, or permission to do something. It can also refer to the act of putting something to a special use or purpose, or a program or piece of software designed to perform a specific function.

words.tr: adj. 每年落叶的；定期脱落的；非永久性的
words.ex: The trees lose their leaves in autumn because they are deciduous.
words.ex_cn: 这些树在秋天落叶，因为它们是落叶的。
words.en: Deciduous trees or plants lose their leaves in autumn or the dry season.

words.ex: He exaggerates his achievements to impress others.
words.ex_cn: 他夸张自己的成就来给别人留下印象。
words.en: If you exaggerate, you indicate that something is, for example, worse or more important than it really is.

words.tr:
v. 倒带；重绕
n. 倒带；重绕
words.ex: He wants to rewind the video to see the part again.
words.ex_cn: 他想倒带视频再看一遍那一部分。
words.en: To wind back a tape or film to an earlier point.

words.ex: The courageous firefighter saved the child from the burning house.
words.ex_cn: 这位勇敢的消防员从着火的房子里救出了孩子。
words.en: Someone who is courageous shows courage.

words.ex: Rabbits proliferate quickly in the wild.
words.ex_cn: 兔子在野外繁殖得很快。
words.en: If something proliferates, it increases in number or spreads quickly.

words.ex: People vote in democracy to choose their leaders.
words.ex_cn: 人们在民主制度下投票选择他们的领导人。
words.en: A system of government by the whole population or all the eligible members of a state, typically through elected representatives.

words.tr: v. 使屈辱；使丢脸；使蒙羞
words.ex: He tried to humiliate her in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在全班面前羞辱她。
words.en: To humiliate someone means to make them feel ashamed or stupid, especially in front of other people.

words.tr:
n. 枢；中心；旋转
v. 在枢轴上转动；以…为中心
words.ex: The door pivots on a hinge.
words.ex_cn: 门围绕一个铰链旋转。
words.en: A pivot is the central point, pin, or shaft on which a mechanism turns or oscillates. It can also refer to the central or most important person or thing in a situation.

words.tr: v. 要求归还；收回；开垦；感化
words.ex: He wants to reclaim his lost wallet.
words.ex_cn: 他想要要求归还他丢失的钱包。
words.en: If you reclaim something that you have lost or that has been taken away from you, you succeed in getting it back. If you reclaim land, you make it suitable for use, for example by draining it or by getting rid of unwanted buildings or plants.

words.tr:
n. 巡逻
v. 巡逻
words.ex: The police patrol the street at night.
words.ex_cn: 警察晚上在街上巡逻。
words.en: A patrol is a group of soldiers or vehicles that are guarding a place at a particular time. Patrol can also refer to the act of moving around an area or building at regular times to check that it is safe.

words.tr: n. 废水；污物；水流 adj. 流出的
words.ex: The factory releases effluent into the river.
words.ex_cn: 工厂将废水排入河中。
words.en: Effluent is liquid waste material that comes out of factories or sewage works.

words.ex: He will surrender when he sees the police.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到警察时，他会投降。
words.en: If you surrender, you stop fighting or resisting someone and agree that you have been beaten.

words.ex: Hitherto, no one has solved the problem.
words.ex_cn: 迄今为止，没有人解决过这个问题。
words.en: Until now or until the point in time under discussion.

words.ex: Exercise can reinforce your muscles.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以增强你的肌肉。
words.en: To reinforce something means to make it stronger or more effective.

words.ex: His answer was vague and hard to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答不明确，难以理解。
words.en: If something written or spoken is vague, it does not explain or express things clearly.

words.tr: adj. 不切实际的；不实用的；
words.ex: It's impractical to walk to work every day if you live 50 kilometers away.
words.ex_cn: 如果你住得离工作地点50公里远，每天步行上班是不切实际的。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as impractical, you mean that they are not good at planning or organizing things in a practical way, or that their ideas or methods are not suitable for a particular situation.

words.tr: adj. 充满大事的；多事故的；多变故的
words.ex: It was an eventful day with many surprises.
words.ex_cn: 那是充满惊喜的一天。
words.en: If you describe a period of time as eventful, you mean that a lot of interesting, exciting, or important things have happened during it.

words.ex: The weather is unpredictable today.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天气不可预测。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as unpredictable, you mean that you cannot tell what they are going to do or how they are going to behave.

words.ex: The city improved its drainage system after the flood.
words.ex_cn: 洪水之后，这座城市改进了它的排水系统。
words.en: Drainage is the system or process by which water or other liquids are drained from a place.

words.tr: adj. 敏锐的；急性的；严重的；
words.ex: He has an acute mind and solves problems quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他思维敏锐，能快速解决问题。
words.en: An acute problem or negative feeling is very severe.

words.ex: The climate is hospitable for growing oranges.
words.ex_cn: 这种气候适合种植橙子。
words.en: If someone is hospitable, they are friendly, welcoming, and generous to guests or strangers.

words.ex: This is a good example of teamwork.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个团队合作的好例子。
words.en: An example is a particular instance of something that is representative of a group or used to illustrate a point.

words.ex: The car exceeded the speed limit.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车超过了限速。
words.en: To be greater in quantity, degree, or intensity than something else.

words.ex: The team's cohesion helped them win the match.
words.ex_cn: 团队的凝聚力帮助他们赢得了比赛。
words.en: Cohesion refers to the action or fact of forming a united whole, especially in the context of a group of people or the parts of a substance.

words.ex: The child has malnutrition from not eating enough food.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子因为吃不够饭而营养不良。
words.en: Malnutrition is a condition that results from eating a diet in which certain nutrients are lacking, in excess (too high in intake), or in the wrong proportions.

words.ex: The climbers found a foothold on the rocky wall.
words.ex_cn: 登山者在岩壁上找到了一个立足点。
words.en: A foothold is a secure position from which further progress or development may be made.

words.tr:
v. 沉思
n. （作家、画家等的）灵感；缪斯
words.ex: He often muses about the meaning of life.
words.ex_cn: 他常常沉思生命的意义。
words.en: In Greek mythology, the Muses are the goddesses of the inspiration of literature, science and the arts. As a verb, to muse means to think about something carefully and for a long time.

words.ex: We decorate the room for the party.
words.ex_cn: 我们为派对装饰房间。
words.en: To make something look more attractive by putting things on it or around it.

words.tr: n. 年代学；年表；按年代次序的排列
words.ex: He wrote the chronology of ancient Rome.
words.ex_cn: 他写了古罗马的年代顺序。
words.en: Chronology is the arrangement of events or dates in the order of their occurrence.

words.tr: adj. 难以理解的；难懂的
words.ex: The handwriting was unintelligible.
words.ex_cn: 字迹无法辨认。
words.en: If speech or writing is unintelligible, it is impossible to understand.

words.ex: He made a digression to tell a funny story.
words.ex_cn: 他岔开话题讲了个有趣的故事。
words.en: A digression is a temporary departure from the main subject in speech or writing.

words.tr: v. 买得起；担负得起；有时间做；
words.ex: I can't afford a new car.
words.ex_cn: 我买不起一辆新车。
words.en: If you cannot afford something, you do not have enough money to pay for it.

words.ex: The two events were contemporaneous and could be connected.
words.ex_cn: 这两件事是同时发生的，可能有关联。
words.en: Existing or occurring in the same period of time.

words.tr: adj. 暂时的；临时的；期间的；
words.ex: He is the interim manager until a new one is hired.
words.ex_cn: 在招聘到新的经理之前，他是临时经理。
words.en: An interim is a period of time between one event, process, or period and another, especially one of temporary nature.

words.ex: You must abide by the rules.
words.ex_cn: 你必须遵守规则。
words.en: If you can't abide someone or something, you dislike them very much.

words.ex: The refugee walked to a new country.
words.ex_cn: 这名难民步行去了一个新国家。
words.en: A refugee is a person who has been forced to leave their country in order to escape war, persecution, or natural disaster.

words.ex: His rude words provoked her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话激怒了她。
words.en: If you provoke someone, you deliberately annoy them and try to make them behave aggressively.

words.tr: adj. 肥沃的；有繁殖力的；多产的；富饶的；
words.ex: The fertile land grows many crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片肥沃的土地长满了各种作物。
words.en: Land or soil that is fertile is able to support the growth of a large number of strong healthy plants.

words.ex: He has an inclination to help others.
words.ex_cn: 他有帮助他人的倾向。
words.en: An inclination is a feeling that makes you want to act in a particular way, or a tendency to do something.

words.tr: v. 逐渐削弱；暗中损害；
words.ex: Constant criticism can undermine your confidence.
words.ex_cn: 不断的批评会逐渐削弱你的信心。
words.en: To undermine something means to weaken it or make it less effective, often in a gradual or sneaky way.

words.ex: I appreciate the beauty of nature.
words.ex_cn: 我欣赏大自然的美。
words.en: If you appreciate something, you recognize its value and feel grateful for it.

words.tr: v. 开创；为（某人）举行就职典礼；为…举行开幕仪式
words.ex: The president will inaugurate the new hospital next week.
words.ex_cn: 总统将于下周为新医院举行揭幕仪式。
words.en: If you inaugurate a new system, service, or project, you start it or introduce it officially.

words.ex: We celebrate my birthday with cake and friends.
words.ex_cn: 我们用蛋糕和朋友庆祝我的生日。
words.en: To celebrate means to mark a special day, event, or occasion with festivities or ceremonies. It can also mean to praise or honor someone or something.

words.ex: He works in a technical department.
words.ex_cn: 他在一个技术部门工作。
words.en: Technical means involving the sorts of machines, processes, and materials that are used in industry, transport, and communications.

words.ex: Children develop cognition as they learn to understand the world.
words.ex_cn: 儿童在学习理解世界时发展认知能力。
words.en: Cognition is the mental action or process of acquiring knowledge and understanding through thought, experience, and the senses.

words.ex: The company will reinstate his job next month.
words.ex_cn: 公司下个月将恢复他的工作。
words.en: If you reinstate someone, you give them back a job or position which had been taken away from them.

words.ex: The loud noise stunned him.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让他震惊了。
words.en: To stun someone means to shock or surprise them very much.

words.ex: He acquired a new skill last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年获得了一项新技能。
words.en: If you acquire something, you buy or obtain it for yourself, or someone gives it to you.

words.ex: He is a sociable man who likes to talk with friends.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢和朋友聊天的外向的人。
words.en: A sociable person is friendly and enjoys being with other people.

words.ex: The needle will pierce the skin.
words.ex_cn: 针会刺穿皮肤。
words.en: If a sharp object pierces something, or if you pierce something with a sharp object, the object goes into it and makes a hole in it.

words.ex: The crowd applauded after the performance.
words.ex_cn: 演出结束后，观众鼓掌了。
words.en: To applaud means to show approval or praise by clapping the hands.

words.tr: v. 接着发生；因而产生
words.ex: The storm ended, and peace ensued.
words.ex_cn: 风暴结束后，和平随之而来。
words.en: If something ensues, it happens immediately after another event, usually as a result of it.

words.ex: He likes to ramble about his travels.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢漫谈他的旅行经历。
words.en: To walk for pleasure, especially in the countryside, without a definite route or destination.

words.tr:
v. 进行无记名投票 
n. 无记名投票
words.ex: He cast his ballot in the election.
words.ex_cn: 他在选举中投了票。
words.en: A ballot is a process of voting, in writing and typically in secret. It is also the piece of paper on which you mark your vote.

words.ex: He made a painstaking effort to fix the small details.
words.ex_cn: 他细心地努力修正每一个小细节。
words.en: If you describe someone's work as painstaking, you mean that they do it very carefully and thoroughly, often taking a long time.

words.ex: Water is made of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom in a molecule.
words.ex_cn: 水由两个氢原子和一个氧原子组成一个分子。
words.en: A molecule is the smallest particle in a chemical element or compound that has the chemical properties of that element or compound. Molecules are made up of atoms that are held together by chemical bonds.

words.ex: Rivers carry sediment to the sea.
words.ex_cn: 河流把沉积物带到大海。
words.en: Material that settles to the bottom of a liquid; matter that has been deposited by some natural process.

words.ex: The weather will deteriorate tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天天气会恶化。
words.en: If something deteriorates, it becomes worse in some way.

words.tr:
n. 合同；契约；
v. 收缩；
words.ex: They signed a contract to buy the house.
words.ex_cn: 他们签署了一份购买房子的合同。
words.en: A contract is a legal agreement between two or more parties. It can also mean to become smaller or tighter, or to catch a disease.

words.ex: He imparts knowledge to his students every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天向学生传授知识。
words.en: If you impart information to people, you tell it to them. To impart a particular quality to something means to give it that quality.

words.tr:
n. 相反；
adj. 相反的；
words.ex: The contrary of hot is cold.
words.ex_cn: 热的相反是冷。
words.en: If you say that something is true contrary to other people's beliefs or opinions, you are emphasizing that it is true and that they are wrong.

words.ex: He reverted to his old habits after the holiday.
words.ex_cn: 假期后，他恢复了旧习惯。
words.en: To return to a former state, practice, topic, etc.

words.tr:
n. 责任；责备；
v. 责怪；归咎于；
words.ex: He took the blame for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他承担了这个错误的责任。
words.en: If you blame a person or thing for something bad, you believe or say that they are responsible for it or that they caused it.

words.ex: The company will advertise its new phone on TV.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司将在电视上为新手机登广告。
words.en: If you advertise something such as a product, an event, or a job, you tell people about it in newspapers, on television, or on posters in order to encourage them to buy the product, go to the event, or apply for the job.

words.ex: Don't bother to clean the room, I'll do it later.
words.ex_cn: 别麻烦去打扫房间了，我稍后会做。
words.en: To bother someone means to cause them trouble or to annoy them.

words.tr:
v. 打滑；侧滑
n. 打滑；侧滑
words.ex: The car skid on the wet road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在湿滑的路面上打滑了。
words.en: If a vehicle skids, it slides sideways or forwards while moving, usually because of bad weather conditions or because the driver is going too fast.

words.ex: The puppy frisks around the garden.
words.ex_cn: 小狗在花园里活蹦乱跳。
words.en: To frisk someone means to search them for weapons or illegal items by feeling their body with your hands.

words.ex: He squeezed into the small seat.
words.ex_cn: 他挤进了小座位里。
words.en: To squeeze something means to press it firmly, usually with your fingers or hands, often to get liquid out of it or to make it smaller.

words.tr: n. 性格；人物角色；特点；
words.ex: His character is kind and patient.
words.ex_cn: 他的性格善良且有耐心。
words.en: The combination of qualities or features that distinguishes one person, group, or thing from another.

words.tr: adj. 全神贯注的；专心致志的
words.ex: The children were rapt during the story.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们全神贯注地听故事。
words.en: If someone is rapt, they are so interested in or fascinated by what they are seeing or hearing that they do not pay attention to anything else.

words.tr: n. 影响；方位；轴承；举止； v. 忍受；“bear”的现在分词；
words.ex: The new policy has a big bearing on our daily lives.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策对我们日常生活有很大影响。
words.en: The manner in which one conducts or carries oneself, including posture and gestures; also refers to a machine part that supports another part and reduces friction.

words.tr:
adj. 平行的；
n. 类似的事物；
words.ex: The two lines are parallel and never meet.
words.ex_cn: 这两条线是平行的，永远不会相交。
words.en: Something that is parallel to something else is similar to it in many ways, or happens at the same time as it.

words.ex: The depredation of forests harms wildlife.
words.ex_cn: 森林的破坏危害了野生动物。
words.en: The act of preying upon or plundering; the act of laying waste; as, the depredations of an army on the country.

words.tr:
n. 茎；柄；梗
v. 跟踪；偷偷接近；昂首阔步地走
words.ex: The stalk of the sunflower is very tall.
words.ex_cn: 向日葵的茎很高。
words.en: The main stem of a plant, typically rising above ground but occasionally subterranean. Also, to pursue or approach stealthily.

words.tr:
n. 最大限度；最大量；
adj. 最大极限的；最多的；
words.ex: The maximum of the crowd is 100 people.
words.ex_cn: 人群的上限是100人。
words.en: The greatest or highest amount possible or attained.

words.ex: The old woman predict rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 那位老妇人预言明天会下雨。
words.en: If you predict an event, you say that it will happen.

words.tr:
v. 诋毁；诽谤；中伤
n. 诋毁；诽谤；中伤
words.ex: He spread slander about his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他散布了关于他邻居的诽谤。
words.en: Slander is the action or crime of making a false spoken statement damaging to a person's reputation.

words.tr:
v. 辩论；争论
n. 辩论；争论
words.ex: The students had a debate about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学生们就作业进行了一场辩论。
words.en: A debate is a discussion about a subject on which people have different views.

words.ex: He wrote copious notes during the lecture.
words.ex_cn: 他在讲座期间写了大量的笔记。
words.en: Something that is copious exists in large amounts.

words.ex: The factory pollutes the river.
words.ex_cn: 工厂污染了这条河。
words.en: To pollute water, air, or land means to make it dirty and dangerous to live in or to use, especially with poisonous chemicals or waste.

words.tr: adj. 荒唐的；荒唐可笑的；
words.ex: It's absurd to wear a coat in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天穿外套是荒唐的。
words.en: If you say that something is absurd, you are criticizing it because you think that it is ridiculous or that it does not make sense.

words.ex: He is downright lazy.
words.ex_cn: 他完全懒惰。
words.en: You use downright to emphasize that something is completely the case, especially when you are describing something bad or negative.

words.ex: The relocation of the factory caused many job changes.
words.ex_cn: 工厂的迁移导致了许多工作变动。
words.en: The act of moving to a new place and establishing one's home or business there.

words.ex: He hesitates to ask for help.
words.ex_cn: 他犹豫着是否要寻求帮助。
words.en: If you hesitate, you pause slightly while you are doing something or just before you do it, usually because you are uncertain, embarrassed, or worried.

words.ex: The temple is a divine place.
words.ex_cn: 这座寺庙是神的圣地。
words.en: Something that is divine relates to a god or goddess.

words.ex: I can't recollect where I put my keys.
words.ex_cn: 我想不起来把钥匙放在哪儿了。
words.en: If you recollect something, you remember it.

words.ex: He idealizes his father as a perfect hero.
words.ex_cn: 他把父亲理想化为一个完美的英雄。
words.en: To regard or represent as perfect or more nearly perfect than is true.

words.ex: The bridge has a stone arch.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥有一个石拱。
words.en: An arch is a structure that is curved at the top and is usually made of stone or brick. Arches are often used to support the weight of a bridge or the roof of a building.

words.tr: n. 种族主义；种族歧视；
words.ex: Racism is wrong and hurts many people.
words.ex_cn: 种族主义是错误的，会伤害很多人。
words.en: Racism is the belief that people of some races are inferior to others, often resulting in unfair treatment of people based on their race.

words.ex: The car had a malfunction in the engine.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的发动机出现了故障。
words.en: If a machine or device malfunctions, it fails to work properly.

words.tr:
adj. 忠实的；坚定的
v. 止住（血等的）流出
words.ex: He is a staunch supporter of environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的坚定支持者。
words.en: A staunch person is someone who is very loyal and firm in their beliefs or support for someone or something.

words.ex: He inserts a coin into the machine.
words.ex_cn: 他把一枚硬币放进机器里。
words.en: To put or introduce something into something else.

words.tr: adj. 一致的；始终如一的；
words.ex: His answers are consistent with the data.
words.ex_cn: 他的答案与数据一致。
words.en: Someone who is consistent always behaves in the same way, has the same attitudes towards people or things, or achieves the same level of success in something.

words.ex: Interest will accrue over time.
words.ex_cn: 利息会随着时间积累。
words.en: If money or interest accrues, it gradually increases in amount over a period of time.

words.ex: The letter 'b' is a consonant.
words.ex_cn: 字母 'b' 是一个辅音。
words.en: A consonant is a speech sound that is articulated with complete or partial closure of the vocal tract.

words.tr: n. 海盗行为；侵犯版权；
words.ex: The ship was attacked because of piracy near the coast.
words.ex_cn: 船在海岸附近因海盗行为遭到袭击。
words.en: The act of illegally copying and selling someone else's work, especially books, videos, or computer programs, or the act of attacking and stealing from ships at sea.

words.ex: He is bellicose when he drinks too much.
words.ex_cn: 他喝多了时就好战。
words.en: Having or showing a tendency to argue or fight.

words.ex: He is learning elementary math at school.
words.ex_cn: 他在学校学习初级数学。
words.en: Elementary means relating to the simplest and most basic aspects of a subject.

words.ex: He postdated the check to next month.
words.ex_cn: 他把支票的日期写成下个月。
words.en: To write a date on a document that is later than the actual date.

words.ex: The workers used a hoist to lift the heavy beams.
words.ex_cn: 工人们用吊升机械吊起沉重的梁。
words.en: To hoist something means to lift or pull it up to a higher position, usually using some kind of equipment such as a crane or pulley.

words.ex: The two events happened simultaneously.
words.ex_cn: 这两个事件同时发生了。
words.en: Happening, existing, or done at the same time.
