words.en: If you describe someone as insular, you are being critical of them because they are unwilling to meet new people or to consider new ideas.

words.ex: He takes insulin to control his blood sugar.
words.ex_cn: 他注射胰岛素来控制血糖。
words.en: A hormone produced in the pancreas by the islets of Langerhans, which regulates the amount of glucose in the blood. The lack of insulin causes a form of diabetes.

words.ex: The intercellular signals help cells talk to each other.
words.ex_cn: 细胞间的信号帮助细胞相互交流。
words.en: Located or occurring between cells.

words.ex: The phone has a simple interface.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机有一个简单的界面。
words.en: An interface is a point where two systems, subjects, organizations, etc. meet and interact.

words.tr: adj. 不同宗教信仰者（间）的；不同宗教团体（间）的
words.ex: There was a significant interfaith dialogue at the conference.
words.ex_cn: 会议上进行了重要的跨宗教对话。
words.en: Involving persons of different religious faiths.

words.ex: The doctor gave him interferon to fight the virus.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他注射了干扰素来对抗病毒。
words.en: A protein released by animal cells, usually in response to the entry of a virus, which has the property of inhibiting virus replication.

words.ex: The threads of the tapestry are intricately interlace.
words.ex_cn: 挂毯的线错综复杂地交织在一起。
words.en: If things interlace or are interlaced, they are joined together by being crossed over each other.

words.tr:
n. 隔行；交织
v. （使）交织；（使）交错；“interlace”的现在分词
words.ex: The technique of interlacing is commonly used in video compression.
words.ex_cn: 隔行扫描技术常用于视频压缩。
words.en: The act of weaving together or intertwining.

words.ex: The interlocking device ensures the safety of the railway system.
words.ex_cn: 联锁装置确保了铁路系统的安全。
words.en: A device that prevents two or more parts of a machine from moving or operating at the same time unless certain conditions are met.

words.tr: n. 间歇；暂停；中间休息
words.ex: There is a ten-minute intermission during the play.
words.ex_cn: 这场戏中间有十分钟的中场休息。
words.en: An intermission is a short break between parts of a play, film, concert, or other performance.

words.tr: adj. 断断续续的；间歇的
words.ex: The rain is intermittent today.
words.ex_cn: 今天雨断断续续地下。
words.en: Something that is intermittent happens occasionally rather than continuously.

words.tr:
v. 做实习生；扣留
n. 实习生
words.ex: He is interning at a hospital this summer.
words.ex_cn: 他今年夏天在医院做实习生。
words.en: An intern is someone who works in a temporary position with an emphasis on on-the-job training rather than merely employment, often to gain experience in a particular field.

words.ex: He did an internship at a hospital last summer.
words.ex_cn: 去年夏天，他在一家医院实习。
words.en: An internship is a period of work experience offered by an organization for a limited period of time. It is typically undertaken by students and graduates looking to gain relevant skills and experience in a particular field.

words.tr:
adj. 疑问的；质问的
n. 疑问句；疑问词；疑问结构
words.ex: He asked an interrogative sentence to check her understanding.
words.ex_cn: 他问了一个疑问句来检查她的理解。
words.en: An interrogative word or sentence is used to ask a question.

words.ex: The spaceship travels through interstellar space.
words.ex_cn: 宇宙飞船在星际空间中航行。
words.en: Existing or occurring between stars.

words.ex: The intestine helps digest food.
words.ex_cn: 肠道帮助消化食物。
words.en: The part of the alimentary canal between the stomach and the anus.

words.ex: His intonation made the sentence sound friendly.
words.ex_cn: 他的语调让这句话听起来很友好。
words.en: Intonation is the way the voice rises and falls in speech, especially the pitch pattern in a sentence.

words.ex: He was arrested for intoxication after drinking too much.
words.ex_cn: 他因饮酒过量而被逮捕。
words.en: The state of being intoxicated, especially by alcohol or drugs.

words.ex: The medication was administered via an intramuscular injection.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物是通过肌肉注射给药的。
words.en: Situated or occurring within a muscle.

words.ex: The drug was administered via an intravascular catheter.
words.ex_cn: 药物通过一根血管内导管给药。
words.en: Inside the blood vessels.

words.ex: The doctor gave him intravenous fluids.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他打了静脉输液。
words.en: Intravenous means within or by means of a vein or veins.

words.ex: The intrepid explorer climbed the high mountain.
words.ex_cn: 这位无畏的探险家爬上了高山。
words.en: If you describe someone as intrepid, you mean that they are brave, fearless, and willing to do things that might be dangerous.

words.ex: The intricacy of the clock made it very special.
words.ex_cn: 这座钟的复杂精细让它非常特别。
words.en: The quality of being intricate; complexity.

words.ex: He is introspective and often thinks about his feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他善于内省，经常思考自己的感受。
words.en: If you describe someone as introspective, you mean that they spend a lot of time examining their own thoughts, ideas, and feelings.

words.tr: n. 内向的人；不喜欢与人交往的人
words.ex: He is an introvert who likes reading alone.
words.ex_cn: 他是个喜欢独自读书的内向者。
words.en: An introvert is a person who tends to shrink from social contacts and to become preoccupied with their own thoughts.

words.ex: The store made an inventory of all the products.
words.ex_cn: 商店对所有商品做了一份清单。
words.en: An inventory is a detailed list of all the items in a place.

words.ex: The jellyfish is an invertebrate.
words.ex_cn: 水母是一种无脊椎动物。
words.en: An invertebrate is an animal that does not have a backbone or spinal column.

words.tr: adj. 不可征服的；不能战胜的
words.ex: He felt invincible after winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 赢得比赛后，他觉得自己不可战胜。
words.en: If someone or something is invincible, they are impossible to defeat or overcome.

words.tr: adj. 非自愿的；不由自主的；
words.ex: His hand moved in an involuntary way.
words.ex_cn: 他的手不自觉地动了一下。
words.en: If you make an involuntary movement or exclamation, you make it suddenly and without intending to because you are unable to control yourself.

words.ex: He took iodine to help his thyroid.
words.ex_cn: 他服用碘来帮助他的甲状腺。
words.en: A chemical element of the halogen group, essential for the production of thyroid hormones.

words.ex: The ion moves quickly in the water.
words.ex_cn: 这个离子在水中快速移动。
words.en: An ion is an atom or molecule with a net electric charge due to the loss or gain of one or more electrons.

words.tr: adj. 不敬的；不逊的；无礼的
words.ex: He made an irreverent joke about the king.
words.ex_cn: 他对国王开了一个不敬的玩笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as irreverent, you mean that they do not show respect for people or things that are generally respected.

words.ex: Ischemia can lead to serious health complications.
words.ex_cn: 缺血可能导致严重的健康并发症。
words.en: A condition in which the blood flow (and thus oxygen) is restricted or reduced in a part of the body.

words.ex: He practices islam every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天 practicing 伊斯兰教。
words.en: Islam is the religion of the Muslims, a monotheistic faith regarded as revealed through Muhammad as the Prophet of Allah.

words.ex: This isotope is used in medical tests.
words.ex_cn: 这种同位素用于医学检查。
words.en: An isotope is one of two or more forms of the same chemical element. Different isotopes of an element have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons in their nuclei.

words.tr:
n. 痒；渴望
v. （使）痒；渴望
words.ex: The mosquito bite caused an itchy on my arm.
words.ex_cn: 蚊子叮咬让我的手臂发痒。
words.en: If you have an itch, you have an unpleasant feeling on your skin that makes you want to scratch. If you itch to do something, you are very eager or impatient to do it.

words.tr:
adj. 巡回的；流动的
n. 四处奔波的人；流浪者
words.ex: The itinerant worker moves from town to town for jobs.
words.ex_cn: 这位流动工人为了工作从一个城镇搬到另一个城镇。
words.en: Someone who is itinerant travels from place to place, usually because they have no permanent home or job, or because they are involved in a particular activity that requires this.

words.ex: He used a jack to lift the car.
words.ex_cn: 他用千斤顶把车顶了起来。
words.en: A jack is a device for lifting heavy objects, especially one for raising the axle of a motor vehicle so that a wheel can be changed or removed.

words.tr:
n. 黄疸病；偏见
v. 使产生黄疸；使怀偏见
words.ex: The baby had jaundice and needed light therapy.
words.ex_cn: 这个婴儿患有黄疸，需要光疗。
words.en: Jaundice is a medical condition in which the skin and the whites of the eyes become yellow, caused by an excess of bile pigment in the blood.

words.ex: The city has increased its efforts to reduce the number of jaywalkers.
words.ex_cn: 该城市加大了减少乱穿马路人数的力度。
words.en: A jaywalker is a person who crosses a street in a careless or dangerous way, especially by not using a designated crossing point.

words.ex: The jejunum is a part of the small intestine.
words.ex_cn: 空肠是小肠的一部分。
words.en: The part of the small intestine between the duodenum and the ileum.

words.ex: The jellyfish floated gently in the sea.
words.ex_cn: 水母在海里轻轻漂浮。
words.en: A jellyfish is a sea creature with a soft, clear body and long tentacles that can sting.

words.ex: He gave the rope a sudden jerk to pull it up.
words.ex_cn: 他猛地一拉绳子，把它拉了上来。
words.en: If you jerk something or someone in a particular direction, or they jerk in a particular direction, they move a short distance very suddenly and quickly.

words.ex: Jesus is central to Christian beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 耶稣是基督教信仰的核心。
words.en: Jesus is the central figure of Christianity, believed by Christians to be the Son of God and the savior of humanity.

words.tr: phrase. 飞行时差反应；时差感
words.ex: He feels tired because of jet lag.
words.ex_cn: 他因为时差而感到疲倦。
words.en: A temporary disorder that causes fatigue, insomnia, and other symptoms as a result of rapid travel across several time zones.

words.ex: He used a jigsaw to cut the wooden board.
words.ex_cn: 他用竖锯切割木板。
words.en: A jigsaw is a machine with a fine blade used for cutting shapes in wood or metal. It is also a puzzle consisting of a picture printed on cardboard or wood and cut into various pieces of different shapes that have to be fitted together.

words.tr: adj. 欢腾的；欢欣鼓舞的
words.ex: The children were jubilant after winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们赢了比赛后非常高兴。
words.en: If you are jubilant, you feel extremely happy because of a success.

words.ex: He poured milk from a jug.
words.ex_cn: 他从一个水壶里倒牛奶。
words.en: A jug is a container used for holding and pouring liquids. It typically has a handle and a spout for easy pouring.

words.ex: Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system.
words.ex_cn: 木星是我们太阳系中最大的行星。
words.en: Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system, known for its prominent Great Red Spot and numerous moons.

words.tr: n. 管辖权；司法权；裁判权；
words.ex: The court has jurisdiction over this case.
words.ex_cn: 法院对这个案件有管辖权。
words.en: The official power to make legal decisions and judgments.

words.ex: He loves studying jurisprudence to understand laws better.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢学习法学以更好地理解法律。
words.en: Jurisprudence is the study of law and the principles on which law is based.

words.ex: The juxtaposition of the old and the new buildings created a striking contrast.
words.ex_cn: 新旧建筑的并置形成了鲜明的对比。
words.en: The act or an instance of placing two or more things side by side often to compare or contrast or to create an interesting effect.

words.ex: He practices karate every evening.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上练习空手道。
words.en: A Japanese martial art in which sharp blows and kicks are administered to pressure-sensitive points on the body of an opponent.

words.ex: His ken does not include quantum physics.
words.ex_cn: 他的知识范围不包括量子物理。
words.en: Ken is the range of one's knowledge or understanding.

words.ex: The kernel of the computer is the operating system.
words.ex_cn: 计算机的核心是操作系统。
words.en: The kernel of something such as a nut or a seed is the part inside the shell. The kernel of an idea or a theory is the central and most important part of it.

words.ex: He uses kerosene to light the lamp.
words.ex_cn: 他用煤油来点灯。
words.en: Kerosene is a type of fuel oil that is used in lamps, heaters, and jet engines.

words.ex: He drank water to help his kidney work better.
words.ex_cn: 他喝水以帮助肾脏更好地工作。
words.en: One of the two organs in your lower back that separate waste products from your blood and make urine.

words.ex: The potter fired the clay in a kiln.
words.ex_cn: 陶匠把陶土放在窑里烧制。
words.en: A kiln is a type of oven that is used to bake clay and pottery in order to make them hard.

words.ex: The heater uses 2 kilowatt of electricity.
words.ex_cn: 这台加热器使用2千瓦的电力。
words.en: A kilowatt is a unit of power equal to one thousand watts.

words.ex: She invited all her kin to the family reunion.
words.ex_cn: 她邀请了所有亲属参加家庭聚会。
words.en: Your kin are your relatives.

words.ex: He learns best through kinesthetic activities like dancing.
words.ex_cn: 他通过跳舞等动觉活动学得最好。
words.en: Relating to a person's awareness of the position and movement of the parts of the body by means of sensory organs in the muscles and joints.

words.tr: v. 点燃；生火；激起；发亮
words.ex: He used a match to kindle the fire.
words.ex_cn: 他用火柴点燃了火。
words.en: To kindle something means to cause it to begin burning or to arouse or inspire it.

words.ex: Kinesiatrics is often used to help patients recover from injuries.
words.ex_cn: 运动疗法常用于帮助病人从受伤中恢复。
words.en: The treatment of disease by means of movement or exercise.

words.ex: The kinetic energy of the moving ball is high.
words.ex_cn: 运动的球的动能很高。
words.en: Relating to or resulting from motion.

words.ex: He put his books in a knapsack and walked to school.
words.ex_cn: 他把书放进背包，然后走路去学校。
words.en: A knapsack is a bag carried on the back, typically made of a strong, waterproof material and used by hikers and soldiers.

words.ex: She wears a warm knitwear sweater in winter.
words.ex_cn: 她在冬天穿一件保暖的针织毛衣。
words.en: Knitwear refers to clothing that has been knitted, as opposed to woven. It includes items such as sweaters, cardigans, and scarves.

words.ex: He turned the knob to adjust the volume.
words.ex_cn: 他转动旋钮来调节音量。
words.en: A knob is a round handle, or a round switch on a piece of equipment.

words.tr:
n. 指关节
v. 用指关节…；屈从
words.ex: He cracked his knuckles before the game.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛前掰响了指关节。
words.en: The knuckles are the joints of the fingers, especially where they join the hand.

words.ex: The labium of the flower is the lower petal that forms the lip.
words.ex_cn: 花的下唇瓣是形成唇的下部花瓣。
words.en: In anatomy, the labium refers to a lip or a lip-like structure. In botany, it can refer to the lower lip of a corolla in certain flowers.

words.tr: n. 迷宫；难解的事件；错综复杂；
words.ex: The child got lost in the labyrinth.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在迷宫里迷路了。
words.en: A labyrinth is a complicated irregular network of passages or paths in which it is difficult to find one's way; a maze.

words.tr: adj. 泪腺的，泪的，满是泪水的
words.ex: The lacrimal gland produces tears to keep the eyes moist.
words.ex_cn: 泪腺分泌泪水以保持眼睛湿润。
words.en: Relating to tears or the tear glands.

words.tr:
n. 乳酸盐
v. 分泌乳汁
words.ex: The mother began to lactate after giving birth.
words.ex_cn: 母亲分娩后开始泌乳。
words.en: To produce milk in the mammary glands, or a salt or ester of lactic acid.

words.ex: He cannot drink milk because he is lactose intolerant.
words.ex_cn: 他不能喝牛奶，因为他乳糖不耐受。
words.en: Lactose is a sugar that is found in milk and milk products.

words.ex: The truck is laden with boxes.
words.ex_cn: 这辆卡车装满了箱子。
words.en: If someone or something is laden with a lot of heavy things, they are holding or carrying them.

words.ex: The doctor used a lancet to draw a drop of blood.
words.ex_cn: 医生用采血针抽取了一滴血。
words.en: A lancet is a small, broad, two-edged surgical knife or blade with a sharp point used to make small incisions.

words.ex: Greenland is the largest landmass in the world.
words.ex_cn: 格陵兰是世界上最大的陆地。
words.en: A landmass is a large area of land such as a continent that is in one piece and not broken up by oceans.

words.tr: n. 山崩；塌方；压倒性的胜利
words.ex: The heavy rain caused a landslide.
words.ex_cn: 大雨引发了山体滑坡。
words.en: A landslide is a victory in an election in which a person or political party gets far more votes or seats than their opponents.

words.ex: The children carried paper lanterns at the festival.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在节日上提着纸灯笼。
words.en: A lantern is a lamp in a container that has a handle for holding or hanging it, and it usually has a protective case around the flame or bulb.

words.tr:
n. 猪油
v. 放入猪油于
words.ex: He put lard on the bread.
words.ex_cn: 他把猪油涂在面包上。
words.en: Lard is a white, solid fat obtained from pigs, used in cooking.

words.ex: The butterfly starts as a larva.
words.ex_cn: 蝴蝶从幼虫开始。
words.en: An insect in the stage of development when it has just come out of an egg and before it changes into its adult form.

words.ex: Laryngology is a specialized branch of medicine focusing on the throat.
words.ex_cn: 喉科学是专注于喉部的医学专业分支。
words.en: Laryngology is the branch of medicine that deals with disorders, diseases, and injuries of the larynx, often called the voice box.

words.ex: The larynx helps us speak and breathe.
words.ex_cn: 喉部帮助我们说话和呼吸。
words.en: The part of the throat that contains the vocal cords and is used for breathing, swallowing, and speaking.

words.ex: The doctor used a laser to fix her eye.
words.ex_cn: 医生用激光修复了她的眼睛。
words.en: A laser is a device that emits light through a process of optical amplification based on the stimulated emission of electromagnetic radiation.

words.tr: n. 倦怠；疲乏；无精打采
words.ex: He felt lassitude after working all day.
words.ex_cn: 他工作了一整天后感到乏力。
words.en: A state of physical or mental weariness; lack of energy.

words.ex: The doctor wears latex gloves to keep clean.
words.ex_cn: 医生戴乳胶手套以保持清洁。
words.en: A milky fluid found in many plants, such as poppies and spurges, which coagulates on exposure to air. It is the source of natural rubber.

words.tr:
n. 车床
v. 用车床加工
words.ex: He uses a lathe to shape wood.
words.ex_cn: 他用车床加工木材。
words.en: A lathe is a machine tool that rotates a workpiece about an axis of rotation to perform various operations such as cutting, sanding, knurling, drilling, or deformation with tools that are applied to the workpiece to create an object with symmetry about that axis.

words.ex: The window was covered with a lattice of iron bars.
words.ex_cn: 窗户被铁条格子覆盖。
words.en: A lattice is a structure consisting of strips of wood or metal crossed and fastened together with square or diamond-shaped spaces left between.

words.ex: He is a Nobel laureate for his poetry.
words.ex_cn: 他因诗歌而获得诺贝尔奖。
words.en: A laureate is someone who has been given a prize or honor for achievement in a particular field, especially in the arts or sciences.

words.ex: He wore a laurel crown on his head.
words.ex_cn: 他头上戴着月桂花环。
words.en: A laurel is a type of shrub or tree, specifically the bay tree, whose leaves are used in cooking and as a symbol of victory or honor.

words.ex: The volcano spilled hot lava down the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 火山喷出炽热的岩浆流下山。
words.en: Lava is the molten rock that comes out of a volcano during an eruption.

words.ex: The lavatory is down the hall.
words.ex_cn: 洗手间在走廊尽头。
words.en: A lavatory is a room equipped with a toilet and sink for washing hands and face.

words.ex: He filed a lawsuit against the company.
words.ex_cn: 他向这家公司提起了诉讼。
words.en: A lawsuit is a case in a court of law which concerns a dispute between two people or organizations.

words.tr: adj. 松弛的；懒散的；马虎的
words.ex: He is lax about his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他对作业很松懈。
words.en: If you say that a person's behaviour or a system is lax, you mean they are not careful or strict about maintaining high standards.

words.tr:
adj. 通便的
n. 泻药；通便剂
words.ex: The doctor prescribed a laxative for his constipation.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他开了一种泻药来治疗便秘。
words.en: A laxative is a substance that you take to make you go to the toilet, especially when you are constipated.

words.tr:
n. 压条法；分层
v. 分层；“layer”的现在分词
words.ex: The technique of layering is used to propagate certain plants.
words.ex_cn: 压条法被用于繁殖某些植物。
words.en: The method of propagating a plant by rooting a part of the stem while it is still attached to the parent plant.

words.ex: The doctor explained the disease in layman terms.
words.ex_cn: 医生用通俗易懂的语言解释了这种疾病。
words.en: A layman is a person who does not have specialized or professional knowledge of a subject.

words.ex: The layout of the room makes it feel bigger.
words.ex_cn: 房间的布局让它显得更大。
words.en: The way in which the parts of something are arranged or laid out.

words.ex: The cat sat on the ledge of the window.
words.ex_cn: 猫坐在窗户的架状突出物上。
words.en: A ledge is a narrow horizontal surface projecting from a wall, cliff, or other surface.

words.tr:
adj. 剩余的；
n. 残留物；
words.ex: We ate the leftover food for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 我们早餐吃了剩下的食物。
words.en: Remaining after the rest has been used, consumed, or dealt with.

words.ex: The legislature passed a new law last week.
words.ex_cn: 立法机构上周通过了一项新法律。
words.en: A legislature is the part of a country's government that is responsible for making laws.

words.ex: He eats beans, a type of legume, every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天吃豆类，一种豆科植物。
words.en: A legume is a plant that has its seeds in pods, such as the pea or bean.

words.ex: The camera has a clear lens.
words.ex_cn: 这台相机有一个清晰的透镜。
words.en: A lens is a piece of curved glass or other transparent substance that is used in things such as cameras, telescopes, or pairs of glasses to make images larger or smaller.

words.ex: The leopard runs fast in the wild.
words.ex_cn: 豹在野外跑得很快。
words.en: A large wild cat that has a yellowish-brown or brown coat with black spots, found in Africa and southern Asia.

words.ex: He was diagnosed with leprosy last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年被诊断出患有麻风病。
words.en: Leprosy is a chronic infectious disease caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium leprae, which primarily affects the skin, the peripheral nerves, mucosal surfaces of the upper respiratory tract, and the eyes.

words.tr: n. 损害；身体上的伤害
words.ex: The doctor found a lesion on his skin.
words.ex_cn: 医生在他的皮肤上发现了一个病灶。
words.en: A lesion is an area of damage to the body, such as a wound, ulcer, or tumor.

words.tr: adj. 慵懒的；没精打采的；懒洋洋的
words.ex: He felt lethargic after eating too much.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多后感到昏昏欲睡。
words.en: If you are lethargic, you do not have much energy or enthusiasm.

words.ex: He felt lethargy after eating too much junk food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃完太多垃圾食品后感到无精打采。
words.en: Lethargy is the condition or state of being lethargic; sluggishness, drowsiness, or apathy.

words.ex: She added lettuce to her sandwich.
words.ex_cn: 她在三明治里加了莴苣。
words.en: Lettuce is a plant with large green leaves that is eaten in salads.

words.ex: He has leukemia and takes medicine every day.
words.ex_cn: 他患有白血病，每天吃药。
words.en: Leukemia is a type of cancer that affects the blood and bone marrow, characterized by an abnormal increase in white blood cells.

words.ex: Leukocytes are essential for fighting infections.
words.ex_cn: 白细胞对于抵抗感染至关重要。
words.en: A leukocyte is any of the colorless cells in the blood that protect the body against infection and disease.

words.tr: n. 白血球增多；白细胞增多
words.ex: Leukocytosis is often observed in bacterial infections.
words.ex_cn: 白细胞增多常在细菌感染中观察到。
words.en: Leukocytosis is an increase in the number of white blood cells in the blood, often due to infection, inflammation, or other medical conditions.

words.ex: Lichen grows on old rocks.
words.ex_cn: 地衣生长在古老的岩石上。
words.en: Lichen is a simple slow-growing plant that typically forms a low crusty, leaflike, or branching growth on rocks, walls, and trees.

words.ex: The word 'licity' is not a standard English word and cannot be used in a sentence.
words.ex_cn: ‘licity’不是一个标准的英语单词，不能用于句子中。
words.en: A misspelling or rare variant of 'licentiousness,' meaning lack of moral restraint or promiscuity.

words.ex: He hurt his ligament while playing soccer.
words.ex_cn: 他在踢足球时拉伤了韧带。
words.en: A ligament is a band of strong tissue in a person's body which connects bones.

words.ex: The child hurt his limb while playing.
words.ex_cn: 孩子玩耍时伤到了肢体。
words.en: A limb is one of the jointed appendages of an animal used for locomotion or grasping: arm; leg; wing; flipper.

words.ex: Farmers spread lime on the soil to make it less acidic.
words.ex_cn: 农民在土壤上撒石灰以降低其酸性。
words.en: Lime is a white substance obtained by heating limestone, used in making cement and in farming to improve soil. It is also a small green fruit that is similar to a lemon.

words.tr: n. 舞台灯光；公众注意的中心
words.ex: He loves to be in the limelight.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢成为众人瞩目的焦点。
words.en: The focus of public attention or notoriety.

words.ex: The building is made of limestone.
words.ex_cn: 这座建筑是由石灰岩建造的。
words.en: Limestone is a sedimentary rock composed largely of the mineral calcite (calcium carbonate: CaCO3).

words.ex: She washed the linen in cold water.
words.ex_cn: 她用冷水洗亚麻布。
words.en: Linen is a kind of cloth that is made from the fibers of the flax plant. It is used to make clothes, sheets, and tablecloths.

words.ex: The liner sailed across the ocean with hundreds of passengers.
words.ex_cn: 这艘邮轮载着数百名乘客横渡了海洋。
words.en: A liner is a large ship that carries passengers on regular journeys.

words.tr: n. 衬里；内衬；衬层； v. 排队；加衬里；“line”的现在分词；
words.ex: The coat has a soft lining for warmth.
words.ex_cn: 这件外套有柔软的衬里以保暖。
words.en: A lining is a layer of material that is fixed to the inside of something in order to protect it or make it warmer.

words.ex: Lipase is an enzyme that breaks down fats in the digestive system.
words.ex_cn: 脂肪酶是一种在消化系统中分解脂肪的酶。
words.en: An enzyme that catalyzes the breakdown of fats into glycerol and fatty acids.

words.ex: The fish contains healthy lipid.
words.ex_cn: 这种鱼含有健康的脂质。
words.en: Lipids are a broad group of naturally occurring molecules which include fats, waxes, sterols, fat-soluble vitamins, monoglycerides, diglycerides, triglycerides, and phospholipids. The main biological functions of lipids include storing energy, signaling, and acting as structural components of cell membranes.

words.tr:
adj. 类脂的
n. 类脂化合物
words.ex: The lipoid content in the cells was significantly reduced.
words.ex_cn: 细胞中的类脂含量显著降低。
words.en: Resembling fat; fatty.

words.ex: He felt listless after the long illness.
words.ex_cn: 他生病后感到无精打采。
words.en: If someone is listless, they lack energy or enthusiasm.

words.tr: n. 连祷文；枯燥冗长的陈述
words.ex: The meeting was filled with a litany of complaints.
words.ex_cn: 会议充斥着冗长的抱怨。
words.en: A litany is a form of prayer in which a series of petitions are recited by a leader with responses from the congregation. It can also refer to any long, tedious account or recital.

words.ex: Lithiasis can be a painful condition, requiring medical intervention.
words.ex_cn: 结石病可能是一种痛苦的疾病，需要医疗干预。
words.en: The formation of stony concretions in the body, especially in the gallbladder or urinary tract.

words.ex: He bought a lithograph of a famous painting.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一幅著名绘画的石版画。
words.en: A lithograph is a print made by a method of printing from a flat surface, especially a metal plate, that has been treated so that the ink sticks only to the parts that are to be printed.

words.ex: The lithosphere moves slowly over the mantle.
words.ex_cn: 岩石圈在地幔上缓慢移动。
words.en: The lithosphere is the solid, outer part of the Earth. It includes the brittle upper portion of the mantle and the crust, the outermost layers of Earth's structure.

words.ex: He eats too much sugar and his liver is hurt.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多糖，他的肝脏受损了。
words.en: The liver is a large organ in the body that cleans the blood and produces bile, or a person who lives in a particular way.

words.ex: The lizard sits on the rock in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 蜥蜴趴在阳光下的石头上。
words.en: A lizard is a reptile with a long body, four legs, a long tail, and rough, scaly skin.

words.ex: The doctor examined the left lobe of the lung.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了左肺叶。
words.en: A lobe is a rounded projection or division, especially a part of the brain, lung, or liver, that is separated from the rest by a fissure.

words.ex: He bought a fresh lobster at the market.
words.ex_cn: 他在市场上买了一只新鲜的龙虾。
words.en: A lobster is a sea creature with a hard shell, two large claws, and eight legs, or the flesh of this animal eaten as food.

words.ex: The liver has many small lobules.
words.ex_cn: 肝脏有许多小叶。
words.en: A small lobe or subdivision of a lobe.

words.ex: The child learns locomotion by crawling.
words.ex_cn: 孩子通过爬行学习移动。
words.en: The ability to move from place to place.

words.ex: The locomotive pulled the train down the track.
words.ex_cn: 机车拉着火车沿着轨道行驶。
words.en: A locomotive is a powered rail vehicle used for pulling trains.

words.ex: The locust flew over the field.
words.ex_cn: 蝗虫飞过了田野。
words.en: A locust is a large insect that lives in hot countries and flies in large groups, destroying crops.

words.tr: adj. 高的；崇高的；傲慢的
words.ex: The mountain has a lofty peak.
words.ex_cn: 这座山有一个很高的山顶。
words.en: If you say that someone behaves in a lofty way, you are critical of them for behaving in a proud and rather unpleasant way, as if they think they are very important.

words.ex: They built a log cabin in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 他们在森林里建了一座木屋。
words.en: A log cabin is a small house made from logs, especially one in a forest or a mountainous area.

words.ex: The law has a loophole that lets companies avoid taxes.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律有一个漏洞，让公司可以避税。
words.en: A loophole is a small mistake in a law or set of rules which allows people to do something that would otherwise be illegal or not allowed.

words.tr: adj. 话多的；健谈的；喋喋不休的
words.ex: He is a loquacious man who talks all day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个整天喋喋不休的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as loquacious, you mean that they talk a lot.

words.ex: He is well-versed in the lore of ancient civilizations.
words.ex_cn: 他对古代文明的知识了如指掌。
words.en: Knowledge and traditions relating to a particular subject or held by a particular group.

words.ex: She puts lotion on her hands after washing them.
words.ex_cn: 她洗手后在手上涂乳液。
words.en: A lotion is a liquid that you use to clean, improve, or protect your skin or hair.

words.tr:
n. 虱子；寄生虫；卑鄙的家伙
v. 办砸；除虱子
words.ex: The boy has a louse in his hair.
words.ex_cn: 那个男孩头发里有一只虱子。
words.en: A louse is a small, wingless, parasitic insect that lives on the skin of mammals and birds. It can also refer to a contemptible person.

words.ex: The mechanic applied a lubricant to the moving parts.
words.ex_cn: 机械师给活动部件涂上了润滑油。
words.en: A substance, such as oil or grease, used to minimize friction, heat, and wear between mechanical parts in contact with each other.

words.ex: Oil helps to lubricate the engine parts.
words.ex_cn: 油有助于润滑发动机部件。
words.en: To apply a substance such as oil or grease to (something) in order to minimize friction and allow smooth movement.

words.tr: adj. 可笑的；荒谬的；滑稽的
words.ex: It is ludicrous to wear a coat in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天穿外套真是荒谬。
words.en: If you describe something as ludicrous, you are emphasizing that you think it is foolish, unreasonable, or unsuitable.

words.ex: The teacher gave a lucid explanation of the math problem.
words.ex_cn: 老师对这道数学题做了一个易懂的解释。
words.en: If someone is lucid, they are able to understand things clearly and think clearly, especially when they have been very ill or confused.

words.ex: The mother sang a lullaby to her baby.
words.ex_cn: 妈妈为她的宝宝唱了一首摇篮曲。
words.en: A lullaby is a quiet song which is intended to be sung to babies and young children to help them go to sleep.

words.ex: He has pain in his lumbar area.
words.ex_cn: 他的腰部有疼痛。
words.en: Relating to the lower part of the back.

words.ex: The light output is measured in lumens.
words.ex_cn: 光输出以流明为单位进行测量。
words.en: A unit of luminous flux in the International System of Units, equal to the amount of light emitted per second in a unit solid angle of one steradian by a uniform point source of one candela.

words.ex: He ate a lump of sugar.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一块糖。
words.en: A lump is a solid piece of something, often with no particular shape. If you lump things together, you put them together in a group or treat them as the same.

words.ex: We had a quick luncheon at the café.
words.ex_cn: 我们在咖啡馆简单吃了顿午餐。
words.en: A luncheon is a formal lunch, or a formal word for lunch.

words.tr:
n. 突然倾斜；急动；踉跄
v. 突然倾斜；急动；踉跄
words.ex: The boat made a sudden lurch to the left.
words.ex_cn: 船突然向左倾斜。
words.en: If you lurch, you move suddenly and uncontrollably in one direction.

words.tr: adj. 精力充沛的；生气勃勃的；健壮的
words.ex: The young man sang a lusty song at the party.
words.ex_cn: 那个年轻人在派对上唱了一首嘹亮的歌。
words.en: If you describe someone as lusty, you mean that they are strong and healthy and full of energy.

words.ex: The lymph helps fight infections in the body.
words.ex_cn: 淋巴有助于抵抗身体中的感染。
words.en: Lymph is a clear fluid that is derived from blood plasma and contains white blood cells, especially lymphocytes.

words.ex: Lymphocytes are a type of white blood cell that plays a key role in the immune system.
words.ex_cn: 淋巴细胞是一种白血细胞，在免疫系统中起着关键作用。
words.en: A lymphocyte is a type of white blood cell that is part of the immune system. Lymphocytes include natural killer cells, T cells, and B cells. They are the main type of cell found in lymph, which prompted the name 'lymphocyte'.

words.ex: The enzyme will lyse the cells, releasing their contents.
words.ex_cn: 这种酶会溶解细胞，释放其内容物。
words.en: To break down or disintegrate a cell or molecule, especially by the action of enzymes.

words.ex: He did an analysis of the data.
words.ex_cn: 他对数据进行了分析。
words.en: Analysis is the process of considering something carefully or using statistical methods in order to understand it or explain it.

words.ex: The macrophage eats bacteria in the blood.
words.ex_cn: 巨噬细胞吞噬血液中的细菌。
words.en: A macrophage is a type of white blood cell that is an important part of the immune system. It engulfs and digests cellular debris, foreign substances, microbes, and cancer cells in a process called phagocytosis.

words.ex: The scientist used a macroscopical approach to study the ecosystem.
words.ex_cn: 科学家使用宏观的方法来研究生态系统。
words.en: Relating to observations made by the naked eye or concerning large-scale structures or phenomena.

words.ex: The astronomer observed a large macula on the surface of the sun.
words.ex_cn: 天文学家观察到太阳表面有一个大的太阳黑子。
words.en: A small area of the retina that is responsible for central vision and the ability to see fine detail.

words.tr:
n. 品红；紫红色
adj. 品红色的；洋红色的
words.ex: The flower is magenta.
words.ex_cn: 这朵花是洋红色的。
words.en: A color that is a purplish red, one of the primary colors in the printing process.

words.tr: n. 地方法官；治安官；行政官；
words.ex: The magistrate decided the small case quickly.
words.ex_cn: 地方法官迅速裁决了这起小案件。
words.en: A magistrate is an official who acts as a judge in law courts that deal with minor crimes or disputes.

words.tr:
n. 磁力悬浮火车
adj. 磁力悬浮火车的
words.ex: The maglev train moves very fast without wheels.
words.ex_cn: 磁悬浮列车没有轮子，跑得很快。
words.en: Maglev is a method of propulsion that uses magnetic levitation to propel vehicles with magnets rather than with wheels, axles and bearings.

words.ex: The volcano spewed hot magma into the air.
words.ex_cn: 火山喷出了炽热的岩浆。
words.en: Magma is molten rock that is found beneath the surface of the Earth, and which may erupt from a volcano as lava.

words.ex: Magnesium helps muscles work properly.
words.ex_cn: 镁有助于肌肉正常运作。
words.en: Magnesium is a silver-white metallic element that is essential for human nutrition and is used in various industrial applications.

words.ex: It was her maiden flight on a plane.
words.ex_cn: 这是她第一次坐飞机。
words.en: A maiden is a young girl or woman who is not married.

words.tr: n. 支柱；中坚；中流砥柱
words.ex: His support has been the mainstay of the project.
words.ex_cn: 他的支持一直是这个项目的支柱。
words.en: If you describe something as the mainstay of a particular thing, you mean that it is the most basic part of it.

words.ex: He grows maize on his farm.
words.ex_cn: 他在农场种植玉米。
words.en: Maize is a tall plant which produces long objects covered with yellow seeds called sweetcorn. It is often grown as a food crop.

words.tr: n. 身体不适；不快；萎靡不振；痼疾
words.ex: She felt a general malaise after the long flight.
words.ex_cn: 长途飞行后，她感到全身不适。
words.en: A general feeling of discomfort, illness, or unease whose exact cause is difficult to identify.

words.ex: He got malaria from a mosquito bite.
words.ex_cn: 他被蚊子叮咬后得了疟疾。
words.en: Malaria is a disease caused by a parasite that is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected mosquitoes.

words.ex: The baby was born with a malformation.
words.ex_cn: 这个婴儿出生时有畸形。
words.en: A malformation is an abnormal shape or structure, especially one that is present from birth.

words.tr: adj. 恶毒的；恶性的；恶意的
words.ex: His malignant words hurt everyone around him.
words.ex_cn: 他恶毒的话语伤害了周围的所有人。
words.en: If you say that someone is malignant, you mean they are very dangerous and cause harm to people.

words.ex: He hit the nail with a wooden mallet.
words.ex_cn: 他用木槌敲钉子。
words.en: A mallet is a tool resembling a hammer but with a larger head, typically made of wood or rubber, used for striking a surface without causing damage.

words.tr:
n. 猛玛（象）；庞然大物；
adj. 巨大的；庞大的；
words.ex: The mammoth lived in cold areas long ago.
words.ex_cn: 猛犸象很久以前生活在寒冷地区。
words.en: If you describe something as mammoth, you are emphasizing that it is extremely large.

words.tr: n. 狂热； 癖好；躁狂症
words.ex: He has a mania for collecting stamps.
words.ex_cn: 他痴迷于收集邮票。
words.en: An extreme enthusiasm or desire for something, often to the point of obsession.

words.tr:
adj. 躁郁症的
n. 躁郁症患者
words.ex: He was diagnosed as a manic-depressive.
words.ex_cn: 他被诊断为躁狂抑郁病患者。
words.en: A manic-depressive illness, also known as bipolar disorder, is a mental health condition that causes extreme mood swings that include emotional highs (mania or hypomania) and lows (depression).

words.tr: n. 指甲修饰师；美甲师
words.ex: She worked as a manicurist at the local salon.
words.ex_cn: 她在当地的美容院做指甲修饰师。
words.en: A manicurist is a person whose job is to care for and beautify people's hands and nails.

words.tr:
adj. 载人的；有人操纵的
v. 操作；工作；“man”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The spaceship was manned by three astronauts.
words.ex_cn: 这艘宇宙飞船由三名宇航员驾驶。
words.en: If a vehicle or a place is manned, it has people in it who operate it or guard it.

words.ex: His mannerism of tapping his fingers shows he is nervous.
words.ex_cn: 他敲手指的行为特征表明他很紧张。
words.en: A mannerism is a particular habit or way of speaking or behaving that someone has, especially one that they have had for a long time and that has become characteristic of them.

words.ex: The technician used a manometer to measure the pressure in the system.
words.ex_cn: 技术人员使用压力计测量系统中的压力。
words.en: A manometer is an instrument for measuring the pressure of a fluid or gas.

words.ex: Farmers spread manure on the fields to help crops grow.
words.ex_cn: 农民把肥料撒在田里以帮助庄稼生长。
words.en: Manure is organic matter used as fertilizer in agriculture.

words.ex: He found an old manuscript in the library.
words.ex_cn: 他在图书馆里发现了一份旧手稿。
words.en: A manuscript is a handwritten or typed document, especially a writer's first version of a book before it is published.

words.ex: The birds live in a quiet marsh.
words.ex_cn: 这些鸟生活在一片宁静的沼泽中。
words.en: A marsh is an area of low-lying land which is flooded in wet seasons or at high tide, and typically remains waterlogged at all times.

words.tr:
n. 元帅；高级军官；典礼官；消防局长
v. 整理；集结
words.ex: The marshal led the army into battle.
words.ex_cn: 元帅率领军队上战场。
words.en: A marshal is a high-ranking officer in the armed forces, especially in the army or air force, or a person who arranges or directs a public event.

words.ex: The marshy land was full of tall reeds and frogs.
words.ex_cn: 这片沼泽地长满了高高的芦苇和青蛙。
words.en: Marshy land is land that is wet and muddy, often because it is near a river or lake.

words.tr:
n. 殉道者；殉教者；烈士
v. 处死；折磨
words.ex: He became a martyr for freedom.
words.ex_cn: 他为自由而成为烈士。
words.en: A martyr is someone who is killed or made to suffer greatly because of their religious or political beliefs, and is admired and respected by people who share those beliefs.

words.ex: He believes in marxism and supports workers' rights.
words.ex_cn: 他相信马克思主义，并支持工人的权利。
words.en: Marxism is a method of socioeconomic analysis that views class relations and social conflict using a materialist interpretation of historical development and takes a dialectical view of social transformation.

words.tr:
adj. 马克思主义的
n. 马克思主义者
words.ex: He is a Marxist who believes in workers' rights.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位相信工人权利的马克思主义者。
words.en: A Marxist is someone who believes in the political and economic theories of Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels, especially the idea that capitalism will inevitably be replaced by socialism and then communism.

words.ex: The mason built a stone wall with care.
words.ex_cn: 石匠仔细地砌了一堵石墙。
words.en: A mason is a person who builds or works with stone or brick.

words.ex: The old church has strong masonry walls.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的教堂有坚固的石砖结构墙壁。
words.en: Masonry is the craft of building with stone, brick, or similar materials, often using mortar.

words.tr:
n. 化妆舞会；伪装
v. 伪装；冒充
words.ex: We went to a masquerade last night.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨晚去参加了一个化妆舞会。
words.en: A masquerade is a party or dance where people wear masks and costumes, or it refers to the act of pretending to be someone or something else.

words.tr:
v. 屠杀 
n. 大屠杀
words.ex: The soldiers committed a massacre in the village.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在村庄里进行了大屠杀。
words.en: The indiscriminate killing of a large number of people.

words.ex: The sailboat's mast is very tall.
words.ex_cn: 帆船的船桅很高。
words.en: A mast is a tall pole on a ship or boat that supports the sails.

words.tr:
n. 母亲身份；
adj. 产妇的；
words.ex: She enjoys her maternity after giving birth to her first child.
words.ex_cn: 她在生下第一个孩子后享受做母亲的身份。
words.en: Maternity refers to the state of being a mother or the period during which a woman is pregnant or has recently given birth.

words.ex: The matrix gave birth to all living things.
words.ex_cn: 母体孕育了所有生命。
words.en: A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers, symbols, or expressions, arranged in rows and columns.

words.tr: n. 护士长；女舍监；已婚妇女
words.ex: The matron checked on the sick children at night.
words.ex_cn: 女管理员晚上查看生病的孩子们。
words.en: A matron is a woman in charge of domestic and medical arrangements in a boarding school, hospital, or other institution.

words.ex: The maturation of the fruit takes several weeks.
words.ex_cn: 水果的成熟需要几周时间。
words.en: The process of becoming mature or the state of being mature.

words.ex: He is a maverick who always does things his own way.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个总是按自己方式做事的独行其是者。
words.en: If you describe someone as a maverick, you mean that they are unconventional and independent, and do not think or behave in the same way as other people.

words.ex: He always follows the maxim 'work hard, play hard'.
words.ex_cn: 他总是遵循‘努力工作，尽情玩耍’这一信条。
words.en: A maxim is a short, easily remembered expression of a basic principle, general truth, or rule of conduct.

words.ex: He put mayonnaise on his sandwich.
words.ex_cn: 他在三明治上加了蛋黄酱。
words.en: A thick, creamy dressing consisting of egg yolks beaten with oil and vinegar and seasoned.

words.ex: The cows are grazing in the meadow.
words.ex_cn: 牛群正在草地上吃草。
words.en: A meadow is a field with grass and often wild flowers in it.

words.ex: He had measles when he was five.
words.ex_cn: 他五岁时得了麻疹。
words.en: An infectious disease that causes fever and small red spots on the skin.

words.tr: n. 运作方式；力学；“mechanic”的复数；
words.ex: The mechanics of this machine are simple to understand.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器的运作方式很简单易懂。
words.en: Mechanics is the branch of physics that deals with the action of forces on bodies and with motion, comprised of kinetics, statics, and kinematics.

words.ex: He is a mechanist who believes everything can be explained by machines.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名机械论者，认为一切都可以用机器来解释。
words.en: A mechanist is someone who believes in or advocates the mechanistic theory, which explains all phenomena by physical and mechanical principles.

words.tr:
n. 中位数；（三角形的）中线
adj. 中间值的；中间的
words.ex: The median of 3, 5, and 7 is 5.
words.ex_cn: 3、5和7的中位数是5。
words.en: The median is the middle number in a sorted, ascending or descending, list of numbers and can be more descriptive of that data set than the average.

words.ex: He uses medicare to pay for his doctor visits.
words.ex_cn: 他使用医疗保险支付看医生的费用。
words.en: A system of health insurance for people over 65 in the US, paid for by a combination of payroll taxes and general federal revenue.

words.tr: n. 媒体与体育的结合；媒体体育学
words.ex: The course in mediathletics explores the intersection of media and sports.
words.ex_cn: 媒体体育学课程探讨了媒体与体育的交汇点。
words.en: The term 'mediathletics' refers to the competitive activities or events that are related to media, where individuals or teams compete in creating, managing, or utilizing media content.

words.ex: The case required a medicolegal examination to determine the cause of death.
words.ex_cn: 这起案件需要法医学检查来确定死因。
words.en: Relating to both medicine and law, especially to the legal aspects of medical practice.

words.ex: The movie was mediocre and not worth watching.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影很平庸，不值得看。
words.en: If you describe something as mediocre, you mean that it is of average quality but you think it should be better.

words.tr:
n. 地中海；
adj. 地中海的；
words.ex: He sailed across the Mediterranean last summer.
words.ex_cn: 他去年夏天横渡了地中海。
words.en: relating to the Mediterranean Sea or the countries around it

words.ex: The medulla is the innermost part of the kidney.
words.ex_cn: 骨髓是肾脏的最内层部分。
words.en: The medulla is the innermost part of an organ or structure, especially the marrow of bones or the medulla oblongata in the brain.

words.ex: The meek boy quietly listened to the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 那个温顺的男孩静静地听老师讲课。
words.en: If you describe a person as meek, you think that they are gentle and quiet, and likely to do what other people say.

words.tr:
n. 夸大狂患者
adj. 妄自尊大的
words.ex: He was a megalomaniac who believed he could conquer the world.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个妄自尊大的人，认为自己可以征服世界。
words.en: A megalomaniac is a person who has an obsessive desire for power and thinks they are much more important and powerful than they really are.

words.tr:
n. 忧愁
adj.  忧郁的
words.ex: He felt melancholy after the rain stopped.
words.ex_cn: 雨停后，他感到忧郁。
words.en: A feeling of deep sadness, typically with no obvious cause.

words.ex: Melanin is responsible for the color of skin, hair, and eyes.
words.ex_cn: 黑色素决定了皮肤、头发和眼睛的颜色。
words.en: Melanin is a dark pigment found in the skin, hair, and eyes of people and animals, responsible for their color.

words.ex: The bird sang a melodic tune at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 鸟在黎明时唱出一首有旋律的歌。
words.en: Something that is melodic has a pleasant tune or a series of sounds that are pleasant to listen to.

words.ex: The bird sang a melodious song at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在黎明时唱出旋律优美的歌。
words.en: If something such as a voice or a tune is melodious, it is pleasant to listen to because it has a musical quality.

words.ex: The movie is a melodrama with crying and loud arguments.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是一部充满哭泣和激烈争吵的煽情剧。
words.en: A melodrama is a dramatic work in which the plot, typically sensational and designed to appeal strongly to the emotions, takes precedence over detailed characterization.

words.ex: The cell has a thin membrane.
words.ex_cn: 细胞有一层薄薄的膜。
words.en: A membrane is a thin layer of tissue or material that covers or lines a part of the body, or separates one area from another.

words.ex: He wrote a memo to remind the team.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一封备忘录提醒团队。
words.en: A memo is a short official note that is sent by one person to another within the same company or organization.

words.ex: He wrote a memoir about his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一本关于自己童年的回忆录。
words.en: A memoir is a book or article that you write about someone who you have known, describing what you remember of them and of particular events in which you both took part.

words.ex: He wrote a memorandum about the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一份关于会议的备忘录。
words.en: A memorandum is a written proposal or reminder, especially in a business context.

words.ex: He looked at her menacingly, his eyes filled with anger.
words.ex_cn: 他恶狠狠地看着她，眼中充满了愤怒。
words.en: In a way that suggests the presence of danger; threateningly.

words.ex: Meningitis can be a life-threatening condition if not treated promptly.
words.ex_cn: 如果不及时治疗，脑膜炎可能会危及生命。
words.en: Meningitis is a serious illness in which there is inflammation of the meninges, the membranes covering the brain and spinal cord, usually caused by infection.

words.ex: The doctor prescribed medication to alleviate her menstrual cramps.
words.ex_cn: 医生开了药来缓解她的月经疼痛。
words.en: Relating to the menstruation or the monthly discharge of blood and mucosal tissue from the inner lining of the uterus through the vagina.

words.ex: My mentor helped me choose my career path.
words.ex_cn: 我的导师帮助我选择了职业道路。
words.en: A mentor is a person who gives a younger or less experienced person help and advice over a period of time, especially at work or school.

words.tr:
adj. 多汞的；含汞的；易变的；灵活的；反复无常的
n. 汞制剂；水银剂
words.ex: His mercurial mood changes from happy to angry quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他多汞的情绪很快从高兴变到生气。
words.en: If you describe someone as mercurial, you mean that they frequently change their mind or mood without warning.

words.ex: The thermometer contains mercury.
words.ex_cn: 温度计里含有水银。
words.en: Mercury is a heavy, silvery-white metal that is liquid at room temperature. It is used in thermometers, barometers, and other scientific apparatus.

words.tr: adj. 俗气的；华而不实的；虚有其表的
words.ex: The decoration was meretricious and lacked any real artistic merit.
words.ex_cn: 装饰俗气，缺乏真正的艺术价值。
words.en: Something that is meretricious is attractive in a showy or cheap way, often without having any real value or quality.

words.ex: The prime meridian passes through Greenwich, England.
words.ex_cn: 本初子午线穿过英国格林尼治。
words.en: A meridian is an imaginary great circle on the earth's surface passing through the north and south poles at right angles to the equator, or the highest point reached by a celestial or other object.

words.ex: The net is made of a fine mesh.
words.ex_cn: 这个网是由细密的网状物制成的。
words.en: A mesh is a material made of a network of wire or thread to catch or hold things, or to allow things to pass through it.

words.ex: Mesothelioma is a rare form of cancer usually caused by asbestos exposure.
words.ex_cn: 间皮瘤是一种罕见的癌症，通常由石棉暴露引起。
words.en: A type of cancer that occurs in the thin layer of tissue that covers the majority of your internal organs (mesothelium).

words.ex: His metabolic rate is very high.
words.ex_cn: 他的新陈代谢率很高。
words.en: Relating to or involving the chemical processes that occur within a living organism in order to maintain life.

words.ex: His metabolism is very fast.
words.ex_cn: 他的新陈代谢非常快。
words.en: Metabolism is the set of life-sustaining chemical transformations within the cells of living organisms.

words.ex: He works in metallurgy at a steel factory.
words.ex_cn: 他在钢铁厂从事冶金工作。
words.en: Metallurgy is the scientific study of the extraction, refining, alloying, and fabrication of metals and of their structure and properties.

words.ex: The cancer showed metastasis to the lungs.
words.ex_cn: 癌症已经转移到肺部。
words.en: The spread of a disease, especially cancer, from one part of the body to another.

words.ex: A bright meteor flashed across the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 一颗明亮的流星划过夜空。
words.en: A meteor is a piece of rock or metal that burns very brightly when it enters the earth's atmosphere from space.

words.ex: The boy found a meteorite in the field.
words.ex_cn: 男孩在田野里发现了一块陨石。
words.en: A meteorite is a piece of rock or metal that has fallen to the earth's surface from outer space.

words.ex: Methane is a gas that comes from cows and landfills.
words.ex_cn: 甲烷是一种来自牛和垃圾填埋场的气体。
words.en: A colorless, odorless flammable gas which is the main constituent of natural gas. It is the simplest member of the alkane series of hydrocarbons.

words.tr: adj. 一丝不苟的；缜密的
words.ex: He is meticulous about checking his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他仔细检查作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as meticulous, you mean that they do things very carefully and with great attention to detail.

words.ex: The microbe causes sickness.
words.ex_cn: 这种微生物会引起疾病。
words.en: A microbe is a very small living thing, which you can only see if you use a microscope. Some microbes can cause diseases.

words.tr: n. 微观世界；小宇宙；缩影
words.ex: The classroom is a microcosm of society.
words.ex_cn: 教室是社会的一个缩影。
words.en: A microcosm is a small, representative system having analogies to a larger system in constitution, configuration, or development.

words.ex: He used microfilm to save old newspapers.
words.ex_cn: 他使用微缩胶片保存旧报纸。
words.en: Microfilm is a film on which documents or printed materials are photographed at a greatly reduced size for ease of storage.

words.ex: A microorganism can cause sickness.
words.ex_cn: 微生物会导致疾病。
words.en: A microorganism is a very small living thing that you can only see with a microscope.

words.tr: n. 微处理器；微处理机
words.ex: The computer has a fast microprocessor.
words.ex_cn: 这台电脑有一个快速的微处理器。
words.en: A microprocessor is a small chip that can process data and carry out instructions in a computer or other electronic device.

words.ex: The bacteria are microscopic.
words.ex_cn: 这些细菌极小。
words.en: So small as to be visible only with a microscope; of or relating to a microscope.

words.ex: She heated the food in the microwave.
words.ex_cn: 她把食物放在微波炉里加热。
words.en: A microwave is a type of oven that cooks or heats food very quickly by using electromagnetic waves rather than heat.

words.ex: He likes middlebrow novels that are easy to read.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢容易阅读的中等品位小说。
words.en: If you describe someone as middlebrow, you mean they are neither intellectual nor lowbrow, but somewhere in between.

words.ex: He feels comfortable in his artistic milieu.
words.ex_cn: 他在他的艺术环境中感到自在。
words.en: The milieu is the environment or setting in which something happens or develops.

words.ex: The millennium began in the year 2000.
words.ex_cn: 一千年始于2000年。
words.en: A millennium is a period of one thousand years.

words.ex: He was such a milquetoast that he never stood up for his own beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个如此懦弱的人，以至于他从未为自己的信念挺身而出。
words.en: A milquetoast is a person who is timid or submissive.

words.ex: The children gave a mimetic performance of the animals.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们表演了模仿动物的节目。
words.en: Mimetic refers to the ability or tendency to mimic or imitate.

words.tr:
v. 切碎；剁碎；装腔作势地小步走
n. 绞碎的肉
words.ex: He minces garlic for the sauce.
words.ex_cn: 他把大蒜剁碎用来做酱。
words.en: To mince means to cut food, especially meat, into very small pieces, or to walk or speak in an affected manner.

words.tr:
adj. 微型的；
n. 微型画；小型模型；
words.ex: He bought a miniature car for his collection.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的收藏买了一辆微型汽车。
words.en: A miniature is a very small detailed painting, often a portrait. It can also refer to a small-scale model or representation of something.

words.ex: She added a mint leaf to her drink.
words.ex_cn: 她在饮料里加了一片薄荷叶。
words.en: Mint is a plant with fresh-tasting leaves. It is also the place where coins are made, or the act of making coins.

words.ex: The minuscule dot was hard to see with the naked eye.
words.ex_cn: 那个极小的点用肉眼很难看到。
words.en: If you describe something as minuscule, you mean that it is very small.

words.tr: adj. 奇迹般的；不可思议的；神奇的
words.ex: The sick boy made a miraculous recovery.
words.ex_cn: 那个生病的男孩奇迹般地康复了。
words.en: If you describe a good event as miraculous, you mean that it is very surprising and unexpected.

words.ex: He saw a mirage in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 他在沙漠中看到了海市蜃楼。
words.en: An optical illusion caused by atmospheric conditions, especially the appearance of a sheet of water in a desert or on a hot road caused by the refraction of light from the sky by heated air.

words.ex: The teacher punished the boy for his misbehavior.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为他的不良行为惩罚了那个男孩。
words.en: Misbehavior refers to actions or conduct that are considered inappropriate or unacceptable in a given context, especially by children or students in an educational setting.

words.tr: n. 流产；早产；误投；失败
words.ex: She had a miscarriage last month.
words.ex_cn: 她上个月流产了。
words.en: A miscarriage is the premature expulsion of a fetus from the womb before it is able to survive independently, or a failure to achieve the intended result of a plan or action.

words.ex: He bought some miscellaneous items at the store.
words.ex_cn: 他在商店里买了一些各种各样的东西。
words.en: Consisting of a variety of ingredients or parts.

words.tr: n. 恶作剧；淘气；伤害；损害
words.ex: The boy caused mischief by letting the cats out.
words.ex_cn: 那个男孩放出了猫，惹了麻烦。
words.en: Mischief is behavior, especially by children, that is slightly bad but is not intended to cause serious harm or damage.

words.ex: The miser saved all his money and never spent it.
words.ex_cn: 这个吝啬鬼把所有的钱都存起来，从不花掉。
words.en: A miser is a person who is extremely unwilling to spend money, often to the point of living in poverty despite having wealth.

words.tr:
n. 疑虑；怀疑
v. 使疑虑；使担忧；“misgive”的现在分词
words.ex: He had a misgiving about the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个计划感到不安。
words.en: A misgiving is a feeling of doubt or anxiety about something that might happen or might have happened.

words.ex: Planting trees can mitigate air pollution.
words.ex_cn: 植树可以减轻空气污染。
words.en: To mitigate something means to make it less unpleasant, serious, or painful.

words.ex: The mitral valve is a critical part of the heart's structure.
words.ex_cn: 二尖瓣是心脏结构的重要部分。
words.en: Relating to the mitral valve, which is the valve between the left atrium and the left ventricle of the heart.

words.ex: He wears a mitten to keep his hand warm.
words.ex_cn: 他戴一只连指手套来暖手。
words.en: A mitten is a glove that has one section for the thumb and another section for all four fingers together, used to keep the hands warm in cold weather.

words.ex: The old castle has a deep moat around it.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的城堡周围有一条深深的护城河。
words.en: A moat is a deep, wide ditch that is dug around a place such as a castle and is usually filled with water, in order to protect the place from attack.

words.tr: n. 嘲鸫（一种鸟，能模仿其他鸟的叫声）
words.ex: The mockingbird sings loudly in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 嘲鸟在早晨大声歌唱。
words.en: A mockingbird is a bird that is known for its ability to mimic the calls of other bird species.

words.ex: This house has a modern design.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子具有现代的设计。
words.en: Modern means relating to the present time, for example the present decade or present century.

words.tr: n. 少量；一点点；一小份
words.ex: He had a modicum of common sense.
words.ex_cn: 他有一点点常识。
words.en: A modicum of something, especially something that is good or desirable, is a small but useful or significant amount of it.

words.ex: The software has five different modules.
words.ex_cn: 这个软件有五个不同的模块。
words.en: A module is one of the separate parts of a course of study, especially at a college or university.

words.ex: He has pain in his molar.
words.ex_cn: 他的磨牙很疼。
words.en: A molar is a large tooth at the back of the mouth, used for grinding food. As an adjective, it relates to the molar teeth or to a measure in chemistry.

words.ex: The mole dug a tunnel under the garden.
words.ex_cn: 鼹鼠在花园下挖了一条隧道。
words.en: A mole is a small animal with black fur that lives underground. It can also refer to a small dark spot on the skin or a person who secretly gives information to an enemy.

words.ex: The molten lava flowed down the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 熔化的岩浆从山上流下。
words.en: Molten is used to describe substances that have been heated to a very high temperature and have turned into a liquid.

words.ex: Monocytes are a type of white blood cell.
words.ex_cn: 单核细胞是一种白细胞。
words.en: A monocyte is a type of white blood cell, part of the human body's immune system. Monocytes are produced by the bone marrow and circulate in the blood, where they can differentiate into macrophages and dendritic cells to fight infection and inflammation.

words.tr:
n. 旷野地；荒野；高沼
v. （使）停泊；系泊
words.ex: The sheep graze on the moor near the village.
words.ex_cn: 羊在村庄附近的旷野地上吃草。
words.en: A moor is an area of open land, often with poor soil, that is covered with grass, heather, and low bushes. It can also refer to the act of securing a ship or boat to a fixed object or the land.

words.ex: He had a mop of curly hair that always looked messy.
words.ex_cn: 他有一头乱蓬蓬的卷发，总是看起来很凌乱。
words.en: A mop is a tool for cleaning floors, consisting of a bundle of thick strings or a sponge attached to a long handle. As a verb, it means to clean or wipe something with a mop.

words.tr: adj. 病态的；心理不健康的
words.ex: He has a morbid fear of the dark.
words.ex_cn: 他对黑暗有一种病态的恐惧。
words.en: If you describe a person or their interest in something as morbid, you mean that they are very interested in unpleasant things, especially death, and you think this is strange.

words.ex: The doctor gave him morphine for the pain.
words.ex_cn: 医生给了他吗啡来止痛。
words.en: A powerful drug that is used to relieve severe pain, especially after surgery or in terminal illness.

words.ex: Biology students learn morphology to study plant shapes.
words.ex_cn: 生物学生学习形态学来研究植物的形状。
words.en: Morphology is the study of the form and structure of organisms or their parts.

words.tr: n. 臼；研钵；灰浆；迫击炮
words.ex: The chef used a mortar to grind the spices.
words.ex_cn: 厨师用臼来研磨香料。
words.en: Mortar is a mixture of sand, water, and cement or lime that is used to hold bricks or stones together. It is also a type of gun that fires explosive shells at a high angle.

words.ex: Moses led the Israelites out of Egypt.
words.ex_cn: 摩西带领以色列人离开了埃及。
words.en: Moses is a prophet in the Abrahamic religions. According to the Hebrew Bible, he was a former Egyptian prince who later in life became a religious leader and lawgiver, to whom the authorship of the Torah is traditionally attributed.

words.tr: n. 穆斯林；伊斯兰教信徒；
words.ex: He is a muslim who prays five times a day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名每天祈祷五次的穆斯林。
words.en: A Muslim is a person who follows the religion of Islam.

words.ex: He goes to the mosque every Friday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周五去清真寺。
words.en: A mosque is a building where Muslims go to worship.

words.ex: A mosquito bit my arm last night.
words.ex_cn: 一只蚊子昨晚咬了我的胳膊。
words.en: A mosquito is a small flying insect that bites people and animals in order to feed on their blood. Some mosquitoes can transmit diseases.

words.ex: The stone is covered with green moss.
words.ex_cn: 石头上覆盖着绿色的苔藓。
words.en: Moss is a small, green plant that grows in damp, shady places, often forming a soft, thick layer on the ground, trees, or rocks.

words.tr:
n. 樟脑丸；卫生球
v. 束之高阁；封存
words.ex: She put mothballs in the drawer to keep clothes safe.
words.ex_cn: 她把樟脑丸放在抽屉里以保护衣物。
words.en: A mothball is a small ball made of a chemical substance which has a strong smell. It is used to keep moths away from clothes. In a figurative sense, to mothball something means to postpone or cancel a plan or project.

words.ex: The motif of love appears in many poems.
words.ex_cn: 爱的主题出现在许多诗歌中。
words.en: A motif is a design or pattern that is used in a piece of art or music, or a theme that is repeated in a work of literature.

words.ex: He drives on the motorway every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都在高速公路上开车。
words.en: A motorway is a wide road specially built for fast travel over long distances, with a limited number of places at which drivers can enter and leave it.

words.ex: Her motto is 'Never give up.'
words.ex_cn: 她的座右铭是‘永不放弃’。
words.en: A motto is a short sentence or phrase that expresses a rule for sensible behavior, especially a way of behaving in a particular situation.

words.tr: adj. 上升的；增长的； n. 底托；登上；乘骑； v. “mount”的现在分词；
words.ex: The mounting pressure made him nervous.
words.ex_cn: 上升的压力让他感到紧张。
words.en: The act of fixing or attaching something in position.

words.ex: The mucosa lining the stomach secretes digestive enzymes.
words.ex_cn: 胃黏膜分泌消化酶。
words.en: The mucous membrane lining various tubular structures in the body, such as the respiratory and digestive tracts.

words.ex: He has a lot of mucous in his nose.
words.ex_cn: 他的鼻子有很多黏液。
words.en: Relating to, producing, or resembling mucus.

words.ex: He has a lot of mucus in his nose.
words.ex_cn: 他的鼻子有很多黏液。
words.en: A thick, slippery substance produced by the mucous membranes and glands for lubrication, protection, etc.

words.ex: The mulberry tree grows near the old house.
words.ex_cn: 桑树长在老房子附近。
words.en: A mulberry is a tree that produces small, sweet berries, which are often used in cooking or eaten fresh.

words.ex: A tree is a multicellular organism.
words.ex_cn: 树是一种多细胞生物。
words.en: Consisting of many cells.

words.tr: adj. 多因素的；多因子的
words.ex: The disease is thought to be multifactorial in origin.
words.ex_cn: 这种疾病被认为是多因子起源的。
words.en: Involving or dependent on a number of factors or causes.

words.ex: He had mumps last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周得了腮腺炎。
words.en: Mumps is a contagious disease that causes swelling of the salivary glands and can lead to more serious complications.

words.ex: The artist painted a colorful mural on the school wall.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家在学校墙上画了一幅色彩斑斓的壁画。
words.en: A mural is a large painting, typically executed directly on a wall.

words.tr: n. 音乐学者；音乐理论家；
words.ex: The musicologist studied ancient folk songs.
words.ex_cn: 这位音乐学者研究了古老的民歌。
words.en: A musicologist is a person who studies music as a subject, especially its history and forms.

words.ex: The perfume contains natural musk.
words.ex_cn: 这种香水含有天然麝香。
words.en: A substance with a strong smell that is used in making perfumes, obtained from a type of deer.

words.ex: He put mustard on his sandwich.
words.ex_cn: 他在三明治上加了芥末。
words.en: A pungent yellow or brown paste made from the ground seeds of certain plants, used as a condiment.

words.ex: Mycology is the study of fungi and their genetic and biochemical properties.
words.ex_cn: 真菌学是研究真菌及其基因和生化特性的学科。
words.en: Mycology is the branch of biology that deals with the study of fungi, including their genetic and biochemical properties, their taxonomy, and their use to humans as a source for tinder, medicine, food, and entheogens, as well as their dangers, such as toxicity or infection.

words.ex: He has myopia and needs glasses to see far objects.
words.ex_cn: 他有近视，需要戴眼镜才能看清远处的物体。
words.en: Myopia is a condition of the eye where light focuses in front of, instead of on, the retina. This results in distant objects appearing blurry while close objects can be seen clearly.

words.tr:
adj. 无数的；
n. 无数；
words.ex: There are myriad stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中有无数的星星。
words.en: A myriad of things or people is a very large number of them.

words.ex: The renaissance brought new art and ideas to Europe.
words.ex_cn: 文艺复兴为欧洲带来了新的艺术和思想。
words.en: The Renaissance was a period in European history marking the transition from the Middle Ages to modernity and covering the 15th and 16th centuries, characterized by an effort to revive and surpass ideas and achievements of classical antiquity.

words.tr: n. 推拿疗法；按摩疗法
words.ex: Naprapathy focuses on treating the connective tissues to alleviate pain.
words.ex_cn: 矫正疗法侧重于治疗结缔组织以缓解疼痛。
words.en: Naprapathy is a method of relieving pain and improving movement by manipulating the connective tissues of the body.

words.ex: The doctor used narcotherapy to help the patient relax.
words.ex_cn: 医生使用催眠疗法帮助病人放松。
words.en: Narcotherapy is a form of therapy that uses narcotics or sedatives to induce a state of deep relaxation or unconsciousness, often used in the treatment of psychological disorders or for pain management.

words.tr:
n. 麻醉药；镇定剂；致幻毒品
adj. 麻醉的；催眠的
words.ex: He took a narcotic for his pain.
words.ex_cn: 他服了一种麻醉药来缓解疼痛。
words.en: A narcotic is a drug that dulls the senses, relieves pain, and induces sleep. It can also refer to something that has a soothing or numbing effect.

words.ex: The narwhal is often referred to as the 'unicorn of the sea'.
words.ex_cn: 独角鲸常被称为“海洋独角兽”。
words.en: A narwhal is a medium-sized toothed whale that possesses a large 'tusk' from a protruding canine tooth.

words.ex: He has a nasal voice when he has a cold.
words.ex_cn: 他感冒时声音有鼻音。
words.en: Nasal is used to describe something relating to the nose or the production of sound through the nose.

words.tr: n. 民族主义；国家主义；
words.ex: Nationalism made people proud of their own country.
words.ex_cn: 民族主义让人们为自己的国家感到自豪。
words.en: Nationalism is a political, social, and economic ideology and movement characterized by the promotion of the interests of a particular nation, especially with the aim of gaining and maintaining the nation's sovereignty over its homeland.

words.tr: n. 自然学家；博物学家；
words.ex: The naturalist studied birds in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这位自然学家在森林里研究鸟类。
words.en: A naturalist is a person who studies or is an expert in natural history, especially a zoologist or botanist.

words.ex: The answer is naught.
words.ex_cn: 答案是零。
words.en: Naught means nothing or zero. It is often used to indicate the absence of something or the result of an effort being unsuccessful.

words.ex: The smell of the food made her feel nausea.
words.ex_cn: 食物的气味让她感到恶心。
words.en: A feeling of sickness with an inclination to vomit.

words.tr: n. 反对者；否定者；爱唱反调的人
words.ex: Despite the naysayers, she managed to achieve her goals.
words.ex_cn: 尽管有那些摇头族，她还是设法实现了自己的目标。
words.en: A naysayer is someone who always says something will not work or is not possible.

words.ex: The necropsy revealed the cause of death.
words.ex_cn: 验尸揭示了死亡原因。
words.en: A necropsy is a post-mortem examination to discover the cause of death or the extent of disease.

words.ex: The injury caused necrosis in the tissue.
words.ex_cn: 受伤导致组织坏死。
words.en: The death of most or all of the cells in an organ or tissue due to disease, injury, or failure of the blood supply.

words.ex: Bees collect nectar from flowers.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂从花朵中采集花蜜。
words.en: A sweet liquid secreted by flowers and collected by bees for making honey.

words.ex: The needy family received food from the charity.
words.ex_cn: 这个贫穷的家庭从慈善机构收到了食物。
words.en: Needy people do not have enough food, medicine, or clothing, or adequate houses.

words.ex: The building has a neoclassical style with white columns.
words.ex_cn: 这座建筑有着带有白色柱子的新古典主义风格。
words.en: Neoclassical refers to a revival of classical styles or influence in art, literature, architecture, or music.

words.ex: People in the Neolithic age used stone tools.
words.ex_cn: 新石器时代的人们使用石器。
words.en: Relating to or denoting the later part of the Stone Age, when ground or polished stone weapons and implements prevailed.

words.ex: The sign glows with bright neon light.
words.ex_cn: 这个标志发出明亮的霓虹光。
words.en: A colourless, odourless inert gaseous element occurring in minute amounts in the earth's atmosphere, used in fluorescent lights and illuminated advertising signs.

words.ex: The neonate cried loudly after birth.
words.ex_cn: 新生儿出生后大声哭喊。
words.en: A neonate is a newborn child, especially one less than four weeks old.

words.tr: adj. 肿瘤的；新造型主义的
words.ex: The treatment focuses on reducing the size of neoplastic tissue.
words.ex_cn: 这种治疗专注于缩小赘生组织的大小。
words.en: Relating to or denoting a neoplasm or neoplasia.

words.ex: He traveled to Nepal last summer.
words.ex_cn: 他去年夏天去了尼泊尔。
words.en: A landlocked country in South Asia, located mainly in the Himalayas, bordered by China to the north and India to the south, east, and west.

words.ex: He has nephritis and must drink more water.
words.ex_cn: 他患有肾炎，必须多喝水。
words.en: Nephritis is a condition in which the kidneys become inflamed, leading to impaired kidney function.

words.ex: She suffers from chronic neuralgia in her left arm.
words.ex_cn: 她左臂患有慢性神经痛。
words.en: Neuralgia is a sharp, severe pain along the course of a nerve, especially in the head or face.

words.ex: He works in neurology at the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 他在医院从事神经学工作。
words.en: The branch of medicine or biology that deals with the anatomy, functions, and organic disorders of nerves and the nervous system.

words.ex: The neuron sends signals to the brain.
words.ex_cn: 神经元向大脑发送信号。
words.en: A neuron is a cell that is specialized to conduct nerve impulses.

words.ex: The neutron has no electric charge.
words.ex_cn: 中子不带电荷。
words.en: A neutron is a subatomic particle found in the nucleus of every atom except that of simple hydrogen. It has no electric charge and a mass slightly greater than that of a proton.

words.tr: n. 时事通讯；业务通讯；简报
words.ex: He reads the weekly newsletter every Monday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周一都读这份周刊。
words.en: A newsletter is a regularly distributed publication that is generally about one main topic of interest to its subscribers.

words.ex: He bought a magazine at the newsstand.
words.ex_cn: 他在报摊上买了一本杂志。
words.en: A newsstand is a place where newspapers and magazines are sold, often located on the street or in a public area.

words.tr:
n. 钢笔尖；尖头
v. 装尖头
words.ex: The nib of his pen is broken.
words.ex_cn: 他的钢笔笔尖坏了。
words.en: The pointed end part of a pen, which distributes the ink on the writing surface.

words.tr: n. 商机；理想的工作或生活；
words.ex: He found a niche in selling eco-friendly phone cases.
words.ex_cn: 他在销售环保手机壳方面找到了商机。
words.en: A niche is a hollow area in a wall which has been made to hold a statue, or a comfortable or suitable position in life or employment.

words.ex: The coin is made of nickel.
words.ex_cn: 这枚硬币是镍制的。
words.en: A hard silver-white metal that is used in making alloys and is a chemical element. It is also a coin worth five cents in the US and Canada.

words.ex: He quit smoking to avoid nicotine.
words.ex_cn: 他戒烟以避免尼古丁。
words.en: Nicotine is a toxic colorless or yellowish oily liquid that is the chief active constituent of tobacco. It acts as a stimulant in small doses, but in larger amounts blocks the action of autonomic nerve and skeletal muscle cells.

words.ex: He is niggardly with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他对待钱很吝啬。
words.en: If you describe someone as niggardly, you are criticizing them for being too mean or unwilling to spend money.

words.tr: n. 夜间游荡的人；梦游者
words.ex: The nightwalker was found wandering the streets in a trance-like state.
words.ex_cn: 这名梦游者被发现像处于恍惚状态一样在街上游荡。
words.en: A person or animal that walks or is active at night.

words.ex: The score was nil at the end of the game.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束时分数为零。
words.en: Nothing or none; used to indicate the absence of something.

words.tr: adj. 灵活的；敏捷的；机敏的
words.ex: The cat is nimble and jumps over the fence.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫很敏捷，跳过了篱笆。
words.en: Someone who is nimble is able to move their fingers, hands, or legs quickly and easily.

words.ex: The nipper was playing with his toys in the corner.
words.ex_cn: 那个小孩正在角落里玩他的玩具。
words.en: A nipper is a tool used for cutting or gripping, or a term used affectionately to refer to a small child.

words.ex: The baby is sucking on the nipple.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿正在吸吮乳头。
words.en: A nipple is a small projection of the breast or bottle from which a baby suckles milk.

words.ex: Plants need nitrogen to grow.
words.ex_cn: 植物需要氮来生长。
words.en: A chemical element with the symbol N and atomic number 7. It is a colorless, odorless, tasteless gas that is the most plentiful element in Earth's atmosphere and is a constituent of all living tissues.

words.ex: He wakes up at night for nocturia.
words.ex_cn: 他晚上因为夜尿而醒来。
words.en: Nocturia is a condition where an individual wakes up during the night because they have to urinate. It is a common symptom among older adults and can be caused by various factors, including an overproduction of urine at night, reduced bladder capacity, or an imbalance in the body's natural rhythms.

words.ex: Owls are nocturnal animals.
words.ex_cn: 猫头鹰是夜间活动的动物。
words.en: Nocturnal means happening in the night or active at night.

words.ex: The node is connected to two wires.
words.ex_cn: 这个节点连接着两根电线。
words.en: A node is a point at which lines or pathways intersect or branch; a central or connecting point.

words.ex: The doctor found a small nodule on her thyroid.
words.ex_cn: 医生在她的甲状腺上发现了一个小结节。
words.en: A nodule is a small lump or swelling, especially in the body.

words.ex: The nomadic family moves with their sheep every season.
words.ex_cn: 这个游牧家庭每季都随着羊群迁移。
words.en: A nomadic way of life is one in which people move from place to place instead of living in one place all the time.

words.tr: n. 命名法；专门名词；术语
words.ex: The scientist uses simple nomenclature for the new species.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家为新物种使用简单的命名法。
words.en: A system of names used in a particular field, especially in science.

words.tr: adj. 态度暧昧的；不表态的；含糊的
words.ex: He gave a noncommittal answer when asked about the plan.
words.ex_cn: 当被问到计划时，他给出了一个模棱两可的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour or attitude as noncommittal, you mean that they do not express their opinion or intentions clearly.

words.tr:
adj. 不信奉国教的；不墨守成规的；不随大流的
n. 不墨守成规者；（不信奉英国国教的）新教徒
words.ex: He is a nonconformist who does not attend church.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名不信奉国教的人，不去教堂。
words.en: A nonconformist is someone who does not conform to prevailing ideas or practices in their behavior or views.

words.tr: n. 不一致；不墨守成规
words.ex: His nonconformity to the rules caused problems.
words.ex_cn: 他对规则的不一致引起了问题。
words.en: The state or quality of not conforming to established standards, rules, or laws.

words.tr: n. 非小说类文学作品；非虚构的（纪实类的）文学作品
words.ex: He likes to read nonfiction books about history.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢读关于历史的非虚构书籍。
words.en: Nonfiction is writing that gives information or describes real events, rather than telling a story.

words.tr: adj. 无职业的；无专行的；非科班出身的
words.ex: The advice given was clearly from a nonprofessional source.
words.ex_cn: 给出的建议显然来自一个非专业人士。
words.en: Not engaged in a profession or not having the skills of a professional.

words.ex: The damage done to the environment is often nonreversible.
words.ex_cn: 对环境造成的破坏往往是不可逆的。
words.en: Not able to be reversed or undone; irreversible.

words.tr: adj. 无足轻重的；不显著的
words.ex: The changes were deemed nonsignificant by the committee.
words.ex_cn: 委员会认为这些变化不重要。
words.en: Not significant; lacking in importance or meaning.

words.ex: The symptoms are nonspecific and could be caused by various illnesses.
words.ex_cn: 这些症状是非特异性的，可能是由各种疾病引起的。
words.en: not detailed or exact; not relating to one particular thing

words.tr: adj. 非传统的；不符合传统的
words.ex: The artist's work is known for its nontraditional style.
words.ex_cn: 这位艺术家的作品以其非传统的风格而闻名。
words.en: not conforming to or following tradition; unconventional

words.ex: He sneezed and air came out of his nostril.
words.ex_cn: 他打了个喷嚏，空气从他的鼻孔里出来。
words.en: Either of the two external openings of the nose, which allow air to enter the lungs and smells to be detected.

words.ex: He went to the notary to sign the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他去公证人那里签字。
words.en: A notary is a person authorized to perform certain legal formalities, especially to draw up or certify contracts, deeds, and other documents.

words.ex: The teacher asked students to annotate the text with notes.
words.ex_cn: 老师让学生们在文本上做注释。
words.en: To add notes or comments to a text or diagram, providing explanation or criticism.

words.tr:
n. V字形刻痕；等级；切口
v. 赢得；刻凹痕
words.ex: He made a notch on the stick to count days.
words.ex_cn: 他在木棍上刻了一个刻痕来计数天数。
words.en: A notch is a small cut or indentation in a surface. It can also refer to a level or degree in a scale or a narrow pass between mountains.

words.ex: The answer is nought.
words.ex_cn: 答案是零。
words.en: Nought is used to refer to the number 0, or to nothing or the absence of something.

words.ex: He is a novice at playing the guitar.
words.ex_cn: 他是个吉他新手。
words.en: A novice is someone who has just started learning or doing something and does not have much experience.

words.tr:
n. 核；核心；原子核
n. 核心；核子；“nucleus”的复数
words.ex: The scientist studied the nuclei of cells under a microscope.
words.ex_cn: 科学家在显微镜下研究了细胞的细胞核。
words.en: The plural form of nucleus, referring to the central and most important part of an object, movement, or group, forming the basis for its activity and growth.

words.ex: The nucleus of the team is the captain.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队的核心是队长。
words.en: The central and most important part of an object, movement, or group, forming the basis for its activity and growth.

words.tr:
adj. 裸体的
n. 裸体；裸体画；裸体像
words.ex: He painted a nude woman by the window.
words.ex_cn: 他画了一位在窗边的裸体女性。
words.en: A nude person is not wearing any clothes. A nude painting or sculpture shows a person who is not wearing any clothes.

words.ex: The loud noise every night is a nuisance.
words.ex_cn: 每晚的噪音真是个讨厌的事。
